findings.title: Builder-yard restock (1/day, shelf 40) and the weekly marble offer cannot supply tier 8 and tier 10 – unmodelled 40-50+ day stalls
evidence: lua/shops/home_shops.lua:189-200 builder_yard fixed stock: brick, glass_pane, roof_tile … all `{ stock = 40, restock = 1 }`
scripts/economy/shop_system.gd:415-416 morning restock = +restock (1) clamped to stock (40)
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:280 tier 8 `brick = 90, glass_pane = 40, marble_block = 20, copper_plate = 30`
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:354 tier 10 `roof_tile = 80, glass_pane = 40, marble_block = 40`
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:127,165,202,239 glass 8/12/16/30, roof_tile 24/40, brick 36 at tiers 4-7
lua/shops/home_shops.lua:213-221 marble/walnut/gold_leaf/copper_plate only in the weekly `ugens_fine_varer` slot: pick 4 of 8, qty 12
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:269 roof_tile appears only in the skovkant (floors 1-3) material pool; :635 marble only in krystalgrotten (10-12); loot rolls are amount 1 (scripts/loot/loot_rules.gd:206)
docs/design/PLAN_2D_FEATURES.md:292 design row: builder_yard `daily | 12 basic materials (qty 40)` – no 1/day trickle specified
tools/features/sim/balance_sim.py:418-425 the model buys any missing builder_yard material instantly (`'fixed': 0` wait), so the restock limit never appears
tests/acceptance/journey.gd:93-105 the only material-buying journey covers tier 2 (all amounts below 40)
findings.description: Brick, glass and roof tile can only be bought at Hasselnød's yard (they are not craftable; loot gives about one unit per dive at most). The shelf holds 40 and refills 1 a day, even on closed days. Per-tier needs exceed what the shelf can hold: brick 90 at tier 8, roof tile 80 at tier 10. A player who did not secretly stock up must buy the 40 on the shelf and then come back daily for 50 or 40 more days. Totals, buying every restock from day 1: glass is 150 for the home (+8 for the greenhouse), so tier 10 is reachable around day 111-119 at the earliest. Roof tile is 144, so about day 105. Brick for tier 8 is 126, so about day 87. Marble (76 total) only arrives as 12 per marble week, offered about 50% of weeks. Waiting for tier 10's cumulative marble takes a median of 13 weeks and a 90th percentile of 19 weeks (binomial calculation). Tier 7 alone (16 marble) needs two marble weeks: median 21 days, 90th percentile 49 days. stone_block (186) and slate are fine because stone is craftable and slate has a daily slot. Nothing in game or docs tells the player to stockpile.
findings.player_impact: From tier 7 on, the home ladder stalls for weeks while the player already has the gold, with no explanation. The Husbyggeri just shows e.g. 'Mursten 40/90'. A child sees a sold-out shelf and gives up, and the 'grand castle in 10 steps' goal becomes a slow daily trickle of single tiles.
findings.recommendation: In lua/shops/home_shops.lua builder_yard, set restock equal to stock (40) for the 12 basic materials, matching timber_yard and the PLAN row. Alternatively raise brick/glass_pane/roof_tile to stock 99, restock 30. Give marble_block a permanent fixed row (e.g. stock 24, restock 8), or raise ugens_fine_varer qty to 24 with marble pinned. Add glass_pane/roof_tile/brick to timber_yard, or add recipes (stone + lime → brick; sand-free glass from crystal_shard). Update balance_sim.py to model restock, and extend journey.gd or a home_progression check so every tier's materials are purchasable within N days.
findings.verification:
confirmed: Re-checked in the worktree at f80e7aed. home_shops.lua:189-200: all 12 builder_yard fixed rows are {stock=40, restock=1}. shop_system.gd:405-416 adds `restock` each morning, clamped to `stock`. The same code defaults `restock` to `stock` when it is left out, so the PLAN row (PLAN_2D_FEATURES.md:292, 'qty 40', no restock given) implies a full refill each day. The 1/day trickle therefore contradicts the plan. It has been there since 983fbff2. Home tier totals from home_tiers.lua:56-354: glass 4+8+12+16+30+40+40=150 (+8 for the greenhouse, farm_equipment.lua:11), roof_tile 24+40+80=144, brick 36+90=126, marble 16+20+40=76. The day estimates are arithmetically right (40 on the shelf + 1 per day). Small correction: brick is also in four loot material pools and glass in three (loot_tables.lua:262,397,400,511,514,620,622), not only skovkant. But each roll is amount 1 (loot_rules.gd:206), and a brick takes about 0.36 (material) x 0.78 (normal) x 1/16 ≈ 1.7% of a trae-container roll, with containers respawning every 7-21 days. So loot does not change the conclusion. The sim ignores restock (balance_sim.py:418-425, 'fixed': 0). No other shop stocks brick, glass or roof tile. | confirmed: I tried to refute this and could not. Every cited fact holds in the game-review worktree.

1. **Shelf and restock.** builder_yard has brick, glass_pane and roof_tile at `{ stock = 40, restock = 1 }` (lua/shops/home_shops.lua:189-196). There is no open_weekdays entry, so the yard is open every day. The comment at lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:6-7 says that leaving `restock` out refills the whole shelf, so the value 1 was set on purpose. ShopSystem._on_day_started (scripts/economy/shop_system.gd:404-416) adds `restock` each morning, clamped to `stock`. Restock days are therefore wasted whenever the shelf is full. Buying past the shelf is refused with `no_stock` (:326). There is no other restock path; grepping for restock finds only these.

2. **Other sources are negligible.** In lua/items/building_materials.lua:319-381, brick, roof_tile and glass_pane have `acquire = { buy, find }` and no craft source. roof_tile is found only in skovkant. Loot rolls give amount 1 (scripts/loot/loot_rules.gd:206). Material is only 20-52% of a container's kinds, and brick or roof tile is 10 of 160 weight in the normal pool (lua/data/loot_tables.lua:261-276). Containers respawn every 7-21 days. Expected finds come to well under one unit per visit.

3. **Tier needs exceed the shelf.** Tier 8 needs brick 90 and glass 40 (home_tiers.lua:280). Tier 10 needs roof_tile 80 and glass 40 (:354). Tier 5 needs exactly 40 roof tile (:165) right after tier 4's 24 (:127), which adds a smaller stall the finding does not mention. scripts/home/home_manager.gd:212-236 pays the materials all-or-nothing from the backpack and chest, with no auto-buy or gold substitute.

4. **The sim hides the limit.** The finding understates this. In tools/features/sim/balance_sim.py:424, `wait` is computed but never used, so the sim ignores even the weekly marble slot and buys any shortfall instantly.

5. **The design row differs.** docs/design/PLAN_2D_FEATURES.md:292 lists the yard as `daily`, 12 basic materials, qty 40, and does not mention a 1-a-day trickle.

The totals check out: glass 150 for the home (+8 for the greenhouse at lua/config/farm_equipment.lua:11), roof tile 144, brick 126 (furniture recipes also use some), marble 16+20+40 = 76 from the weekly pick of 4 of 8 at qty 12.

Two things soften it slightly, but not enough to downgrade:
- **Steady buyers are not slowed.** The supply floor puts tier 10 around day 111-119, earlier than the dedicated finish at day 185 (BALANCE.md). A player who buys every day never waits.
- **The cost is visible early.** husbyggeri_ui.gd:70 lets the player look ahead at tier details, so the material counts can be seen in advance.

Even so, nothing tells the player to stockpile, and a full shelf throws restock away. A typical player who saves gold for tier 8 (BALANCE.md says gold is the binding constraint from tier 5) and then buys gets 40 bricks and faces a 50-day wait for the other 50. At 10 minutes per game day that is more than 8 real hours. Tier 10 roof tile works the same way: 40-day wait. This is a real pacing break in the home-upgrade core loop, and P1 stands.

findings.title: There is no keyboard key for attack, so combat cannot be played with the keyboard alone
evidence: project.godot:158-163: `attack` = InputEventMouseButton(button_index 1) + InputEventJoypadButton(2) only; no InputEventKey
project.godot:152-157: `use_tool` likewise LMB + joypad only
docs/design/UI_NAVIGATION.md:161: `use_tool` / `attack` | LMB | X
localization/dungeon_run.csv:64: DTUT_ABILITIES "Klik: slå. Mellemrum: undvig. Q: fe-lys. R: drik." (keys hard-coded in copy)
Owner requirement: 'full keyboard play'
findings.description: Dodge (Space), fairy light (Q) and drink (R) have keys, but striking, and using a tool in general, needs a mouse button or a gamepad. The keyboard-only acceptance flows in UI_NAVIGATION cover menus and home screens, not combat. The tutorial line also hard-codes 'Klik' and the other keys, so it will be wrong once keys can be rebound. Note: the main checkout has uncommitted edits to project.godot and tests/tools/input_contract.gd that may already address this. They are not in this worktree.
findings.player_impact: A keyboard-only player can walk into Mørkeskoven but cannot fight, mine or chop, which blocks the dungeon loop and the boss gates that home progression depends on.
findings.recommendation: Bind attack and use_tool to a key (for example J or K, or F if fly_toggle moves), add the key to the P01 input contract and to UI_NAVIGATION.md's action table, extend the keyboard-only acceptance flow to one forest fight, and build DTUT_ABILITIES from the live InputMap labels instead of literal key names. Fix this together with the routing bug above so that the key reaches `combat.request(&"slash")`.
findings.verification: confirmed: project.godot:152-163: `use_tool` and `attack` have only an InputEventMouseButton and an InputEventJoypadButton, no InputEventKey. UI_NAVIGATION.md:161 and :877 list LMB / X only. localization/dungeon_run.csv:64 hard-codes 'Klik: slå. Mellemrum: undvig. Q: fe-lys. R: drik.' This also means `use_tool` (tilling, watering, chopping) has no keyboard key in general. E/`interact` covers only some node interactions. The finding correctly scopes this to the worktree. The uncommitted main-checkout edits to project.godot are not in it. | confirmed: Confirmed in the worktree. In project.godot, both `use_tool` and `attack` contain only an InputEventMouseButton (button_index 1) and an InputEventJoypadButton (2), with no InputEventKey. docs/design/UI_NAVIGATION.md:161 documents the same thing: `use_tool` / `attack` | LMB | X. R: drik.' The finding's own caveat stands: uncommitted edits in the main checkout (project.godot, tests/tools/input_contract.gd) may address this, but they are not in this worktree, so I judged it against the committed state.

findings.title: Indretning (furniture placement) has no discoverable entry point
evidence: scripts/ui/indretning_ui.gd:25 hotkey_action = &"decorate" (H / pad Back). This is the ONLY way to open it; a repo-wide grep finds no other opener.
scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:39 pause rows = inventory, journal, people, build, garderobe, samlerbog. There is no Indretning row. The only row that prints its hotkey is the cheat menu ('Testmenu · F8').
lua/farm/farm_tutorial.lua:28-37 hints cover hoe, seeds, can, harvest, bin, energy, bridge, bed, mail, expand. None covers decorate/H (or I/J/P/G).
docs/PLAYING.md:37 'use … the decorating screen to place owned furniture' names no key.
localization/features_ui.csv:54 INDRET_ONLY_HOME 'Sæt det op i Indretning.' tells the player to use Indretning without saying how to open it.
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_home_interior.png: at home the only prompt is 'E Sov'; nothing hints at decorating.
findings.description: Bought furniture goes to a separate store ('Møbler og tøj har deres egne magasiner', KISTE_HINT). The only way to place it is Indretning, and that opens only through the H hotkey while standing at home. The pause menu does not list it, the tutorial never teaches it, no world prompt, furniture-shop line or NPC mentions it, and even the player doc omits the key. The one message that names Indretning does not say how to reach it.
findings.player_impact: A player who buys furniture (one of the owner's headline systems: furniture in 5 rarities, hygge and sets gating home tiers 7-10) cannot find out how to place it, short of pressing random keys. Hygge-gated home tiers then stall with no visible reason.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Indret' row to the pause menu while at home (pause_menu.gd _specs, same transfer pattern as garderobe). Add a world prompt or interactable at the home chest or bed ('H · Indret'), plus a one-time whisper the first time furniture enters FurnitureManager.stock or the player first enters home with stock > 0. Show hotkeys on the pause rows (e.g. 'Rygsæk · I') via UiHints.glyph, and give H in PLAYING.md.
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-verified. indretning_ui.gd:25 hotkey_action=&"decorate" is the only opener. A grep for indretning/decorate across scripts and lua finds no get_screen(&"indretning"), no event and no pause row. pause_menu.gd:39 lists inventory, journal, people, build, garderobe and samlerbog only. The amenities and chest panels (home_chest_ui.gd:21, furniture_node_2d.gd:11) link to each other but never to Indretning. farm_tutorial.lua:28-37 has no decorate hint. PLAYING.md:37 names no key. There is no key-rebinding screen that would reveal H. player_2d.gd:339 whispers INDRET_ONLY_HOME ('Sæt det op i Indretning.') when a furniture item is used from the hotbar, and it does not say how. P1 is defensible: a headline owner feature is reachable only through an undocumented hotkey. | confirmed: I checked this in the game-review worktree at f80e7aed and could not refute it. (1) scripts/ui/indretning_ui.gd:25 sets hotkey_action=&"decorate". In project.godot the decorate action is bound to physical key 72 (H) and joypad button 4 (Back). Outside the home map, _hotkey_open_allowed (lines 69-74) refuses to open and whispers INDRET_ONLY_HOME. (2) A repo-wide search for "indretning", &"indretning", INDRET_ and decorate finds no other opener. The only hits are game_ui's screen registration, the tests and fixtures, FurnitureManager.decorate_mode and the whisper. home_chest_ui.gd links only to home_amenities (line 20). husbyggeri_ui and home_amenities_ui have no Indretning button, and the HUD sets no hint for decorate. (3) In scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:39 the rows are inventory_ui, quest_journal, people, build_menu_ui, garderobe and samlerbog. Indretning is missing, even though Garderobe, also a hotkey-only screen, does get a row. (4) The hints in lua/farm/farm_tutorial.lua:28-37 are hoe, seeds, can, harvest, bin, energy, bridge, bed, mail and expand, so none teaches decorating. No Lua quest or dialogue mentions Indretning either. (5) docs/PLAYING.md:37 says only 'use storage and the decorating screen' and names no key. The only text that names H, INDRET_HINT (home_ui.csv:30), is shown inside the panel, so the player sees it only after opening the screen. (6) localization/features_ui.csv:54 INDRET_ONLY_HOME says 'Sæt det op i Indretning.' and gives no key. An extra point makes this worse: scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:338-340 emits INDRET_ONLY_HOME every time the player uses a placeable=home item from the hotbar, with no check that the player is in the home area. So a player standing at home and trying the intuitive 'use the furniture item' gets 'Det her hører til derhjemme', which is misleading as well as unhelpful. Severity: the feature works through H, but nothing in the game points to that key. For a player who doesn't know it, the core owner requirement (furniture in 5 rarities, hygge, sets) is out of reach. P1 is defensible because the screen is effectively unusable for that player, though one could argue P2 since the hotkey does work. I did not run the game, per the rules; the screenshot reference was not re-inspected.

findings.title: 'Nyt spil' silently overwrites the autosave of an existing run within 5 minutes
evidence: scripts/ui/main_menu.gd:83-85 _on_new_game goes straight to character_select with no confirm, even though Continue is enabled (has_any_save)
scripts/ui/character_select.gd:195-207 _on_confirm calls GameManager.start_new_game with no confirm
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:4-11 there is ONE auto slot (save_auto.json, 'the auto slot has no backup') and AUTOSAVE writes it every AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS and at every day end
save_manager.gd:72 AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS := 300.0; :155-160 _process autosaves while PLAYING; :163-168 reset() on new_game_started only zeroes the timer
localization/menus.csv:21-22: overwrite and replace confirmations exist for save/load but there is none for New Game
findings.description: A run that lives only in the auto slot is the normal case for children, who rely on autosave. If anyone starts a new game, the new run autosaves into the same auto slot after 300 real seconds or at the first bed, whichever comes first. That destroys the previous run with no warning and no backup.
findings.player_impact: On a shared family computer, a sibling clicking 'Nyt spil' (or a child exploring the other heroes) wipes weeks of progress. This is unrecoverable save loss.
findings.recommendation: In main_menu.gd _on_new_game, when SaveManager.has_any_save() is true, show a UiConfirm along the lines of 'Dit gemte spil (Dag N) bliver erstattet, når det nye spil gemmer. Fortsæt?' with a 'Gem først' hint. Better still, make the first autosave of a new run copy the old save_auto.json to a save_auto.prev.json backup, or move the old autosave into a free manual slot.
findings.verification: confirmed: main_menu.gd:83-85: _on_new_game changes straight to character_select. character_select.gd:195-207: _on_confirm calls start_new_game. Neither file has a confirm dialog (grep for confirm/has_any_save finds only the Continue enable at main_menu.gd:42). save_manager.gd:4-11 documents one auto slot with no backup (backup_path returns '' for AUTO_SLOT). :72 sets interval 300 s. :155-160 _process autosaves while PLAYING. :262-274 autosaves after day_ended. :164-170 reset() only zeroes timers. menus.csv:20-21 has overwrite and load-replace confirmations, but there is none for a new game. Manual slots survive. A run kept only in save_auto.json is overwritten at the new run's first autosave. Small precision: the 300 s timer counts only in the PLAYING phase, so the tutorial cutscene and the pause menu delay it. | confirmed: Confirmed, and the real risk is worse than stated. main_menu.gd:83-85 _on_new_game changes scene with no confirm. character_select.gd:195-207 _on_confirm calls GameManager.start_new_game with no confirm. menus.csv:21-22 has only SAVELOAD_OVERWRITE/LOAD_CONFIRM, with no new-game confirmation. save_manager.gd:4-11 and :226-259: autosave always writes the single save_auto.json, and the auto slot gets no _roll_backup (backup_path returns '' for AUTO_SLOT). reset() on new_game_started (:163-169) only zeroes the timer and does not protect the old file. The overwrite also happens well before 300 s or the first bed, because many early paths call SaveManager.autosave(). event_runner.gd:99 runs after every scripted event finishes. pause_menu.gd:110 runs on 'leave to menu/quit', so a player who starts a new game by mistake and immediately quits to title destroys the old auto-only run. Others: mother_story.gd:70, runestone_2d.gd:52, loot_service.gd:415. Continue (main_menu.gd:42 has_any_save) then loads the new run. Only players who also made a manual save keep the old run, so silent loss of a whole run is a fair P1.

findings.title: Glow berry regrowth makes it about 3x more profitable than any other crop; current balance tables miss this
evidence: lua/config/game_balance.lua:53 glow_berry = { stages = 5, days_per_stage = 2, regrow_days = 4, seasons = { sommer, efteraar }, sell_price = 150 }
lua/items/magic.lua:58 glow_berry_seeds buy_price = 95; :68 glow_berry sell_price = 150
scripts/world2d/farm_grid.gd:248-249 harvest keeps the plant (regrowing = regrow_days > 0) and :134-135 later harvests need only regrow_days
lua/shops/greenhouse_seeds.lua:11 glow_berry_seeds = { stock = 99, restock = 99 } (vs magic_store.lua:24 stock 8 / restock 4 at buy_multiplier 1.1)
docs/review/mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18.md:73 lists glow_berry at 4.6 g/day ('magic-store seeds'), treating it as a single-harvest crop
lua/config/game_balance.lua:50 carrot 4 days, sell 65, seed 20 (best non-regrowing crop)
findings.description: Glow berry gives its first harvest after 10 watered nights and then every 4 nights for the rest of summer and autumn. A day-by-day simulation over its 56-day window gives 12 harvests: +1,705 g net per plot, or 30.4 g per plot per day (59 g/day with fertilizer every harvest). The best alternatives in the same seasons are carrot (10.5 g/day), pumpkin (about 5-7), sunflower (4.5) and moonflower (2.1). In the greenhouse it earns about 34 g per bed per day all year, against carrot's 10.7. Because the plant regrows, a field is planted once and then needs only harvesting and sprinklers, so it also needs about half the actions of carrots. The only limit on seeds was the magic store's 8 + 4 per day. The greenhouse shelf (reachable at home tier 2) removes that limit with 99 per day at the cheaper base price. All prior reviews' tables either omit regrowth (4.6 g/day) or call it 'a strong long-term investment', so the team's balance picture is wrong. In 2 of 4 seasons every other outdoor crop is strictly dominated for gold.
findings.player_impact: From the first summer, the best play is 'fill the field with glow berries and harvest every 4 days'. Crop variety stops mattering for two seasons. A 126-plot glow-berry field nets about 215,000 g over summer and autumn, roughly 3x the 74,000 g total of all ten home upgrades, so home progression is front-loaded much faster than the tier curve intends.
findings.recommendation: Model regrowth in the balance tables (docs/qa/game-mechanics/analyze_balance.py). Bring glow berry's rate into the carrot band (10-14 g/day). For example: regrow_days = 7 and sell_price = 110, or keep regrow_days = 4 with sell_price about 60 and seed about 120. Alternatively, limit it to one season (sommer). Also align greenhouse_seeds.lua:11 with the magic store's scarcity (stock 8 / restock 4, or remove glow_berry_seeds from the shelf) so the shelf does not bypass the gate.
findings.verification: partly: Mechanics and numbers re-verified. Season is 28 days (game_balance.lua:87). The first harvest needs 10 growth days (5x2), and later ones need regrow_days=4 (farm_grid.gd:134-135). Harvest keeps the plant (farm_grid.gd:248-252). Planting on sommer day 1 gives harvests on days 11, 15 ... 55: 12 harvests, 1800-95 = +1705 g, about 30.4 g/plot/day against carrot's ~11.25. The greenhouse shelf sells 99 seeds per day at 95 g (greenhouse_seeds.lua:11) against magic_store 8/4 at x1.1. Corrections: (1) docs/qa/game-mechanics/analyze_balance.py:34-37 already models regrowth, so the first recommendation is moot. (2) docs/review/game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md:101-117 already publishes a regrowth-aware table: glow berry +645 per 28-day season against carrot +270, about 2.4x. The team's numbers are not wrong; they are interpreted as 'a strong long-term investment' instead of a dominance problem. Only the 10-18 deep-dive tables (mechanics-story-deep-dive:73 at 4.6 g/day, game-review:100 at 5.5) omit regrowth. (3) 'About half the actions' is overstated: regrowing plots still need watering every night (eligible_water is reset nightly, farm_grid.gd:329-334). Only replanting and tilling are saved. The dominance in sommer and efteraar is real, but similar to premium regrowing crops in genre peers, and with no softlock this fits P2 better than P1. | partly: The mechanics hold up when traced through the code. lua/config/game_balance.lua:53 gives glow_berry regrow_days=4, stages 5 x 2, seasons sommer+efteraar, sell 150. farm_grid.gd:248-253 keeps a regrowing plant with growth_days reset to 0, and _growth_needed (farm_grid.gd:132-136) then needs only regrow_days. _on_day_started (farm_grid.gd:316-335) adds +1 for each eligible watered night and withers the plant only when it goes out of season, so it survives the summer->autumn change (days_per_season=28, game_balance.lua:87). Planting on summer day 1 gives harvests on days 11, 15, ..., 55, which is 12 harvests: 12x150 - 95 = 1,705 g, or 30.4 g per plot per day. The non-regrowing best, carrot, gives about 45 g per 4 days, or 11.25 g per plot per day. The greenhouse shelf (greenhouse_seeds.lua:11, 99/99 at x1.0) and indoor in_season()=true (farm_grid.gd:138-140) make it a year-round option. The numbers are correct, and the 10-18 reviews (mechanics-story-deep-dive:73, game-review-2026-10-18:100) do treat it as single-harvest. Why it is over-rated: (1) The team already knew about the regrowth. docs/review/game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md:109,117,142 lists glow berry as '10 / 4' regrowth with 5 harvests per season and calls it 'a strong long-term investment', so 'the team's balance picture is wrong' is only true of the two newest reviews. (2) Regrowing crops that beat replanted crops is standard in the genre (for example blueberries and cranberries in Stardew). It is gated by a 95-105 g seed, a 10-night wait before any return, and the magic store's 8+4 stock; the shelf that removes the stock limit needs a built greenhouse (farm_equipment.lua:9-15: 1500 g + wood/stone/8 glass, min_home_tier 2, capacity only 12 beds), not just home tier 2. (3) Processing narrows the gap: preserve_carrot 180 vs preserve_glow_berry 350 (lua/items/farm_equipment.lua:11,17), which works out to about 40 vs about 73 g/day before jar throughput limits, so not 3x. Nothing is broken or softlocked, and other crops still have uses (quests, gifts, spring/winter). It is a real dominance/tuning issue worth flagging, but it is P2 balance, not P1.

lua/items/crops.lua:84 seed 120 / :94 sell 180 (12 days)
findings.description: A moonflower only grows on nights when it was watered between 20:00 and 06:00. Watering in the morning, which is what the tutorial teaches ('Vand hver dag'), and every sprinkler (fixed at 06:00) still set the plot to watered. The soil turns dark, but the night does not count. Nothing on screen or in the seed text says the plant needs watering after 20:00. 'Gror kun om natten' reads as 'it grows by itself at night'. Watering on a rainy or already-watered plot also fails with no whisper (player_2d.gd use_selected: ok=false, no message). Separately, prior M5 (moonflower dominated) is still open. Even when watered correctly it nets 2.1 g/day over its window (120 g seed, 12 nights, 180 g sale), the worst crop in the game despite being the 'uncommon' premium seed.
findings.player_impact: A player who waters every morning, or uses sprinklers, sees wet soil on a 120 g crop that never grows. This feels like a bug, and the description gives no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Show moon crops as 'waiting for night' when watered outside the window: a distinct soil tint, or a whisper on the first daytime watering, e.g. new key FARM_MOON_WATER_AT_NIGHT 'Månebønner skal vandes efter kl. 20'. Add the window to farming_details.gd when the crop def has water_window. Rewrite economy.csv:41 to 'Vand efter kl. 20 – gror kun om natten. Høst efter 12 nætter'. Either let quality_sprinkler count for night crops or say in ITEM_SPRINKLER_DESC that it does not. Rebalance (e.g. seed 80, sell 260) so the night chore pays off.
findings.verification: partly: The UX failure is confirmed. _water() always sets watered=true and sets eligible_water only inside the window (farm_grid.gd:189-194). Growth needs eligible_water (farm_grid.gd:329-330). Sprinklers water at 6.0 (farm_equipment.gd:80), and in_water_window(6.0) is false for {20,6}. farm_view.gd:42 tints the soil watered whenever p.watered is set. economy.csv:41 says only 'Gror kun om natten'. farming_details.gd shows no water window. The only explicit mention is the dev doc docs/qa/farm-completion/REVIEW.md. A failed watering with the can gives no whisper (player_2d.gd:366). Mitigations the finding omits: re-watering the same plot after 20:00 is allowed (farm_grid.gd:201-202), and rain or fairy-dust auto-water re-water it hourly inside the window (farm_grid.gd:296-311). The economics are misstated. Seed 120 (crops.lua:84) and sell 180 over 12 nights give 5.0 g/day per cycle. Across the 56-day sommer+efteraar window that is 4 harvests, +240, about 4.3 g/day, not 2.1. It is not 'the worst crop': catnip (4.0) and sunflower (~4.4) are equal or lower. Prior game-review M5 (moonflower listed at 5.0 g/day as dominated) is still open.

findings.title: Five repeatable quests 'collect' goods with have=true and never take them – one held stack pays about 650 g/day forever
evidence: lua/quests/dark_forest_mining.lua:22,30 iron ore x6 / amethyst x2 `have = true`; :34 return_to_smith has no needs/consume; :44 gold 600 + gem_bag + iron_sword; :57 cooldown 7
lua/quests/crystal_cave.lua:22 crystal_shard x5 have; :33 return without consume; :43 600 g + 3 amethyst + emerald + 2 fairy_dust; cd 7
lua/quests/night_flower.lua:15 night_bloom x1 have; :19 'return_to_oak' no consume; :29 350 g + fairy_dust + 5 moonflower_seeds; :42 cd 5
lua/quests/forest_patrol.lua:22 moss x6 have; :26 no consume; :36 220 g + 3 iron_ore; cd 3
lua/quests/fairy_friendship.lua:22,30 tokens/fairy_dust have; :36 600 g + 5 fairy_dust; :49 cd 14
scripts/autoload/quest_manager.gd:481-483 on accept, owned items count immediately; :1013-1014 _have_value = EconomyManager.count_item
localization/quests.csv:47 'Smeden Thorin skal bruge jernmalm og ametyst…' (he needs them, yet keeps nothing)
contrast: lua/quests/supply_run.lua:32, animal_products, cookie_delivery, rare_mushroom_hunt use `consume = true`
findings.description: Prior review M8 noted that have=true goals can be bought. This is a different defect: in these five repeatables the turn-in never consumes the goods. After the first run, keep 6 iron ore + 2 amethysts, 5 shards, 1 night bloom, 6 moss, 5 tokens + 2 fairy dust. Each later run is just: accept (instantly complete), enter the forest or cave, talk. Sell-value income: mining 1,050 g/7 days ≈ 150/day; crystal cave 1,370/7 ≈ 196/day; night flower 650/5 ≈ 130/day; patrol ≈ 88/day; fairy friendship 1,425/14 ≈ 102/day. That totals about 650 g/day, or about 75,000 g over one 112-day year, which equals the whole home ladder, for no gathering. Related, but legitimate: supply_run consumes goods but can be fed from Brumme's timber yard (wood 10 + stone 6 = 74 g) for 230 g + 300 g of seeds every 2 days.
findings.player_impact: The gather loop of the dungeon errands becomes meaningless after the first run, and the story of 'Thorin is short of ore' is broken because he never takes any. It is a large unintended income stream that flattens the economy.
findings.recommendation: Add a turn-in with `needs = {...}, consume = true` to the return objective of dark_forest_mining (iron_ore 6, amethyst 2), crystal_cave (crystal_shard 5), forest_patrol (moss 6) and fairy_friendship (fairy_dust 2; keep the tokens as 'show'). For night_flower either consume the bloom (Oak keeps it for his lantern) or make it non-repeatable. Re-check rewards against vendor value after the change.
findings.verification: partly: Core defect confirmed. All five quests use `have = true` with no needs/consume on the turn-in (dark_forest_mining.lua:22,30,34-40; crystal_cave.lua:22,33-39; night_flower.lua:15,19-25; forest_patrol.lua:22,26-32; fairy_friendship.lua:22,30). quest_manager.gd:481-483 and :1013-1014 count owned items at accept time and never consume them; consume only runs on objectives that have `needs` (quest_manager.gd:942). The reward sell values check out: 1,050 / 1,370 / 650 / 265 / 1,425. Correction: 'for no gathering' does not mean 'no effort'. fairy_friendship needs 3 help/errand quest completions per run (help_citizens, fairy_friendship.lua:11-15). crystal_cave forces floors 10-12 every run (explore_cave, :26-30). Only mining, night_flower and patrol are near-free (enter the forest and talk), which is about 370 g/day. The ~650 g/day and ~75k g/year totals overstate the free income. P2 is still right.

lua/items/resources.lua:8 'wild_flower / night_bloom: yields of flower_patch and night_bloom resource nodes (quests flower_necklace…)'

findings.description: resource_nodes.lua never had a flower_patch row (git: only added in 1ea1ca3a, without it), so the farm's only wild-flower node is dropped at map build. For every hero except Kiki the monkey, wild flowers come only from Stokrose's weekly keeper sample (after 3 hearts, which means 3 weeks of weekly chats) plus 5 flowers from heart events. The repeatable flower_necklace quest, offered from day 1, needs 5 at once, so it realistically cannot be finished before about week 7-8. It then competes with hjertebuket, the partner gift that needs 3, and with five NPCs who love the flower as a gift.
findings.player_impact: A child accepts Lily's necklace quest on day 1 and finds no flowers anywhere for weeks. The marriage gift (Hjertebuket) is unexpectedly scarce.
findings.recommendation: Add `flower_patch = { art = "<flower prop>", hp = 1, forage = true, item = "wild_flower", amount = { 1, 3 }, respawn_days = 1 }` to lua/config/resource_nodes.lua. Consider 2-3 more patches in Trætoppen/Hyggebyen maps, and a validator rule that every `node kind=` marker in data/maps resolves to a resource_nodes row.
findings.verification: confirmed: lua/config/resource_nodes.lua:5-23 has no flower_patch row. farm.map:59 places `kind=flower_patch`, the only flower_patch marker in data/maps. resource_node_2d.gd:23-24 returns null on an empty row, so the node is skipped silently. A grep of lua/, scripts/ and data/ finds no other gatherable wild_flower source and no shop stocking it. The remaining sources are: Kiki's crown caches (species_perks.lua:31; one random item of 4, traetoppen.lua:48); Stokrose's keeper sample, 1 per weekly-heart chat once at 3+ hearts (social_manager.gd:405-414, citizens.lua:31; gifts can reach 3 hearts faster, but it is still only 1 per week); and heart events (lyra h4 = 1, lyra h10 = 2, birk h6 = 2). flower_necklace (5 wild_flower, have=true, no requirement, cd 4) is available from day 1. The 'week 7-8' estimate is speculative, but the block is real. There is no validator: no test or tool checks map node kinds against resource_nodes.

findings.title: Greenhouse seed shelf: all seeds 99/day, open 24/7, cheaper glow berries, and it buys every item at full price
evidence: lua/shops/greenhouse_seeds.lua:3-14 keeper merchant_pip, every seed `{ stock = 99, restock = 99 }`, no `buys`, no open_weekdays
data/maps/greenhouse.map:21 `@marker S greenhouse action=seeds`; scripts/farm/greenhouse/greenhouse_2d.gd:46-47 opens the shop
lua/buildings/*.lua claim seed_shop…lantern_house but not greenhouse_seeds → scripts/towns/hours.gd:157-159 returns null → shop_system.gd:142-148 always open
scripts/economy/shop_system.gd:270 an empty `buys` list buys every category: furniture, gems, weapons, clothing
designed scarcity it overrides: lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:32 moonflower 8/4; lua/shops/magic_store.lua:24 glow_berry_seeds 8/4 at ×1.1 (105 g) vs 95 g here
lua/config/farm_equipment.lua:10-15 greenhouse: 1,500 g + 8 glass, home tier 2 (available in week 1-2)
findings.description: After a cheap tier-2 build, the farm has an unattended shelf that sells every seed in bulk with no Sunday or hours closure, undercuts Zephyr's glow-berry seeds by 10%, and makes the 8/4 shelves of the seed shop and magic store irrelevant. Because it has no `buys` list, it is also an instant-pay sell point for any sellable item (rare furniture, gems, weapons) at the 1.0 multiplier, at 02:00 or on a festival day. The same no-`buys` rule makes the bakery, smithy, animal store, magic store, seed shop and festival markets buy everything. As a result, the `buys` specialisation of the home shops and the opening hours have no effect on selling.
findings.player_impact: Town shops' hours, closed days and keepers stop mattering for the economy. The glow-berry plus keg strategy can scale with no supply friction from week 2.
findings.recommendation: Give greenhouse_seeds `buys = {}` with sell_multiplier 0, or `buys = { "seed" }`. Limit stock to the winter seeds (snow_turnip, snowdrop, frost_kale) plus small amounts of others (e.g. 10/5), and price glow_berry_seeds at magic-store parity. Give the town shops category-appropriate `buys` lists (bakery: food, crop, product; smithy: weapon, tool, mineral, gem; magic: gem, magic, forage).
findings.verification: partly: The facts are accurate: greenhouse_seeds.lua:3-18 has every seed at 99/99 and no `buys`; no lua/buildings claims it, so it is always open; shop_system.gd:270 means an empty `buys` list buys every category at sell_multiplier 1.0. Glow-berry seeds base price is 95 (magic.lua:58), so 95 here vs 105 at the magic store (x1.1, stock 8/4). Moonflower is 8/4 at seed_shop. Greenhouse min_home_tier is 2 (farm_equipment.lua:14). The bakery, smithy, animal store, magic store and seed shop also have no `buys` (only timber_yard, lantern_house and the home_shops define one). Correction: two parts are deliberate and test-pinned, not oversights. 'No opening hours' is decision DT44/C28 (TOWNS_FARM_SOCIAL_ADDENDUM.md:1045,1122), so winter planting cannot be blocked; farm_automation.gd:202 checks seed_shelf_open_after_midnight. 'Every crop has greenhouse seeds' is asserted at farm_automation.gd:23-27, which goes beyond the original 'two winter seeds' scope. The real balance problems are the unlimited bulk stock of seeds designed to be scarce, the glow-berry undercut, and the universal instant buyback, which bypasses the shipping bin's category filter and its next-morning payout (shipping_bin_2d.gd:23). The fix must keep every crop's seed on the shelf or update the test.

findings.title: The progression model (BALANCE.md, about 52 h typical) is stale and contradicts the data; approximate curve attached
evidence: docs/features/BALANCE.md:13-17 typical day 345 / casual 919 / dedicated 185; :25 'The binding constraint is money from tier 5 on'
tools/features/sim/balance_sim.py:418-425 builder_yard materials always in stock; `rg keg|preserve|regrow|glow_berry|greenhouse` finds nothing in the sim
lua/config/game_balance.lua:53 glow_berry regrow_days 4 (summer and autumn)
lua/items/farm_equipment.lua:18 juice_glow_berry 450 vs raw 150; lua/config/farm_equipment.lua:7 keg 3 days; seed_shop keg 500 g, restock 3/day
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:58,129-131,167,204,241-245,282,319,356 gates (quests, hearts, hygge)
findings.description:
The model includes no glow-berry regrowth, preserves jars or kegs, greenhouse, winter crops, or keep-the-goods repeatable quests, and it assumes unlimited builder-yard stock. Its 'money binds' conclusion is therefore wrong in both directions. Approximate curve from the current data (dedicated player, estimates):
• Day 1: 900 g (start 500 + intro_lottery 250 + forste_dage 150). Tier 2 costs about 550 g including materials, so it can be built that day.
• Days 5-7: carrots on 68 plots, about 600 g/day. Tier 3 (about 900 g).
• Day 8 at the earliest: tier 4 (Lyra 2 hearts = 2 weekly chats).
• Days 10-20: tier 5 (first_animal plus 4 copper plates from the weekly rotation).
• Days 20-40: tier 6, gated by crystal_cave (floors 10-12).
• Summer (days 29-56): glow berries + kegs ≈ 2.5-3.5k g/day farm, + about 650 g/day from repeatables, + dives. All tier gold (74k + about 10k materials) is plausibly in hand by about day 45-60.
• Materials gate: tier 7 needs glass ≥ day 31 and marble median day 21 / 90th percentile day 49. Tier 8 needs brick ≈ day 87. Tier 10 needs roof tiles ≈ day 105, glass ≈ day 111 and marble median day 91 / 90th percentile day 133.
So from tier 7 on, the late game is paced by restock and rotation, not by gold. After the castle, income can reach 10k g/day with almost no sinks left (furniture about 43k, MAX_GOLD 999,999).
findings.player_impact: Pacing decisions such as home_cost_scale and quest rewards are being tuned against a model that no longer describes the game. The real walls (materials) and runaway sources (processing, free repeatables) are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Extend tools/features/sim/balance_sim.py with shop restock and rotation limits, the regrow/keg/jar/greenhouse income paths and the actual repeatable consume semantics. Re-run it and update docs/features/BALANCE.md. Add a long-term gold sink (e.g. coop/barn tier art, a town donation board, furniture commissions) or cap keg throughput (keg days 4-5, or a per-farm machine limit).
findings.verification: confirmed: BALANCE.md:13-17 and :25 say what the finding says ('The binding constraint is money from tier 5 on'). The doc itself admits it is a pre-P12/P13 model to be re-run (:39-41). `rg keg|preserve|regrow|glow_berry|greenhouse|restock` on balance_sim.py returns nothing, and :418-425 buys any lacking builder_yard material with 'fixed': 0 wait. Data: glow_berry regrow_days 4 (game_balance.lua:53); juice_glow_berry sells for 450 and preserve for 350 (items/farm_equipment.lua:17-18); keg takes 3 days (config/farm_equipment.lua:7); seed_shop keg restocks 6/3 (stock 6, restock 3). Start gold 500 + 250 + 150 = 900, which matches. The progression curve is a set of labelled estimates, and its '+650 g/day repeatables' figure inherits the overstatement noted in ECON-02. The core claim stands: the model is stale and leaves out restock limits and the main late-game income paths.

findings.title: In the forest a click or gamepad X always uses the selected hotbar item, so attack, its input buffer and the Cozy assist's auto-swing never fire
evidence: project.godot:152-163: `use_tool` and `attack` both bind only LMB (button_index 1) and joypad button 2
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:194: `elif event.is_action_pressed("use_tool"):` ... `use_selected()` is checked BEFORE the action-area branch
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:199-201: `elif _is_action_area(): if event.is_action_pressed("attack"): combat.request(&"slash")` (unreachable for LMB/X)
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:386-389: use_selected: `"consumable", "food": ok = GameData.eco().use_item(item)` / `"weapon": return combat.swing(item)`
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:66-70,95: `attack_held` is set only by request(&"slash"); auto-swing requires attack_held
lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:27: cozy preset `assist_auto_swing = 1`; dungeon_run.lua:14 `feel.buffer = 0.15`
lua/data/starter_kit.lua:9-18: default hotbar = hoe, can, axe, pickaxe, sword_rusty, scythe, seeds, lantern_oil (8 slots)
tests/sections/forest.gd:124-127 only asserts that use_tool works in the action area; no test presses a real attack input
findings.description: The forest HUD shows a 'slash' ability on `attack` and the tutorial says 'Klik: slå'. But every real attack input also matches `use_tool`, and the `use_tool` branch comes first in the elif chain, so in Mørkeskoven a click or X runs use_selected() on the selected hotbar item. A swing only happens when that item is a weapon. With the pickaxe or axe selected (needed for the crystals and trees on every floor) the click hits a node or whispers that the tool is too weak. With seeds or the hoe it does nothing. With a tonic, lantern oil or tornebær selected the click consumes the item. combat.request() is never called, so the 0.15 s input buffer never works and attack_held is never set. The Cozy preset's assist_auto_swing therefore can never work. The swing also uses the hotbar weapon, while the picker lines, the weak-weapon hint and the chest-sense effect read the separately equipped weapon slot.
findings.player_impact: A player who arrives from the farm holding the hoe, or who has just mined a crystal, clicks at a bat and nothing happens, or a tonic is drunk. Children and less dexterous players who pick the Cozy preset get no auto-swing although the settings say it is on. Swings pressed during the cooldown are dropped instead of buffered, so combat feels unresponsive.
findings.recommendation: In player_2d.gd `_unhandled_input`, check `_is_action_area()` before the `use_tool` branch. In the forest, route the shared press to `combat.request(&"slash")` (with the equipped weapon) unless the selected item is a tool aimed at a node in reach (use_selected for tool/pickaxe/axe only). Never consume an item on a forest click. Alternatively, auto-select the weapon slot in DungeonFloors.start_run. Add a combat test that drives a real `InputEventMouseButton` in the forest with the pickaxe and with a tonic selected, and one that checks auto-swing under the Cozy preset.
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-verified in the worktree at f80e7aed. project.godot:152-163 gives `use_tool` and `attack` the same two events (LMB button_index 1 and joypad button 2). In player_2d.gd:194-198 the `use_tool` branch comes before `elif _is_action_area()` at :199, so `combat.request(&"slash")` at :201 cannot be reached by any real input. Dungeon floors use projection `ortho` (dungeon_verify.gd:59, iso_area.gd:221), so they are the action area. use_selected (player_2d.gd:331-389) consumes a consumable or food through eco().use_item and only swings when the selected item's category is weapon. `combat.request` is called only at player_2d.gd:201-203, so `attack_held` (player_combat_2d.gd:70) is never set and the Cozy `assist_auto_swing` (:95) is dead. Nothing auto-selects the weapon slot on entering a floor (grep for hotbar.select finds only slot keys and garderobe). Tests miss the bug because drive.gd:145-152 `tap()` sends an InputEventAction, so a tapped `attack` never matches `use_tool`. The divergence between the hotbar weapon and the equipped weapon is also real: the swing uses `swing(item)` from the hotbar, while fairy light (player_combat_2d.gd:250 `_read_weapon()`) and picker_lines read `equipped_item(&"weapon")`. Mitigation: E (`interact`) can also use the selected mining tool on a node (forest.gd:131-133), so mining has a second route. | partly: The mechanism is real; I traced it in the worktree at f80e7aed. project.godot binds `use_tool` and `attack` to the same inputs: LMB (button_index 1) and joypad button 2. In player_2d.gd `_unhandled_input`, the `elif event.is_action_pressed("use_tool")` branch (lines 194-198) comes before `elif _is_action_area(): if event.is_action_pressed("attack"): combat.request(&"slash")` (lines 199-201). For LMB/X that attack branch can never be reached, and nothing else in scripts/ calls request(&"slash"). So in the forest, `combat.request()` never runs and the input buffer (player_combat_2d.gd:66-70) never fires. `attack_held` is never set to true, so the Cozy preset's `assist_auto_swing = 1` (lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:27, checked in player_combat_2d.gd:95) is dead. With a consumable or food selected, `use_selected` (player_2d.gd:386-387) consumes the item on click. I am lowering the severity because combat itself is not broken. With a weapon in the hotbar (sword_rusty is in the starter kit), `use_selected` returns `combat.swing(item)` (player_2d.gd:388-389), and swing() (player_combat_2d.gd:157+) does the full swing, aim nudge and hit logic. That is the usual Stardew-style 'select the weapon slot' pattern, so players have a workaround. What is actually broken: the input buffer, the Cozy auto-swing accessibility assist, accidental item use on click, and the HUD's 'slash' ability having no effect of its own. That is P2. Related small find: the code reads `dungeon_run.feel.input_buffer`, but the Lua key is `feel.buffer` (dungeon_run.lua:14). Only the 0.15 fallback is ever used, and it happens to match.

findings.title: Hitting a dazed boss cuts its punish window from 1.5–1.8 s to ~0.4 s and can stack its attacks; fairy light cancels boss attacks through armor
evidence: scripts/dungeon_run/bosses/boss_base.gd:83-84: after each attack `remaining = float(cfg.dazed)` / `cooldown = remaining` (1.8/1.7/1.5 s, bosses.lua:4-6)
scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:320-323: `var armoured := armor and state in [S.WINDUP,S.LUNGE]` - in RECOVER (dazed) a hit applies 550 knockback and `stun(.38)`
scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:305-312: stun() sets `state = S.STUN`, `remaining = .38`, `cooldown = .4` (overwrites the dazed cooldown)
scripts/dungeon_run/bosses/boss_base.gd:42: `if state == S.CHASE and cooldown <= 0:` -> next pattern ~0.4 s after the first hit
scripts/dungeon_run/bosses/boss_base.gd:64-68: rain/cloud keep the boss in RECOVER for up to ~5.3 s while the AttackSequence keeps landing
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:264-267: fairy light calls `enemy.stun(1.6)` on every enemy incl. bosses (cancels WINDUP via _cancel_attack)
docs/design/dungeon_v2_workpackages.json:1077: 'vulnerable dazed window after every attack'
findings.description: The boss loop is meant to go: telegraph, dodge, then a dazed window to punish the boss. In practice the first hit in that window replaces RECOVER with a 0.38 s STUN and sets the cooldown to 0.4 s, so the boss starts a new pattern about 0.4 s later. Left alone it would have waited the full 1.5–1.8 s. Hitting the boss therefore makes it attack sooner. Slow families (club 0.54 s, staff 0.50 s, spear 0.43 s) get one hit per window instead of the 3–4 the window was tuned for (C4's 8/11/12-swing math assumed a full window). During the Konge's rain or the cloud patterns, a hit lets the boss start a dash or quake while the earlier hazards are still falling. Separately, the 'armor' flag never stops the fairy light, which stuns a boss mid-windup for 1.6 s and up to 2.4 s with light_boost. With the minimum 3 s cooldown (staff_star plus an amethyst gem) that is close to a permanent lock.
findings.player_impact: Boss fights feel erratic: attacking at the right moment is punished with an instant counter, while spamming the fairy light trivialises the bosses late on. Neither matches the readable telegraph, dodge and punish rhythm the design describes.
findings.recommendation: In DungeonBoss2D, override take_hit/stun: while RECOVER (dazed), take damage and flash but do not change state, remaining or cooldown. Optionally allow knockback, or skip it entirely for bosses. While an AttackSequence child is alive, do not start a new pattern. Decide whether the fairy light should only shorten a boss windup (for example to 0.5 s) rather than stun it, and add bosses.gd checks for 'hit during dazed keeps remaining' and 'light vs boss'.
findings.verification: partly: The mechanism is accurate. boss_base.gd:83-84 sets remaining and cooldown to cfg.dazed (1.8/1.7/1.5, bosses.lua:4-6). In enemy_2d.gd:320-323 a hit outside WINDUP/LUNGE calls stun(.38), and stun() (:305-312) sets state STUN, remaining .38 and cooldown .4. boss_base.gd:42 then starts the next pattern about 0.4 s after the hit instead of 1.5-1.8 s. Rain and cloud (boss_base.gd:57-68) put the boss in RECOVER for up to (9-1)*0.35+1.0+1.5 = 5.3 s, and a hit there lets a new pattern start while the AttackSequence is still landing. Fairy light: player_combat_2d.gd:264-267 stuns every enemy including armored bosses for 1.6 s, plus up to 0.8 s from staff_star's stun_bonus_s (weapons.lua:459) = 2.4 s. The cooldown floor is 3 s (dungeon_loot.lua:109, weapon_fx.gd:78). Light-stun 2.4 s + 0.4 s cooldown + a 0.9-1.0 s windup is longer than 3 s, so near-permanent lock holds. Overstated: the claim that slow families get 'one hit per window instead of 3-4'. Armor only suppresses stun and knockback; take_hit still subtracts HP during WINDUP (enemy_2d.gd:319-321), so the player can keep striking through the 0.9-1.0 s windup. The damage loss is therefore smaller than stated. The real effects are a compressed rhythm (the boss attacks sooner when hit) and a 550 push, about 137 px of travel per hit. The opposite failure also exists: fast weapons can stun-lock. A dagger cycles every 0.26 s, so a follow-up hit lands inside the 0.38 s STUN and each hit resets cooldown to .4, which can keep the boss stunned if the player keeps chasing into reach. Either way the dazed window does not work as designed (dungeon_v2_workpackages.json:1077).

findings.title: Per-family weapon knockback is never applied; every hit pushes enemies a hard-coded 550
evidence: lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:16-20: knockback sword 433, club 693, spear 346, dagger 260, staff 433
lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:14: `feel.knockback_enemy = 550` (also unused)
scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:322: `ground_velocity = Iso.to_ground(global_position-from).normalized()*550`
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:141-143: knockback copied into `_weapon` but take_hit receives only (damage, from, attacker)
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:68 reads `feel.input_buffer` while the Lua key is `buffer` (harmless today, same default)
findings.description: The five weapon families are distinguished in data by damage, timing, reach, arc and knockback. Knockback is read into the swing info but Enemy2D.take_hit ignores it and always applies 550, and the `knockback_enemy` key is dead data too. The club's crowd-control push (693) and the dagger's stay-in-range low push (260) do not exist, and the dagger's 158 px reach is often shorter than the forced push (about 137 px of travel per stun), which hurts its intended chain play. A few other feel keys are hard-coded duplicates (shake 2.0/4.0 at player_combat_2d.gd:221,301; dodge-cancel 0.4 at :227), so tuning them in Lua has no effect.
findings.player_impact: The families feel more alike than designed, the dagger is weaker in practice, and tuning knockback in Lua silently does nothing.
findings.recommendation: Pass the attacker's `_weapon.knockback` (or the family value) into take_hit, for example through a `knockback` parameter or by reading attacker.combat._weapon, and use it instead of 550. Fall back to `feel.knockback_enemy`. Wire the shake, dodge-cancel and buffer keys to their Lua names, and add a weapons.gd check that knockback differs per family.
findings.verification: confirmed: enemy_2d.gd:322 hard-codes `*550`. take_hit(damage, from, attacker) (:315) never reads the attacker's weapon knockback. player_combat_2d.gd:141-143 copies the family knockback into `_weapon` and :215 passes only damage and position. The only other knockback use is the player's own hurt knockback (:311). `feel.knockback_enemy`, `shake_hit`/`shake_hurt` (hard-coded 2.0/4.0 at :220/:302) and `dodge_cancel_from` (hard-coded 0.4 at :226) are never read; only `hit_stop_frames` is (:216). `_feel("input_buffer")` (:68) does not match the Lua key `buffer`, and both default to 0.15. Small wording fix: the dagger's 158 px reach is not 'shorter than' the ~137 px push. The push moves an enemy at typical melee distance (about 40-80 px) out to about 180-220 px, beyond the dagger's reach. The conclusion stands.

findings.title: Legendary weapons arrive only after the content they could help with is beaten; the power curve tops out at rare
evidence: lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:7: expected_weapon tops at 24 on floor 12; :8 `deep_step` 'only used when floors above 12 exist'
lua/config/dungeon.lua:15: `max_floor = 12`
lua/items/weapons.lua:99,141,245,349,453: rare sword 22 vs legendary sword_moon 42, club_trunk 57, spear_root 45, staff_star 47
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:857,870: the legendaries come only from the floor-8 and floor-12 boss pools (repeat kills only, reward_rules.gd:20-39)
scripts/dungeon_run/combat_rules.gd:20-24: weapon_range already rates a rare weapon (22) as good for floors 1-12
findings.description: Enemy HP is normalised to expected_weapon, so a rare weapon (about 22) already clears every floor at the intended pace. Uniques (30–40) overshoot floors 7–12, and the Konge legendaries (sword_moon, staff_star) can only drop after the final boss has been beaten at least once and a week has passed. Nothing exists beyond floor 12: no deeper floors, no harder repeat mode and no stronger boss variants. The 5-tier weapon ladder therefore has no reason to exist above rare, which weakens the owner's 'weapons in 5 rarity tiers' progression.
findings.player_impact: Finding a legendary weapon is a trophy with nothing left to test it on, and the endgame dive loop gets easier instead of more interesting.
findings.recommendation: Add post-game depth: activate deep_step by allowing floors 13+ as an endless 'Dybet' band with escalating expected_weapon, or add a 'night/hard' re-run of floors 10–12 after the Konge with stronger enemy HP and the legendary pools. Alternatively, move one legendary per family into floor 8–12 sources so it lands before the Konge.
findings.verification: confirmed: dungeon_run.lua:7 expected_weapon tops out at 24, deep_step is used only when number > curve.size (combat_rules.gd:16), and max_floor = 12 (dungeon.lua:15). The rating is damage*0.4/period, so rare weapons rate about 22 (sword 22, club 30*0.4/0.54 = 22.2) and weapon_range (:20-24, expected <= rating/0.9) covers floors 1-12. Legendary sword_moon and staff_star sit only in the Konge pool (loot_tables.lua:870) and can drop only on a repeat kill at least 7 days later (reward_rules.gd:20-21). Nothing exists beyond floor 12. Nuance: the floor-8 Glød pool (club_trunk, spear_root) can drop before the Konge fight, so 'only after the content is beaten' is strictly true only for the Konge items. Uniques also arrive mid-progression from spots and wanderers (for example wpn_spear_owl in svampelunden). The core argument holds: nothing needs gear above rare.

findings.title: Crystal nodes drawn as amethyst, emerald or moonstone never give those gems in the dungeon, while quests send the player to mine them
evidence: lua/config/resource_nodes.lua:11-14: amethyst/emerald/moonstone/crystal_shard nodes, item = the gem, pickaxe power 2/2/3/1
lua/config/dungeon_loot.lua:57-61: in the dungeon every crystal kind is `alias = "crystal"` -> rough stone 30 %, else glimmer dust
scripts/world2d/resource_node_2d.gd:142-150: on a floor (>0) deplete() uses LootService.node_loot, never cfg.item
lua/config/dungeon.lua:27: `hard_nodes = { "moonstone" }` - the generator guarantees moonstone nodes that yield no moonstone
localization/quests.csv:47-48: QUEST_DARK_FOREST_MINING 'Thorin skal bruge jernmalm og ametyst fra Mørkeskoven' (lua/quests/dark_forest_mining.lua:26-29 needs 2 amethyst)
localization/features_quests.csv:15: 'Find en månesten i Mørkeskoven' (moonstone_crown)
findings.description: Floors show four kinds of gem crystals, require stronger pickaxes for the 'better' ones (moonstone needs power 3), and are listed per floor as amethyst, emerald or moonstone. Every one of them yields the band's unknown stone or glimmer dust, so mining a moonstone gives the same result as mining a shard. The gems themselves come only from Fru Ugle's appraisal lottery (amethyst is about 1/6 of uncommon results), krystalugle drops, the boss first-kill extras or the magic store. Thorin's early quest asks for amethyst 'from Mørkeskoven', which mining there never produces.
findings.player_impact: Players learn that the visible crystal colour and the pickaxe-power gate mean nothing, and they get stuck on 'mine amethyst / find a moonstone in the forest' quests until they think of appraising or buying.
findings.recommendation: Make each crystal kind roll its own gem with a small chance, for example amethyst node -> amethyst 15 % / rough stone / dust, moonstone node -> moonstone 10 %, in dungeon_loot.node_yields, with the depth band scaling the chance. Or give all crystals one neutral art and a 'Krystal' name, and reword the quests ('bring en ametyst – Fru Ugle kan slibe dem') to point at appraisal.
findings.verification: confirmed: resource_nodes.lua:11-14 defines gem nodes with item = the gem, at power 2/2/3/1. dungeon_loot.lua:57-61 aliases every crystal kind to `crystal`, which gives the rough stone at 30 % or else dng_glimmer_dust. resource_node_2d.gd:142-150 uses node_loot on floor > 0 and never cfg.item. hard_nodes = { "moonstone" } (dungeon.lua:27) still applies power 3. This was a deliberate decision (DX30, dungeon_loot.lua:40-42: 'colour is art only'), so the inconsistency lies in the quests and copy. dark_forest_mining.lua:24-29 needs 2 amethyst, and its copy (quests.csv:47-48) says 'fra Mørkeskoven'. It is worse than reported: crystal_cave.lua:18-23 needs 5 crystal_shard, but shard nodes also yield no shards. Shards come only from krystalugle drops (15 %, dungeon_loot.lua:72), appraisal and the magic store (magic_store.lua:18). Additional gem sources the finding omits: festival markets (festival_markets.lua, maanemarkedet.lua) and the static-area forage rare_gem_chance 0.08 (resource_node_2d.gd:157-158).

findings.title: Enemy and boss variety is thin and the difficulty curve is flat after floor 4; the final boss hits softer than ordinary enemies
evidence: lua/config/enemies.lua:5-11: 7 kinds on 5 sprites (sporesvamp = lysesvamp tinted, krystalugle = ugleoje tinted); lysesvamp is a harmless critter
lua/config/dungeon.lua:43: floors 1-3 mix = bat 60 / tornebusk 40, and tornebusk only shoots `from_tier = 2` (enemies.lua:7)
lua/config/bosses.lua:4-6: all three bosses `visual = "snurresvamp"` + tint; scripts/dungeon_run/bosses/{snurre,gloed,konge}.gd share the dash core
lua/config/dungeon_run.lua:10: damage ladders identical for tiers 2 and 3 (standard/heavy {1,2,2,2}); scripts/dungeon_run/combat_rules.gd:28-31 normalises HP to expected_weapon
lua/config/bosses.lua:4-6 `damage = 1` and attack_sequence.gd:29 `impact.damage = 1`, while floor 10-12 trash deals 2 (light tier 4 = 2, keeper lance 2: enemies.lua:11)
scripts/dungeon_run/dungeon_run.gd:51-62: +1 heart per first boss kill
findings.description: At the intended gear every enemy takes the same 1/2/3 hits on every floor, and damage only steps from 1 to 2 half-hearts at floor 4. Floors 4–9 therefore play alike apart from the enemy mix, while the player gains a heart after each boss. Floors 1–3 have only bats and non-shooting bushes. The three bosses are recolours of one sprite with a shared dash. The Svampekonge deals 1 half-heart per hit, half of what the owls and bats in its own arena deal, and it drops two healing berries mid-fight. The rest of the dungeon's variety (hidden spots, lake chests, four surprise types at about 3.6 % per chest, whispers) is front-loaded: once the 27 keepsakes are claimed, floors contain only ordinary chests.
findings.player_impact: The middle and late dungeon feels repetitive, and the climax is the gentlest fight on its own floor, which undercuts the action-adventure half of the pitch.
findings.recommendation: Give each band one signature enemy and introduce mosfroe or sporesvamp earlier. Give the Konge `damage = 2` (the cozy assist already clamps damage to 1) or a unique pattern. Add repeatable floor events after the keepsakes are gone, for example a Natteblik errand, a timed glow-ring and a rare wandering merchant. Plan distinct boss bakes (the design notes this as P21).
findings.verification: confirmed: enemies.lua:5-11 has 7 kinds. sporesvamp uses visual lysesvamp with a tint, krystalugle uses visual ugleoje with a tint, and lysesvamp is class critter with behavior flee. Band 1's enemy_mix is bat 60 / tornebusk 40 (dungeon.lua:43) at enemy_tier 1 (:40), and tornebusk shoots only from tier 2 (enemies.lua:7). All bosses use visual snurresvamp with a tint (bosses.lua:4-6) and damage = 1 (Enemy2D dmg_half reads cfg.damage, enemy_2d.gd:99). attack_sequence.gd:29 sets impact.damage = 1. Band-4 trash deals 2: light ladder tier 4 = 2, standard/heavy tier ≥2 = 2, keeper lance 2. Enemy HP is normalised to expected_weapon (combat_rules.gd:28-31), so hit counts stay constant. Two tornebaer drop at 66/33 % (boss_base.gd:88-90). The +1 heart per first boss kill comes from hearts_per_boss = 2 half-hearts (dungeon_run.lua:5, dungeon_run.gd:57). The '3.6 % surprise per chest' figure was not re-derived. The design opinion is stated accurately.

findings.title: Club's stun effect still does nothing against armored enemies and bosses, and ordinary hits already stun everything else (prior C2 still open)
findings.prior_ref: mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18 C2 'Club's signature stun is null vs every boss'
evidence: scripts/combat/weapon_fx.gd:58: `if bool(enemy.get("armor")): return` (unchanged)
lua/config/bosses.lua:4-6 all `armor = true`; lua/config/enemies.lua:7,10 tornebusk/sporesvamp `armor = true`
scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:320-323: every non-armoured hit already applies `stun(.38)`
lua/items/weapons.lua:208,231: wpn_club_mushroom stun_chance p 0.25 s 0.5; wpn_club_thornberry p 0.5 s 0.6
findings.description: Re-verified against the current code: still open. It is also worse than first reported. Against the non-armored kinds, every hit from any weapon already stuns for 0.38 s, so the club's 25 % or 50 % chance at 0.5–0.6 s adds about 0.1–0.2 s. Against the armored kinds, the only targets where a stun would matter, the effect is switched off. The rare and unique club's signature effect is close to worthless everywhere, and the item text does not say so.
findings.player_impact: Players who pick the club for its stun get almost nothing for it, including in the boss fights where it should shine.
findings.recommendation: Let stun_chance work on armored targets at a reduced duration (for example ×0.5, never during LUNGE). Or make it interrupt a WINDUP once per cycle. Then state the rule in ITEM_WPN_CLUB_*_DESC.
findings.verification: confirmed: Still open; prior ref mechanics-story-deep-dive C2 (docs/review/mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18.md:97-101). weapon_fx.gd:58 still has `if bool(enemy.get("armor")): return`. All bosses have armor = true, as do tornebusk and sporesvamp (enemies.lua:7,10). Every non-armoured hit already calls stun(.38) (enemy_2d.gd:320-323). on_hit runs after take_hit (player_combat_2d.gd:215-219), so the club's stun (0.5 s at p 0.25, weapons.lua:208; 0.6 s at p 0.5, :231) only lengthens an existing 0.38 s stun by 0.12-0.22 s. The extension of the prior finding is accurate.

findings.title: No dungeon material is above rare, although the owner promised rare, unique and legendary materials
evidence: lua/config/rarity.lua:2,63,78: rarities 'shared by furniture, clothing and materials', unique material_price 600 / legendary 2500 defined

lua/items/dungeon_materials.lua:116-136: dng_moon_silver / dng_crystal_root are the top tier (rare); :151,169,187 the only 'unique' materials are the three boss runes, consumed by runehvaelvingen (loot_tables.lua:768-776)
Scratch parse of lua/items/*.lua: category material/building_material legendary = 0, unique = 3 (runes only)
findings.description: Furniture, clothing, gems and weapons span all five tiers, but crafting materials stop at rare. The only 'unique' materials are key-runes that disappear when used, and nothing anywhere is a legendary material. The rarity table already prices unique and legendary materials, which suggests they were planned.
findings.player_impact: The adventure loop never produces the special materials the pitch advertises, and late crafting has no aspirational inputs.
findings.recommendation: Add 2–3 unique materials (for example 'Svampekongens spore', 'Månesølv-kerne') as boss-repeat or lake-chest drops, and one legendary material (for example 'Skovhjerte-rav') from the Konge pool. Gate one top furniture or weapon recipe in lua/recipes/dungeon.lua on them so they have a use.
findings.verification: confirmed: A scratch parse of lua/items/*.lua by (category, rarity) gives material: normal 4 / uncommon 3 / rare 2 / unique 3 (dng_rune_snurre, dng_rune_gloed, dng_rune_konge) / legendary 0, and building_material normal 14 / uncommon 7 / rare 5 with no unique or legendary. rarity.lua:2 says the ranks are 'shared by furniture, clothing and materials', and the unique and legendary rows define material_price 600 / 2500. Gems do reach legendary (gem_star_tear, gem_moon_heart, gem_rune_heart), so only 'materials' in the owner's list fall short.

findings.title: Shopkeepers leave open shops on two festival days (Sofus' badedag closes nothing; Bagedagen's host keeps the open bakery)
evidence: lua/festivals/fixed/badedagen.lua:31,34,39 - closes = "none", from = 10, to = 18 (sommer 27 = Saturday)
scripts/social/social_data.gd:278-300 - every home citizen of the area joins the roster (cap 15). Only keepers of a stays_open shop are skipped, and the host never is

lua/buildings/traetoppen.lua:17 (uglehulen 12-20, closed Mon/Thu), :26 (postkontoret 9-17, closed Sun), :73 (torvestanden 10-16, Sat/Sun); lua/buildings/ext.lua:35 (torvekroen 11-23). All of them are open on a Saturday

scripts/social/social_manager.gd:900-925 override_for - attendees stand at the festival post from one hour before the start (09:00) until the end. relationship_flow.gd:110-119 keeper_departure only makes them leave early when the shop is open after the festival ends
lua/festivals/fixed/bagedagen.lua:36,40-41 - host = baker_maja, stays_open = { bakery } (vinter 21 = Sunday; bakery open 7-17)
tools/social/core/validate_social.py:317-320 - the project's own validator warns about this exact case: 'the host ... keeps the shop that stays open (... the shop would have no keeper)'
scripts/towns/shop_counter.gd:101-110 - the 'shop' counter opens ShopSystem.open_shop even when no keeper is in the room
findings.description:
On Sofus' badedag (closes = "none"), every Trætoppen citizen joins the festival roster, and override_for puts them at the bath-house gather posts from 09:00 to 18:00. Their shops stay open under their normal hours:
- Postman Pip: Postkontoret is open 9-17 with nobody there all day.
- Fru Ugle: Uglehulen is open from 12 with nobody there until about 17:30.
- Kvak: Torvekroen is open from 11 with nobody there until about 17:45.
- Brumme: his weekend Torvestanden stall is open 10-16 with nobody there for the whole window.
On Bagedagen the host, Maja, stands on Hyggetorvet from 11:00 while her bakery is listed in stays_open and is open until 17:00. In both cases the counter still sells, but the talk/gift slots are disabled. The keeper-hours check (towns_validate.keepers_cover_hours) only tests ordinary days, so these festival days are never checked.
findings.player_impact: The player walks into an open post office, inn or bakery and finds nobody behind the counter, yet can still buy. This is exactly the 'shopkeeper absent while the shop is open' inconsistency the owner asked about. It breaks the walk-in shop fantasy on two of the nine festival days.
findings.recommendation: badedagen: either switch to closes = "all" with stays_open = { "badehuset" }, or skip keepers whose building is open during the window in SocialData.festival_roster (the same rule stays_open already uses). bagedagen: drop "bakery" from stays_open (bakery goods are sold at fest_bake_market anyway), or move hosting to Bodil. Add a test that runs keepers_cover_hours against festival_on(td) days, using override_for.
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-checked against the worktree at f80e7aed. badedagen.lua:31 has closes="none", from 10 to 18, and sommer 27 is a Saturday (first_weekday=0, game_balance.lua:89). shop_closed_by_festival (social_manager.gd:783-794) returns false when closes is none. SocialData.festival_roster (social_data.gd:278-300) only skips keepers of stays_open shops. Trætoppen has about 12 non-ghost home citizens after the host, which is under the cap of 15, so effectively all of them attend. Routines.festival_block (routines.gd:111-120) applies override_for to everyone on the roster. keeper_departure (relationship_flow.gd:110-119) only adds an early leave when the building closes after the festival ends. Kvak (Torvekroen open until 23) and Ugle (Uglehulen open until 20) therefore leave around 17:30. Pip's post office closes at 17, so he gets no early leave and is away for its whole Saturday window. Brumme's Torvestanden (traetoppen.lua:73) is open 10-16 on Saturday, also with nobody there. Hours.state/now_ctx (hours.gd:33-47, 112-140) never checks whether the keeper is present. shop_counter.gd:111-114 calls ShopSystem.open_shop with no presence check (shop_system.gd:388-394), and a 'talk' counter does nothing when keeper_node() is null. Bagedagen: vinter 21 is a Sunday, host is baker_maja, stays_open = {bakery}, and the bakery is open 7-17 (hyggebyen.lua:22-26). The validator warning at validate_social.py:317-320 is accurate. keepers_cover_hours (towns_validate.gd:74-99) only builds ctx with total_day 99, so festival days are never checked. Small note: Torvekroen has no `shop` field, so there it is an empty inn rather than a self-serve counter.

findings.title: Silke's 8-heart scene 'Det sidste lys' can only be triggered in the first 24 game minutes after waking (12 real seconds); almost no player will see it
evidence: lua/events/ghostfam/natlys.lua:458-468 - ev_ghostfam_silke_h8: area = "traetoppen", when = "hour:6-6.4&!fest:any&at:ghostfam_silke"
lua/routines/ghostfam/ghostfam_silke.lua:14 - Silke is at traetoppen.f_lamp only 06:00-06:25 (the 25:45 lamp block ends at the 02:00 pass-out)
lua/config/dungeon.lua:16 - wake_area = "farm"; lua/config/game_balance.lua:84-86 - 2 game minutes per real second, so 0.4 h = 12 real seconds

data/towns/routes.json - farm.porch to farm.gate_traetoppen is 2,860 px, and traetoppen.gate_farm to f_lamp is 3,284 px (about 6,100 ground px). lua/config/game_balance.lua:16-30 - run 450 px/s with 100 energy at 15/s (6.7 s of sprint), walk 285 px/s, so the trip takes about 17 s
docs/design/GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM.md:413 - the design offered an alternative ('or, after midnight, the vigil at the forest lift'), which was not implemented
findings.description: Every game day starts at 06:00 on the farm (after a pass-out or after sleeping). The scene only fires if the player talks to Silke at the Trætoppen lamp before 06:24. Walking straight there takes about 17 real seconds (about 15 s even for a ghost with its cheaper sprint), against a 12-second window. The only way in time is to sprint to the bridge, use the Rejsestolpe stop 'hyggebyen' (if already unlocked) and walk the last 386 px. Nothing in the game hints at this. Unlike the other heart scenes, this window cannot be waited out in place, because the player never starts a day in Trætoppen. The design's after-midnight alternative was never implemented.
findings.player_impact: In practice Silke has only one heart scene (h4). Her emotional beat at 8 hearts is lost for nearly every player, even though her hearts keep rising.
findings.recommendation: Widen the window to include the night vigil, as designed: e.g. when = "hour:23.5-25.7&!fest:any&at:ghostfam_silke" while she makes her lamp round / stands at f_lamp (ghostfam_silke.lua:20-23), keeping the dawn variant as an extra. Alternatively, make the dawn scene start automatically when the player first enters Trætoppen before 07:00 and Silke is on her f_lamp/f_bench blocks (until 06:45).
findings.verification: confirmed: natlys.lua:458-468 has when = hour:6-6.4 & !fest:any & at:ghostfam_silke. The hour term (social_manager.gd:960-962) limits it to 06:00-06:24, which is 12 real seconds at 2 game minutes per real second (game_balance.lua:84-86). The player always starts the day on the farm. A pass-out or faint goes to _wake_area() = farm (world_2d.gd:709, 753-755, 779). Ordinary sleep keeps the player at the bed, and the only bed hooks are the iso-area 'bed' marker and home furniture; no town bed marker exists (an rg for type 'bed' only matches lua/items/furniture.lua). The route distances check out: farm porch to gate_traetoppen is 2860 and traetoppen gate_farm to f_lamp is 3284 (routes.json). Silke is at f_lamp/f_bench until 06:45 (ghostfam_silke.lua:15-16), but the 6.4 hour cap is the binding limit. GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM.md:413 offers the after-midnight vigil alternative, and it is not implemented.

evidence: scripts/social/events/festival_activities.gd:9-10 - score = sell_price x (1 + 0.5 x rarity pips); :38-53 - the three bars are 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 x the BEST score in the category, each +/-15%

lua/festivals/fixed/bagedagen.lua:8-12 'Småkagekonkurrence' and honningdagen.lua:8-12 'Honningkonkurrence' use select = "category:food", whose only items are apple 5, cookie 10, flour 5, honey 12 and honey_cake 90 (uncommon)

Calculation: honey_cake scores 135, so the lowest (third-place) bar is 57-78. The best possible cookie score is 11.5 and honey 13.8, so both always come 4th. findings.description: Contests rank entries by the sell value of the item, weighted by rarity, compared against the most valuable giftable item in the whole category. The festival's own theme item can never win: a cookie at the cookie contest, honey at the honey contest, a flower at the flower contest, a pumpkin at the pumpkin contest (at most 2nd place). One item dominates each category (honey_cake for both food contests). Because the entry is used up and the prize caps are small, winning loses the player money. Getting 4th place tells the player nothing useful.
findings.player_impact: A child who brings their best cookie to the cookie contest always loses, with no explanation. The contests feel arbitrary and teach the player to sell rather than to take part. This adds to the earlier 'thin festival rewards' finding.
findings.recommendation: Make the themed item the reference: add an optional `theme = { cookie = 1.0, honey_cake = 0.8 }` (or a narrower select such as "item:cookie,honey_cake") and compute the bars from the theme's own value. Also let quality or rarity of the themed item matter. Return the entry or give a participation token. Raise the first prize to something unique per festival (a decor piece or recipe), still within the SV14 cap. Change the copy for 4th place to 'Ikke en præmie denne gang - men tak for dit bidrag!'.
