findings.title: The four heroes are unbalanced: the fairy has no perk with any gameplay effect, and the ghost dominates the dungeon
evidence: lua/config/race_perks.lua:52-55 fairy: can_fly, flight_max_seconds 8, flight_energy_per_second 10, talks_to_flowers (flavour); no economic, combat or dungeon value differs from neutral
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:260 `speed = _run * 0.9` (flight 405 px/s is slower than running at 450, game_balance.lua:17)

scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:325 and :332 try_interact/use_selected return false while is_flying (no tools, harvest or interaction in the air); :595 needs stamina >= 15; :611-612 drains 10/s and lands after 8 s
rg can_fly/is_flying: apart from player_2d.gd, only combat/footsteps read is_flying, and nothing requires flight; data/maps: @flight true only on farm, hyggebyen and secret_garden
lua/config/race_perks.lua:104-106 ghost: run_cost_mult 0.6, oil_use_mult 0.75 (200 s per fill instead of 150), dark_light_mult 1.25
lua/config/race_perks.lua:26-28 animal (Rasmus): harvest_bonus_chance 0.2 = about +20% crop income; tool_cost_mult 0.75 is close to worthless (see the energy finding)
scripts/data/perks.gd:95 `1600 gold -> 1360 fox, 1280 hobbit`: hobbit 0.10 shares the 0.20 discount_total cap (perks.gd:69-71), so with gear at its 0.15 cap the hobbit's lead drops to 5 points
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:246-254 fairy_light is available to every race, so the fairy has no dungeon niche
findings.description: The owner wants four heroes that are 'balanced and meaningfully different'. In code, the fox earns about 20% more from every harvest, the hobbit gets 10% off in shops plus a bake bonus, and the ghost gets 25% cheaper lantern oil and 25% more light radius in the dungeon (prior R1). The fairy's perks are flight and talking to flowers. Flight is slower than running, costs energy, lasts at most 8 s, blocks tools, harvest and interaction, works only on 3 maps, and no content uses it. Talking to flowers is a whisper. So the fairy is mechanically the 'no perk' choice. The ghost's run perk is real but small: cycling between running and walking after exhaustion, it travels about 6% faster than other races (360 vs 340 px/s). The ghost's oil and light advantage in the dungeon is unchanged from prior R1. The hobbit's discount shrinks late in the game because it shares the 20% cap with gear discounts.
findings.player_impact: A child who picks the fairy, likely a popular choice, quietly gets a weaker game: no extra gold, no shop savings, no dungeon help. The flight perk makes them slower than running and cannot be used to work. Ghost players have an easier dungeon.
findings.recommendation: Give the fairy a real mechanical niche in race_perks.lua, for example auto-watering the 8 neighbouring plots while landing, letting flight cross into the secret_garden or onto canopy-only forage spots, or a pollination yield bonus on crops within 2 cells (hook it in farm_grid.gd next to the harvest_bonus_chance roll at :242). Make flight at least as fast as running (player_2d.gd:260: `_run * 1.1`). Trim ghost oil_use_mult to 0.85 as R1 proposed, or give animal and hobbit a forest lever. Consider exempting the race discount from discount_total so the hobbit keeps its edge.
findings.prior_ref: mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18 R1 (Ghost is the dungeon's dominant race): still open, re-verified; the fairy half is new
findings.dim: Core loop, time, energy, heroes, save/load
findings.verification: partly: Most of the evidence checks out. race_perks.lua:44-64: the fairy gets only can_fly, 8 s of flight, 10 energy/s and talks_to_flowers. talks_to_flowers is read only at player_2d.gd:301-310, where it plays a WHISPER_FLOWER_n line. Flight runs at _run*0.9 = 405 px/s (player_2d.gd:259-260). try_interact and use_selected return false while flying (:325, :332). Take-off needs 15 energy (:595). Maps with @flight true: farm, hyggebyen, secret_garden. Ghost values 0.6/0.75/1.25 are unchanged (prior R1 still open). The ghost cycle maths is right: about 360 vs 340 px/s. The hobbit claim is right too: discount_total 0.2 against gear cap 0.15 (rarity.lua:88; perks.gd:69-71). Corrections: (1) Flight is not purely flavour. MASK_FLYING (iso.gd:50-51) leaves out LAYER_GROUND_BLOCK, so a fairy crosses ground-block tiles such as ponds. world_2d.gd's _inside_area comment says 'fairies hover over ponds'. That is a small traversal shortcut, though no content needs it. (2) The fox's harvest_bonus_chance 0.2 adds +1 to the base yield (farm_grid.gd:239-243). That is about +20% on unfertilised crops but only about +10% when fertilizer makes the base 2. (3) The quote 'balanced and meaningfully different' is not in the owner's stated intent. Balance intent appears only implicitly, in GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM.md:134. (4) Kiki (species_perks.lua:25-31) gives the animal race extra non-economic perks. A weak fairy perk set is a real balance and design gap, but no system is broken, so P2 fits better than P1. | partly: Most of the cited facts are accurate, but the finding is over-rated and half of it repeats an earlier review. Checked: race_perks.lua:52-55 (fairy has can_fly 8 s and 10/s, and talks_to_flowers, described as 'flavour ... stub'). player_2d.gd:259-260 sets flight speed to _run*0.9 (405 vs 450 px/s), and :325/:332 block interaction and tool use while flying. :595 requires stamina >= 15, and :611-612 drain energy and land the fairy after 8 s. data/maps @flight is true only on farm, hyggebyen and secret_garden; it is false on moerkeskoven, traetoppen, home and greenhouse. The flower perk is only a whisper (player_2d.gd:301-308). perks.gd:69-71 confirms the hobbit's 0.10 shares the 0.20 discount_total cap. fairy_light (player_combat_2d.gd:246) works for every race. CORRECTIONS: (1) Flight is not entirely without effect. Iso.MASK_FLYING = 1+4+64 (iso.gd:51) leaves out LAYER_GROUND_BLOCK 128, which is water, bog and the void rim (area_tileset.gd:9). The fairy can therefore fly over water and bog on the three flight maps as a shortcut. This is small, but real. (2) The fairy perk being mechanically weak is intended and documented: PLAN_2D.md:1697 lists it as 'STUB | flavour perk'. Prior review mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18.md R1 (lines 137-141) already said 'fairy's flight is traversal flavour'. (3) The 'ghost dominates the dungeon' part is prior R1 restated. It is STILL OPEN: race_perks.lua:104-106 is unchanged (run 0.6, oil 0.75, light 1.25). It should carry prior_ref R1 and not be presented as new. Its size is also overstated: GHOST_ADDENDUM.md:14 measures it at about 5% of a dive's income ('a utility perk of the fairy / hobbit class'). GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM.md:134 puts the animal at about 20% of crop income, the hobbit at about 4-5% of gross and the ghost at about 5% of a dive. So the animal, not the ghost, is the outlier in raw economic value. (4) The quoted owner requirement 'balanced and meaningfully different' does not appear in the relayed owner intent, which only lists the four hero choices. No content is gated by race, so there is no broken loop and nothing is locked. Net: this is a real design and balance gap, mainly that the fairy perk has almost no gameplay value plus the still-open R1. It belongs at P2 (design/balance), not P1.

findings.description: EconomyManager keeps a tool 'equipment' (strongest tool per type, auto-equipped on purchase, changeable with Udstyr), but no gameplay code reads it. Tool use, the stamina cost and the ore power check all use the item in the selected hotbar slot. The starter hotbar holds pickaxe_wooden (power 1). A player who buys pickaxe_iron (500 g) sees it auto-equipped, or presses Udstyr, then mines gold ore or moonstone with the starter hotbar and is told 'the tool is too weak, Thorin can help'. They have already bought Thorin's upgrade. In Mørkeskoven the HUD shows the weapon, not the selected tool.
findings.player_impact: Players can believe a 500 g upgrade is broken, or buy it twice. The ore gate that drives the pickaxe ladder becomes confusing, especially for young players.
findings.recommendation: Make one owner the source of truth. Either use_selected() and resource_node_2d.interact() resolve the tool by type through EconomyManager.equipped_item(TOOL_SLOTS[type]) (so any pickaxe in the hotbar swings the equipped best one), or equip() and _auto_equip() for tools emit hotbar_assign_requested to replace the same-type item in the hotbar. Then remove the dead get_tool_power path or wire it in, and change FOREST_TOOL_WEAK to name the tool that is needed.

findings.description: Re-verified that prior M4 is unchanged. Energy refills from empty in about 9 s of not running, so it only slows play while a large field is watered non-stop, by about 1.1 s per plot after roughly 66 plots. As a result, the two farm-tool upgrades (1,000 g together) change only a cost that barely matters, and their descriptions promise only that. findings.title: Manual save and load in the dungeon gives back full hearts, lantern oil and energy
evidence: scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd:861-877 to_dict saves area, player_pos, placed, area_flags, farm, greenhouse and hotbar, but not half_hearts, oil or stamina
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:69-72 _ready sets `stamina = max_stamina`, `half_hearts = max_half_hearts`, `oil = max_oil`

scripts/dungeon/floors/dungeon_floors.gd:283-307 from_dict keeps active and floor and registers floors -1..+1, so the load re-enters the saved floor
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:155-160 the 300 s autosave also runs on floors
findings.description: Player vitals are not part of the save. Loading a save made on a dungeon floor puts the player back on that floor at the saved position, with a freshly made Player2D at full hearts, full oil and full energy. Pause, Save, then Load is therefore a free full heal and lantern refill anywhere in Mørkeskoven. That bypasses the oil economy the prior review called 'the real resource pressure' (C5) and the 10% gold defeat penalty.
findings.player_impact: The dungeon's main tension (oil and hearts) can be skipped, and kids will find it. The reverse also happens: a legitimate Continue after a crash restores stats the player did not have.
findings.recommendation: Persist vitals: add `"vitals": {half_hearts, oil, stamina}` to world_2d.gd to_dict and apply it in _apply_saved after the player exists (clamped to the max values). Or disable manual Save while DungeonFloors.current_floor() > 0, leaving runestones as the checkpoints (pause_menu.gd:48, the same check as :50).

findings.verification: confirmed: Confirmed. world_2d.gd to_dict (:859-876) saves no vitals. The save sections (CORE_SECTIONS plus home, furniture, wardrobe, loot, dungeon and social) do not hold half_hearts, oil or stamina either. Load changes scene (save_manager.gd:321), so a new Player2D starts full (player_2d.gd:69-73). pause_menu.gd:48 always shows Save and Load, and :50-51 adds Leave Dungeon on floors. DungeonFloors.from_dict keeps active and floor and makes sure floors -1..+1 exist (dungeon_floors.gd:283-307). save_game is gated only by the 'event' modal. Save then Load is therefore a free full heal and oil refill on a floor.

findings.description: The task asked about the pass-out at 02:00 and its penalty. There is no penalty: the player wakes at 06:00 at farm:from_home with full energy, hearts and oil, exactly as if they had gone to bed. Going to bed early gains nothing, since sleep_until_morning wakes at 06:00 either way. The best routine is to never use the bed and collapse at 02:00 every night. On the farm, the main place for late watering of moonflowers, there is no warning before the collapse.
findings.player_impact: The day/night rhythm has no decision in it: the bed is cosmetic and staying up is free. The 'Udmattet' toast describes exhaustion that has no effect.
findings.recommendation: Keep it gentle but real. Option A: after a pass-out, wake at 08:00 instead of 06:00 (wake_hour + config time.pass_out_wake_delay_hours = 2) and with 50% energy once energy matters. Option B: reward the bed with a 'well rested' buff (for example +20 max energy or +5% walk speed until noon) when sleeping before 24:00. Add a farm whisper at 01:30 (a 'WHISPER_LATE' row) so children are warned outside the towns too.
findings.dim: Core loop, time, energy, heroes, save/load
findings.verification: confirmed: Confirmed. In _sleep_sequence, passed_out only changes the wake area and posts NOTIF_PASSED_OUT (world_2d.gd:698-711). _restore_player calls restore_after_sleep, which refills hearts, energy and oil (player_2d.gd:503-510). sleep_until_morning always wakes at day_start_hour (game_manager.gd:502-510). The bed has no bonus, and rg finds no rested buff. DT50 records 'no gold loss, no run end'. One nuance: in towns the curfew does more than whisper at 01:30; at 01:45 the night watch walks the player home (lua/towns.lua:16, go_home 25.75). Curfew is off on the farm and in int_ rooms (town_director.gd:44), and the HUD shows no late-night warning, so the farm point stands. The design was deliberately gentle, but the reasoning that the bed is pointless is accurate.

findings.title: Closing the window quits without saving; the pause menu's Quit autosaves
evidence: scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:88-89 `auto_accept_quit = false`; `close_requested.connect(quit_game)`
scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:91-97 quit_game only pauses, shuts down audio and quits; it does not save
scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:105-118 _leave(quit_game) calls SaveManager.autosave() first and asks for confirmation if that fails
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:72 AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS 300 (600 game minutes = half a game day)
lua/config/game_balance.lua:92 `auto_save_minutes = 30` is dead config (rg finds no reader)
findings.description: Closing the window (red close button or Cmd+Q on macOS, the close button or Alt+F4 on Windows) runs GameManager.quit_game, which never saves. Pause, Quit game does autosave. Between autosaves (every 300 real seconds while PLAYING, plus day ends) a player who closes the window loses up to half a game day of work: harvests, purchases and quest steps. Continue then loads the older autosave without saying so. The game_balance key that looks like the autosave interval does nothing.
findings.player_impact: Children usually quit by closing the window. Losing a morning of farming, or a just-bought item, with no message feels like a bug, and it is inconsistent with the menu path.
findings.recommendation: In quit_game(), when a run exists (SaveManager._game_running() and not GameManager.is_modal_open(&"event")), call SaveManager.autosave() before get_tree().quit(). Remove time.auto_save_minutes from game_balance.lua, or make SaveManager read it as the interval (minutes to seconds) instead of the const.
findings.dim: Core loop, time, energy, heroes, save/load
findings.verification: confirmed: Confirmed. game_manager.gd:88-89 routes close_requested to quit_game. quit_game (:91-97) only pauses, shuts down audio and quits. No other WM_CLOSE_REQUEST or _notification handler saves. pause_menu.gd _leave autosaves first (:105-118). main_menu.gd:17 also calls quit_game, but there is no run there. AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS is 300 (save_manager.gd:72); at minutes_per_real_second 2.0 that is 600 game minutes, about half of a 20 h day. time.auto_save_minutes = 30 (game_balance.lua:92) has no runtime reader; it appears only in the key list of tests/sections/data.gd:160.

findings.title: Builder gifts alone meet almost every cosiness gate and the finale's 'treasures' objective, so found furniture is never needed
evidence: lua/data/home_tiers.lua:176,213,254,291,328,368 gift_items: throne_root (t5), clock_moon (t6), piano_star (t7), bookshelf_floating (t8), throne_crystal (t9), bed_moon + chandelier_star (t10)
lua/items/furniture.lua decor: throne_root 24, clock_moon 42, piano_star 52, bookshelf_floating 52, throne_crystal 42, bed_moon 63, chandelier_star 42
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:372-378 hygge_levels: index 2 = 45, index 3 = 110, index 4 = 240, index 5 = 420 decor
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:244 t7 hygge=2; :282 t8 hygge=3; :319 t9 hygge=3; :358 t10 hygge=4
lua/data/starter_kit.lua:25-26 starter furniture = 7 pieces x 2 decor = 14
lua/quests/slotsdroemmen.lua:11-17 furnish_treasures target 6, placed_by_rarity 'unique,legendary'
lua/config/rarity.lua decor vs price: chair_pine 2 decor / 70 g (0.029 per g), chair_honey 5 / 180 (0.028), chair_ebony 11 / 940 (0.012), bed_walnut 16 / 2200 (0.007)
findings.description: Running totals from the gifts the builder hands over: at tier 6 the gifts already give 66 decor, which meets tier 7's hygge 2 (45). At tier 7 they give 118, which meets the hygge 3 (110) required by tiers 8 and 9. At tier 9 the gifts plus the starter kit give 226 of the 240 needed for tier 10, a gap of 7 cheap pieces. The finale quest 'Slotsdrømmen' asks for 6 placed unique or legendary pieces, and tier 10 alone has delivered 7. The tier-10 cosiness requirement (420) is then met with about 45 normal pieces at 2 decor each. So the 'go into Mørkeskoven for rare, unique and legendary furniture' loop has no role in home or story progression. Its only value is small set perks (luck is capped at 0.20 overall) and looks. Prior finding E5 (decor per gold is inverted: normal 0.029 per g vs rare 0.012) is still true. In practice the furniture-capacity limit and the gifts make it mostly irrelevant. The prior stall-risk row 'Hygge 3/4 vs capacity (High)' does not hold up: the gifts alone exceed those thresholds.
findings.player_impact: Players never need to furnish thoughtfully or hunt keepsakes. Gates labelled 'Hyggeniveau' are met without the player noticing, and the dungeon's furniture rewards feel optional.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the decor of tier gifts to rare level (about 11-16) or leave them out of the cosiness score. Or raise the requirements so placed finds matter: for example t8/t9 hygge 3 → 4 and slotsdroemmen furnish_treasures to 'unique,legendary found in the forest' (exclude tier_gift sources, or raise the target to 10). Make decor grow faster than price with rarity (for example normal 2, uncommon 6, rare 18) so that rare purchases pay off per slot.
findings.prior_ref: E5 'Hygge decor is cheapest via spam-furniture' (docs/review/mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18.md:82) - still open; the stall-risk row 'Hygge 3/4 vs furniture_capacity' in the same doc is not reproduced
findings.verification: partly: Core claim holds. FurnitureManager.hygge_score() (scripts/furniture/furniture_manager.gd:154-159) is a plain sum of `decor` over placed pieces. It has no per-type cap and no diminishing returns. Gift decor checked in lua/items/furniture.lua: throne_root 24 (unique), clock_moon 42, piano_star 52, bookshelf_floating 52, throne_crystal 42, bed_moon 63, chandelier_star 42. finish_upgrade (home_manager.gd:275) delivers gift_items(tier) on reaching that tier. Running totals: 24 / 66 / 118 / 170 / 212 / 317. hygge_levels are 0-based in GDScript: 2=45, 3=110, 4=240, 5=420 (home_tiers.lua:372-379). So t7 (hygge 2, :244) is met at t6 with 66 decor. t8 and t9 (hygge 3, :282 and :319) are met at t7 with 118. t10 (hygge 4 = 240, :358) is at 212 + 14 (starter kit, 7 pieces x 2) = 226. Capacity is no obstacle (t7 cap 46, t9 cap 65, t10 cap 74). The prior 'High' stall-risk row (mechanics-story-deep-dive:275) is indeed not reproduced. E5 (line 82) is still open: chair_pine 2/70, chair_honey 5/180, chair_ebony 11/940, bed_walnut 16/2200. Corrections: (1) 420 is not a tier-10 requirement. It is the Slotsdrømmen objective reach_royal_hygge, min_level 5 (lua/quests/slotsdroemmen.lua:19-25). From 331 decor (gifts + starter) that still needs about 45 normal pieces, which fits in the 74 slots. (2) The 7 keepsakes for furnish_treasures (target 6) are delivered across t5 to t10 (1 unique + 6 legendary), not by tier 10 alone. (3) The decor/price figures are in lua/items/furniture.lua (e.g. :545-549, :672-676, :737-741, :171-175), not lua/config/rarity.lua. The luck cap of 0.2 is confirmed at lua/config/rarity.lua:88.

findings.description: Rarity has real effects on clothing perks (speed, energy, luck, discount), on furniture decor and in 9 furniture plus 7 outfit sets with tiered bonuses and 4 legendary capstones. findings.description: The quest card is the HUD's only guidance surface, but which quests it shows is fixed: always the three accepted earliest. Long-running quests (the mother story chain, weekly or seasonal errands) occupy it permanently. Once three are active, a newly accepted quest, such as today's post letter, a board errand or a birthday task, never appears on the HUD, and the player has no way to change this.
findings.player_impact: The player has to open the journal to remember what they just agreed to do. The HUD tracker loses its purpose in mid-game, when several quests are active at once.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-quest `tracked` flag (saved) with a 'Følg / Følg ikke' row in the journal's Aktive tab. get_tracked should return tracked quests first, then the most recently progressed or accepted ones (newest first) instead of the oldest. Pin the behaviour with a hud check that uses 4 or more active quests.
findings.verification: confirmed: quest_manager.gd:1072-1078 get_tracked takes the first max_count entries of get_active_ids(). get_active_ids (1081-1092) sorts by rt.order, oldest first. hud.gd:203 calls get_tracked(3). quest_journal.gd has no track or pin control (the grep for track/pin/følg finds only fixture data). findings.description: These six panels are built in code with SocialLayout. They rebuild their whole button list on every action. The focused button is freed, TTScreen's focus-loss guard finds no last-good control and falls back to _initial_focus(), and that is 'Luk' (top-right) in each panel. They also open on 'Luk' instead of the control their screen card names. The ui_audit only checks that some initial focus exists, and tests/sections/home_ui.gd drives these panels with button.pressed.emit() and direct field writes, so this never fails a test. The spec's checks home_ui.husbyggeri_focus_walk, keyboard_only_upgrade, drawer_focus_map and chest_focus_map do not exist in tests/.
findings.player_impact: Keyboard and gamepad players (the owner asks for full keyboard play) must walk back from the top-right 'Luk' after every chest transfer, every house-tier or building pick and every animal selection. Moving 10 stacks into the chest takes about 10× the presses it should. Esc out of furniture placement loses your place in the drawer.
findings.recommendation: Before L.clear, remember the focused row's id. After rebuilding, re-grab the matching new button (the pattern appraisal_ui.gd:150 already uses), or update rows in place like shop_ui's _row_cache. Make each _initial_focus() follow its screen card: the chest's first backpack row, Husbyggeri's row tier+1, the build menu's first building, the animal from the interaction, and in Indretning the drawer row of `selected`. Add the spec'd keyboard-only checks to tests/sections/home_ui.gd using UiAudit.press instead of pressed.emit().

The core defect holds. UI_NAVIGATION.md:512-536 specifies other initial focus targets (interacted animal, first building, tier+1 row, first backpack cell). The named checks (husbyggeri_focus_walk, keyboard_only_upgrade, drawer_focus_map, chest_focus_map) appear only in docs, not in tests/. tests/sections/home_ui.gd:36,44 uses build_button.pressed.emit().

findings.title: Husbyggeri hides the current tier, and its gate rows skip the authored wording ('Borgmester Hyldeblomst 1 / 2')
evidence: scripts/ui/husbyggeri_ui.gd:59-63 every ladder row is a plain '%02d  %s' toggle. There is no built/current/next/locked state (spec S18: 'LadderRow (current / done / next with a gold chip / locked dashed)').
scripts/ui/husbyggeri_ui.gd:69-75 the gate rows (quest/friend/hygge) fall to the `_` branch '%s  %d / %d' with row.name_key. The row's own `key` is ignored.

scripts/home/home_manager.gd:178-188 each row carries key HOME_GATE_QUEST_FMT / HOME_GATE_FRIEND_FMT / HOME_GATE_HYGGE_FMT. localization/features_ui.csv:18-20 'Fuldfør opgaven: %s', '%s: %d hjerter', 'Hyggeniveau: %s' are never used.

scripts/home/home_manager.gd:198-199 any tier other than tier+1 returns not_next. Selecting an ALREADY BUILT tier shows its gold and material rows against current stock (red 'missing' rows) plus 'Byg det næste trin først.' (home_ui.csv:11).
pass3_ui_husbyggeri.png: tiers 01-10 look identical apart from the selected fill, materials show '0 / 20' in pink, and nothing says where Fyrretræsplanke/Kalk/Søm/Glasrude come from.
findings.description: The 10-step home ladder (an owner requirement) never shows which tier you live in or which are built. The gate requirements that pace tiers 4-10 (mayor friendship, crystal_cave, snurresvampen, hygge levels) appear as bare '<name>  have / need'. A heart gate reads 'Borgmester Hyldeblomst  1 / 2' with no word for hearts, a quest gate reads '<quest title>  0 / 1' without 'Fuldfør opgaven', and a hygge gate reads '<level name>  2 / 3' as level indices, although localized formats for all three exist. Browsing a past tier shows misleading unmet requirements. Missing materials get only 'Saml de manglende materialer.' with no source.
findings.player_impact: Players cannot see their own progress on the main long-term goal. They also cannot tell that tier 4 needs 2 hearts with Hyldeblomst or that tier 6 needs a deep-forest quest. Prior reviews already flagged the authored mid-tier wall (M1); this UI makes that wall unreadable.
findings.recommendation: Render each row with tr(row.key) % name (plus have/need for hearts and hygge). Mark ladder rows as done (✓, muted), current ('Dit hjem'), next (gold chip) and locked (dashed). For built tiers show 'Bygget' instead of the requirement list. Add a short source hint per material (e.g. 'Tømmerhandlen' from the shop stock lookup).
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. husbyggeri_ui.gd:61-65 ladder rows are plain '%02d  %s' toggles with no done/current/next state. :69-75 quest/friend/hygge rows fall to the `_` branch '%s  %d / %d' using name_key. HOME_GATE_QUEST_FMT/FRIEND_FMT/HYGGE_FMT (features_ui.csv:18-20) appear only as strings in home_manager.gd:180-188 and are never passed to tr(). The data has these gates: home_tiers.lua:129-131 friendship mayor_lyra=2, :241-245 mayor_lyra=4 + hygge=2, :282/:319 hygge=3, :356-358 mayor 8 + fairy_king 2 + hygge 4. So a heart gate shows as '<name>  1 / 2' and a hygge gate as level indices. requirements(n) returns gold/material rows for any n>=2, so a past tier shows them against current stock, and can_start_upgrade gives not_next → 'Byg det næste trin først.'

findings.title: Detail pane follows focus in some panels and only Enter in others (shop, backpack, garderobe)
evidence: scripts/ui/shop_ui.gd:197 rows only connect `pressed` → _activate_row. There is no focus_entered → _select, yet hover_focus is applied (:317).
scripts/ui/inventory_ui.gd:40 slots connect only `pressed` → _activate_slot.
scripts/ui/garderobe.gd:369 grid items connect only `pressed` → _activate. :365 focus_entered only scrolls.
Following focus: quest_journal.gd:144, social/people.gd:149, social/gift_picker.gd:161, appraisal_ui.gd, rune_picker.gd (focus_entered → _select).
docs/review/pass3/shots/baseline_compare/shop_ui_smith_weapon_card_da.png: gold focus ring on 'Månesplint' while the detail and Køb describe 'Jernsværd'.
pass3_ui_garderobe.png: ring on the dress tile, detail says 'Tom plads / Vælg en ting …'.
findings.description: In the journal, people, gift, appraisal and rune screens, moving focus updates the detail. In the shop, backpack and garderobe it does not. The detail, the 'I alt' total and the Køb/Brug/Tag på buttons stay bound to the last row pressed, while the gold ring sits elsewhere. Pressing Enter selects but also jumps focus to the stepper or action button, so reading through items means Enter, back, next, Enter. The mouse makes it worse: hover moves the focus ring (hover_focus) but not the detail.
findings.player_impact: When browsing a shop or the wardrobe by keyboard or pad, the ring shows one item and the description, price total and buy button another. A child can easily buy or equip the wrong thing, or never read item descriptions and rarity at all.
findings.recommendation: Connect focus_entered → _select (preview only, no focus move) on shop rows, backpack slots and garderobe tiles, as gift_picker.gd:161 does. Keep Enter as 'select and go to the action'. In the garderobe, call _select(id, false) on focus so the try-on only runs on Enter.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. shop_ui.gd:197 connects rows only through pressed→_activate_row, and _activate_row (:235-240) selects, then moves focus to the stepper or Luk. :317 has UiNav.hover_focus(_rows). inventory_ui.gd:40 is pressed→_activate_slot, which selects and grabs the first action button (:153-158). garderobe.gd:365 focus_entered only scrolls, :369 pressed→_activate. gift_picker.gd:161 and quest_journal.gd:144 connect focus_entered→_select. The shop_item_row/item_slot components add no focus hooks. UI_NAVIGATION S15 (inventory) explicitly says 'Selecting = focusing (the detail card follows)', so the backpack violates its own spec.

findings.title: Toasts are hidden while any panel is open, so a full backpack in a shop gets a 'sold out' line instead
evidence: scripts/ui/hud.gd:58 EventBus.modal_changed → toasts.visible = not GameManager.is_modal_open().
scripts/autoload/economy_manager.gd:509-511 a buy that does not fit posts only NOTIF_INVENTORY_FULL (a toast, hidden behind the shop).
scripts/economy/shop_system.gd:331-342 refusal = &"no_room".
scripts/ui/shop_ui.gd:333 keeper line = 'CANNOT_PAY' if no_gold else 'SOLD_OUT'. localization/keepers.csv:64 KEEP_ANY_SOLD_OUT 'Den er der ikke flere af lige nu.'

Toasts tick down while hidden (toast_stack.gd process ALWAYS, 4 s), so most are gone before the panel closes. That also drops STORE_ASSIGNED_FMT (inventory_ui.gd:223) and the save toast NOTIF_SAVED_MSG behind pause > Gem.
findings.description: The HUD toast stack is hidden whenever a modal is open, but several panels rely on toasts for their feedback. In the shop, a purchase that fails because the backpack is full gets no visible toast, and the keeper says the item is sold out, which is false. Other refusals (no_stock via NOTIF_NO_STOCK) are likewise invisible but at least match the keeper's line.
findings.player_impact: A player with 24/24 slots clicks Køb, sees 'Den er der ikke flere af lige nu' with stock clearly left, and doesn't learn that the backpack is the problem. The same blind spot hides hotbar-assignment confirmations and the save confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Map last_refusal &"no_room" to a keeper line such as KEEP_ANY_BAG_FULL ('Din rygsæk er fuld …') and also set a status line in the footer. More generally, keep toasts visible above the scrim (draw ToastStack on a layer above GameUI modals) or queue them until modal_changed empties the stack.
findings.prior_ref: devin-review-2026-10-15 §1.11 (shop refusal reasons not surfaced in the UI). The no_gold case is fixed; no_room is still open.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. hud.gd:58 hides toasts while any modal is open. economy_manager.gd:509-511 posts only NOTIF_INVENTORY_FULL on no room. shop_system.gd:331-342 refuses with &"no_room" when affordable. shop_ui.gd:333 maps every non-no_gold refusal to SOLD_OUT → keepers.csv:64 'Den er der ikke flere af lige nu.' shop_ui.gd:280-293 never checks backpack room before enabling Køb, so the path is reachable. ToastStack is PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS with a 4 s default (notification_toast.gd:28). The save toast is less important: save_load_ui.gd:145-148 refreshes the slot list, which is some feedback. The prior ref (devin §1.11, last_refusal not surfaced) is about the sell path, but the underlying issue is still open for no_room.

findings.title: Key hints are missing on 11 screens and almost invisible (1.7:1) where drawn on the dark scrim
evidence: Only 7 scenes carry a HintBar node (character_select, inventory_ui, save_load_ui, quest_journal, pause_menu, shop_ui, settings_ui; garderobe adds one in code). Missing on animal_care, appraisal, build_menu, home_amenities, home_chest, husbyggeri, rune_picker, gift_picker, people, forest_help/assist_panel and cheat_menu. UI_NAVIGATION.md 3.9: 'the same style is used for the hint line of every screen with focusable controls'.
scenes/ui/inventory_ui.tscn:326, quest_journal.tscn:256, shop_ui.tscn:373 put the HintBar on the root (outside the panel, on the scrim). The spec says 'bottom-right inside the panel'.

Measured from pass3_ui_inventory.png and pass3_ui_journal.png: hint text rgb(100,85,73) on scrim rgb(58,49,80) = 1.69:1 contrast. towns_city_seed_shop_panel.png shows the same problem in the real shop.
scripts/ui/indretning_ui.gd:64 INDRET_HINT and towns/post_ui.gd:84 POST_HINT ('Skift by med sidetasterne') are static prose. Indretning's lists keyboard keys even for pad players.

The shop hint offers only '↑↓ Vælg · Enter OK · Esc Tilbage'. Tab switching with PgUp/PgDn/LB/RB (shop_ui.gd:111) is never hinted, and neither is the hotbar-assign by number keys in the backpack (inventory_ui.gd:79-89).
findings.description: The hint system works (device-aware glyphs, live-key filtering), but most of the newer panels don't use it. Where it is used on full-screen panels it sits outside the parchment in #6a5a48 mono on the dark purple scrim, about 1.7:1 contrast, far below a legible threshold. Panel features that exist only as keys (page tabs, number-key assignment, R/X in Indretning) are never shown to the player.
findings.player_impact: Gamepad and keyboard players get no on-screen guidance on half the panels, and the guidance that exists on the backpack and journal is practically unreadable. This undercuts the 'full keyboard play' requirement and hides features.
findings.recommendation: Move the HintBar inside the panel's bottom edge (as pause/settings/save_load already do) or give it a chalk pill background on scrims. Add a HintBar to every TTScreen (e.g. instantiate it in TTScreen._ready when the subclass sets `hints`). Include PgUp/PgDn 'Skift fane' wherever _on_page is overridden, and '1-8 Hurtigplads' in the backpack. Replace INDRET_HINT and POST_HINT with HintBar items built from rotate_item / pickup_item / decorate / ui_page_*.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. HintBar exists in character_select, inventory_ui, quest_journal, pause_menu, settings_ui, save_load_ui and shop_ui (plus main_menu); garderobe.gd:150-152 instantiates one in code. There is none in animal_care, build_menu, husbyggeri, home_chest, home_amenities, appraisal, rune_picker, gift_picker, people or assist_panel. inventory_ui.tscn:326, quest_journal.tscn:256 and shop_ui.tscn:373 parent HintBar to the root, anchored to the screen corner and outside the panel. Token contrast Eyebrow #6a5a48 on scrim #3a3150 is about 1.83:1 (the finding measured 1.69 from antialiased pixels; same conclusion). The KeyCap glyphs (chalk on ink, gold border) stay legible in pass3_ui_inventory.png, so 'almost invisible' applies to the words rather than the keys. shop_ui.gd:63 hints omit page tabs, and inventory hints omit 1-8 (inventory_ui.gd:84). INDRET_HINT is static prose with keyboard keys only. POST_HINT does substitute a ui_cancel glyph (post_ui.gd:84) but is otherwise static.

evidence: lua/festivals/fixed/hoestfesten.lua:34 desc_key = "FEST_HOESTFESTEN_DESC", :39 spot = "torvet", :12 contest select = "category:crop". localization/festivals.csv has 9 FEST_*_DESC rows. A grep for desc_key in scripts/ finds only home_manager.gd:400 (home unlocks), so no UI ever reads a festival description.
scripts/ui/social/social_hud.gd:39-44 the day-of ribbon is name + 'åben til / fra HH:MM' only (rel_ui.csv:40-41). There is no location.

scripts/ui/social/calendar_tab.gd:118-120 the full text is only in captions (clipped) and the mouse tooltip. :122-130 the left panel always shows TODAY. Cells are focus stops that do nothing on focus or press.

pass3_ui_calendar.png and sections/social_ui_journal_calendar.png: 'Månemarkede t…', 'Blomsterfeste n…' are broken mid-word, the left panel is mostly empty, and the journal's column divider (x≈533) shows through the calendar tab above and below the grid.
findings.description: The owner wants 5 Trætoppen and 4 Hyggebyen festivals, and the data is rich (description, host, place, times, activities such as a pumpkin contest that needs a crop). The UI shows only a clipped name in the calendar and a name-plus-time ribbon on the day. Keyboard users can move through calendar days but the side panel never changes, and the full names live only in mouse tooltips.
findings.player_impact: Players don't know which town a festival is in, what happens there or what to bring (e.g. a crop for Høstfesten's contest), so festivals feel like random crowds. Planning ahead, the point of a calendar, isn't possible.
findings.recommendation: Make the calendar's left panel show the FOCUSED day: date, festival name, tr(desc_key), place (spot → area name), from-to hours, activity names and needs (e.g. 'Tag en afgrøde med'), plus birthdays. Wire cell focus_entered to that panel. Use word-wrap with ellipsis per word, not per character. Add the place to REL_HUD_FROM/OPEN ('Høstfesten i dag · Torvet · fra 12:00'). Cover the journal divider behind the calendar host.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. The 9 fixed festivals have desc_key (e.g. hoestfesten.lua:34), and spot is set (:39). No script reads desc_key except home unlocks (home_manager.gd:395-400), and no FEST_*_DESC consumer exists. social_hud.gd:39-44 ribbon is name + from/open time. calendar_tab.gd:118-130 puts the full text only in captions and the tooltip. The left panel always shows today (date, birthdays, festival name), and no cell has focus_entered/pressed handlers (only the season chips :41 and edge wrap :146-153). pass3_ui_calendar.png shows 'Månemarkede t…' and 'Bagerfe' clipped mid-word and an empty left panel. I could not confirm the journal-divider bleed claim from pass3_ui_calendar.png (fixture without the journal), so I leave it unverified. Festival hosts do speak FEST_<ID>_OPEN/END lines in-world (festival_director.gd:117), but that is not a UI description.

findings.title: Indretning drawer: invisible active filter, room for about 1 row, overlaps the HUD, and controls bypass the input map
evidence: scripts/ui/indretning_ui.gd:41-51 the 12 layer and rarity filter buttons are plain ButtonTertiaryS: no toggle_mode or button_group, so the active filter is never shown (pass3_ui_indretning.png: both 'Alle' chips look like every other chip).

indretning_ui.gd:29 panel Rect2(24,80,340,590). The filter grid plus header leave a list viewport of about 60 px. pass3_ui_indretning.png shows 'Jernstanderlampe ×1' cut mid-row, and the panel covers the HUD date chip ('Forår · Dag 1' peeks out behind it).
indretning_ui.gd:113-117 drawer rows are a bare TTItemIcon + 'name ×n' button with no rarity tile, pips or rarity name, although rarity is a filter.

indretning_ui.gd:169-170 rotate = physical KEY_R or JOY_BUTTON_Y and pickup = KEY_X or JOY_BUTTON_X, hard-coded. project.godot defines rotate_item (R / pad button 10 = RB) and pickup_item (X / RMB / pad X), and spec S19 says 'rotate_item (R / RB)'. On a pad, RB does not rotate.
Spec S19 asks for filter chips as a radio row switched with Left/Right/LB/RB. Here they are a 3×4 button grid and _on_page is not overridden.
findings.description: The furniture drawer is the main surface for one of the owner's headline features. The filter state is invisible, so after choosing 'Sjælden' the player can't tell why the list shrank. The list area shows about one and a half rows, so any real collection is a long scroll through a slot. The panel sits over the HUD. Rarity, an owner requirement, appears only as a filter, never on the items. Gamepad rotate uses Y instead of the mapped RB, and the in-panel hint lists only keyboard keys.
findings.player_impact: Decorating, the payoff of collecting furniture, is cramped and confusing, and players can lose track of which filter is on. Pad players following the spec or the input map can't rotate with RB.
findings.recommendation: Make the filters PillTab toggles in ButtonGroups (or one radio row cycled by ui_page_*). Collapse the rarity filters into a single cycling chip, which frees about 120 px for the list. Use RaritySlot rows with pips, as spec S19 says. Hide the HUD date chip in decorate mode or move the drawer below it. Replace the hard-coded keys with event.is_action_pressed(&"rotate_item") / (&"pickup_item").
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. indretning_ui.gd:41-51 filter buttons have no toggle_mode or ButtonGroup, so the active filter is invisible. :29 panel is Rect2(24,80,340,590), and pass3_ui_indretning.png shows about 1.5 list rows, 'Jernstanderlampe ×1' clipped, and the HUD date chip 'Forår · Dag 1' peeking out behind the panel. :113-117 rows are TTItemIcon + 'name ×n' with no rarity. :169-170 hard-code KEY_R/JOY_BUTTON_Y and KEY_X/JOY_BUTTON_X. project.godot maps rotate_item to R + joy button 10 (RIGHT_SHOULDER) and pickup_item to X + joy 2. A grep finds no use of rotate_item/pickup_item in scripts, so pad RB does not rotate (pad X pickup happens to match). _on_page is not overridden.

findings.title: Cheat menu ships in the player's pause menu and on F8, ungated
evidence: scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:43 rows.append(["CheatButton", "CHEAT_TITLE", …]) unconditionally.
project.godot:59 cheat_menu action (F8). scripts/ui/testing/cheat_menu.gd:2 'F8 and pause-menu access'.
localization/cheats.csv:2 'Testmenu · F8', :10 'Giv 10.000 guld'. The menu also unlocks all clothing, fills hearts/energy/oil, travels anywhere and sets time and weather (PLAYING.md:73).

pass3_ui_pause.png and sections/menus_pause_full_game.png: 'Testmenu · F8' sits between Garderobe and Gem, and it is the only pause row that shows a hotkey.
findings.description: The test menu is a first-class row in the player-facing pause menu and one key away in any build. Its actions write to the normal save ('Genstande, penge og fremskridt bliver gemt med spillet.'). Release targets are macOS and Windows exports, and nothing hides it in a release build.
findings.player_impact: A child who opens the pause menu sees 'Testmenu' and can give themselves 10 000 gold, skip progression and unlock all clothing permanently in their save. That collapses the economy and home progression the game is balanced around.
findings.recommendation: Show the row and the F8 binding only when OS.is_debug_build() or a dev feature tag / settings flag is set (pause_menu.gd _specs and cheat_menu._hotkey_open_allowed). Keep the tests working through the debug build. Optionally give non-debug builds a hidden code entry for the owner.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. pause_menu.gd:43 appends CheatButton unconditionally, with no _screen() null check. cheat_menu.gd:25 hotkey_action=&"cheat_menu" (F8). _hotkey_open_allowed → cheat_actions.gd:8-10 Actions.available() checks only world state, not build type. The only OS.is_debug_build use is lua_runtime.gd:71/76. cheats.csv:2,7,10 confirm 'Testmenu · F8', the persistence notice and 'Giv 10.000 guld'. findings.title: No accessibility settings: no key remapping, text size, text/hint speed or reduce-motion option
evidence: scripts/ui/settings_ui.gd:4-6 - the only persisted options are PATH settings.cfg, SIZES [1280x720,1600x900,1920x1080], BUSES [Master, Music, Sfx, Voice]
scripts/ui/settings_ui.gd:16-36 - the controls wired up are language, four volume sliders, fullscreen, window size, plus the in-world 'Hjælp i skoven' button
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_ui_settings.png - Sprog / Hovedvolumen / Musik / Lyde / Stemmer / Fuldskærm / Vindue only
docs/design/UI_NAVIGATION.md:337 - 'a rebinding in a later version changes the hint' (remapping is deferred, and no InputMap.action_erase_events/action_add_event exists in scripts/)
scripts/world2d/player_combat_2d.gd:220,302,320 - camera shake (_shake_camera 2.0 / 4.0) with no toggle
assets/ui/theme.tres:4038,4123,4139 - Eyebrow 11 px, HintButton 11 px, KeyCap 13 px: the smallest text, with no UI-scale option
scripts/ui/dialogue_ui.gd:39 - typewriter speed is a Lua config value, not a player setting
findings.description: Settings offer only language, volume, fullscreen and window size. Players cannot rebind keys, cannot enlarge text or UI, cannot slow or lengthen transient text (whispers and toasts), and cannot turn off camera shake. A colour-vision option is missing too, though rarity already carries shapes. The forest assist panel covers combat difficulty only. For a children's game whose release targets are desktop keyboard/mouse plus gamepad, remapping and text size are baseline expectations, and the code already reads glyphs from the live InputMap, so remapping would propagate to all hints.
findings.player_impact: Left-handed players, players with motor impairments or AZERTY/odd layouts, and young or low-vision readers cannot adapt the game. Small 11-13 px hint and secondary text cannot be enlarged.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Tilgængelighed' section to settings_ui: (1) a key-remap list over the actions in project.godot, written to settings.cfg [input] and applied at boot; UiHints already reads the live InputMap. (2) A UI scale of 100/115/130% via content_scale_factor, or theme font-size multipliers. (3) 'Tekst bliver stående' (whisper/toast duration ×1.5/×2, or until dismissed). (4) 'Ryst skærmen' on/off, gating _shake_camera. (5) Typewriter speed, including instant. Store all of it beside the existing [audio]/[video] sections.
findings.verification: confirmed: settings_ui.gd:4-6 and 16-36 match: language, 4 bus sliders, fullscreen, 3 window sizes, plus the ASSIST_TITLE forest-help button. A grep of scripts/ finds no action_erase_events, action_add_event, content_scale_factor or ui_scale. player_combat_2d.gd:220/302 call _shake_camera(2.0/4.0) at :320 with no toggle. theme.tres:4038 Eyebrow 11, :4123 HintButton 11, :4139 KeyCap 13. dialogue_ui.gd:39 reads chars_per_second from Lua config ui.dialogue_chars_per_second. UI_NAVIGATION.md:337 defers rebinding. Accurate as stated.

findings.title: Tutorial and refusal feedback are 3.5-second whispers shown once per save, replaced by the next whisper, and impossible to re-read
evidence: scripts/ui/components/whisper_line.gd:9 - SECONDS := 3.5 regardless of text length; :3-5 - 'A second whisper replaces the first and restarts the timer'
scripts/farm/steading/tutorial/tutorial_hints.gd:94-96 - sets flag tut_hint_<id> and then emits the whisper, so each farm tutorial hint is shown at most once per save
lua/farm/farm_tutorial.lua:24-37 - all ten farm hints (hoe, seeds, can, harvest, bin, energy, bridge, bed, mail, expand) are delivered this way
localization/farm_tutorial.csv:23 TUT_HINT_BED (13 words), localization/dungeon_run.csv:62 DTUT_HUB (15 words), localization/look.csv:2 LOOK_NATTEBLIK_SLEEPS (15 words): each must be read in 3.5 s
No help, controls or 'Sådan spiller du' screen exists: no HELP_/GUIDE_/CONTROLS_ keys in any CSV
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_farm_day_hud.png - the hint box (x≈40-392) also overlaps hotbar slot 1, the very slot it tells you to pick
findings.description: The farm tutorial, the dungeon tutorial (DTUT_*) and every world refusal (bed before 18, locked warp, wrong tool) go through WhisperLine, which shows text for a fixed 3.5 s. A child reading 1.5-2 words/s needs 7-10 s for a 13-15-word hint. Each farm hint is flagged as shown the moment it is emitted, so a hint missed while looking elsewhere, or overwritten by another whisper (only one at a time), is lost for the whole save. Nothing in the game lets the player look the instructions up again.
findings.player_impact: Young players miss core instructions (how to sleep, sell, water, use runestones) with no way to recover them, which leads to confusion or stalling in the first days.
findings.recommendation: Make the duration length-based: max(4.0, 1.5 + 0.4 × word count) s, multiplied by the new accessibility setting. Queue whispers instead of replacing them, or at least never replace a tutorial whisper with a refusal. Keep a tutorial hint on screen until its step completes ('on' event) instead of a timer. Add a 'Hjælp' tab to the journal (quest_journal) that lists every hint already shown (the tut_hint_<id> flags already record them) plus the controls from UiHints.
findings.verification: confirmed: whisper_line.gd:9 SECONDS := 3.5, and :3-5 documents replace-and-restart. tutorial_hints.gd sets tut_hint_<id> immediately before emitting whisper_requested, so a hint is consumed once per save. farm_tutorial.lua:26-37 lists the 10 hints and enforces a gap of at least 12 s (tutorial hints cannot overwrite each other, but refusal whispers still can). Rows verified: TUT_HINT_BED farm_tutorial.csv:23, DTUT_HUB dungeon_run.csv:62, LOOK_NATTEBLIK_SLEEPS look.csv:2. No HELP_/CONTROLS_ screen keys exist; the only grep hits are DLG_CHOICE_HELP_* and SG_GUIDE_*. In pass3_farm_day_hud.png the whisper box reaches x~392 and clips the edge of hotbar slot 1. Partial mitigation: the persistent tracker shows the forste_dage objectives (e.g. 'Hak tre felter 0/3'), so the step goal stays visible even though the key instructions are lost.

findings.title: Key-hint bar is about 1.8:1 contrast on dark-backdrop screens (inventory, journal and others)
evidence: scripts/ui/components/hint_bar.gd:3 - 'Plex Mono 11 (Eyebrow, #6a5a48)'; :125,129 - the word labels use Eyebrow
assets/ui/theme.tres:4036-4038 - Eyebrow font_color (0.416,0.353,0.282) = #6a5a48, font_size 11
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_ui_inventory.png and pass3_ui_journal.png (bottom right: 'Vælg · OK · Tilbage') - bar drawn on the dark plum backdrop (58,49,80)
Computed WCAG ratio: #6a5a48 on (58,49,80) = 1.83:1 (pixel-sampled 1.6-1.7:1); the same colour is 5.35:1 on the cream panel and 4.26:1 on the lilac shop backdrop
findings.description: HintBar always uses the Eyebrow style, which was designed for cream panels. On screens where the bar sits outside the panel on the dark modal backdrop, the brown 11 px mono words are close to invisible. Only the KeyCap chips are readable, so the player sees the keys but not what they do.
findings.player_impact: Keyboard and gamepad players cannot read what Enter/Esc/arrows do on the inventory and journal screens, which are among the most used.
findings.recommendation: Give HintBar an 'on_dark' variant, for example EyebrowOnDark with cream #fbf5e6 (≈12:1 on #3a3150) at 13 px. Select it automatically when the bar's parent is the screen root rather than a panel, or set it in inventory_ui/quest_journal. Add a ui_audit contrast check of ≥4.5:1 for HintBar labels.
findings.verification: confirmed: hint_bar.gd:125/129 use Eyebrow for the separator and the words. theme.tres:4037 Eyebrow color (0.416,0.353,0.282) = #6a5a48. inventory_ui.gd:61 and quest_journal.gd:48 set the hints. In pass3_ui_inventory.png the bar sits bottom-right on the plum backdrop and 'Vælg · OK · Tilbage' is nearly invisible. Recomputed WCAG: #6a5a48 on (58,49,80) = 1.83:1.

findings.title: Hero-select blurbs are design-sheet notes shown verbatim to players, gendered and partly wrong
evidence: scripts/ui/character_select.gd:106 - %HeroBlurb.text = tr(chosen.blurb_key)
localization/cast.csv:6 HERO_RASMUS_BLURB 'Standardfiguren, når man vælger skovdyr. Stærke poter, så han graver hurtigere…'
localization/cast.csv:9 HERO_KLOEVERMYNTE_BLURB 'Driver frøbutikken i Hyggebyen. Samme grundfigur bruges, når spilleren vælger at være fe…'

localization/cast.csv:12 HERO_BIRK_BLURB 'Mandlig variant af feen og Kløvermyntes bror…'; :18 HERO_BODIL_BLURB 'Kvindelig variant af halvlingen og Bertils søster…'; :15 'Standardfiguren for halvlinge'; ghost.csv:10 'Standardfiguren for spøgelser'
cast.csv:3 comment - 'the card BLURB verbatim from the Figurer v2 sheet (English = draft)'
docs/copy/STYLE_SHEET.md R3 - 'no sentence assumes the hero's gender'
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_ui_select_1.png - 'Standardfiguren, når man vælger skovdyr…' shown under the Udseende chips
findings.description: The look descriptions on character select are art-direction notes ('default figure', 'base figure is used when the player chooses…', 'male/female variant of…'), not player copy. The fairy look tells the player that their hero runs the seed shop, which conflicts with the NPC Kløvermynte who does run it. Rasmus's text uses 'han' and two blurbs frame looks as male/female variants, contrary to R3.
findings.player_impact: The first screen of the game reads like an internal document. Choosing the Kløvermynte look implies the player is the shopkeeper, and the gendered framing goes against the project's own rule.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite HERO_*_BLURB (da+en) as short in-world descriptions with no 'figur/variant/spilleren' and no he/she. Example for Rasmus: 'En rød ræv med stærke poter. Graver hurtigt og får mere ud af høsten.' For Kløvermynte: 'Lette vinger og blomsterkrans. Kan flyve kort over markerne.' Keep the design notes in docs/ or as CSV comment rows. Add 'figur', 'variant' and 'spilleren' to tools/copy/forbidden_words.json for CHAR_/HERO_ keys.
findings.verification: confirmed: character_select.gd:106 shows tr(chosen.blurb_key), and pass3_ui_select_1.png shows 'Standardfiguren, når man vælger skovdyr… så han graver…' under Udseende. Several cited line numbers are wrong: cast.csv:6 RASMUS is correct, but KLOEVERMYNTE is :12 (not :9), BIRK :15, BERTIL :18 and BODIL :21; ghost.csv:9 is HERO_BU and :12 is HERO_HVISKE ('variant af spøgelset'). The texts are exactly as described. The cast.csv:3 comment confirms they are verbatim sheet notes. STYLE_SHEET R3 (line 41) forbids hero-gender assumptions.

findings.title: Social copy is mad-lib templated: identical NPC bios, gift reactions, birthday, bark and shop lines across citizens and archetypes
evidence: localization/social_talk.csv:21,41,61,81,…,336 - 30 of 34 *_BIO_1 rows follow 'Du møder mig ved X. Jeg holder af Y og af de små samtaler, der gør Trætoppen hjemlig.' (incl. Hyggebyen residents Kløvermynte/Birk/Hyldeblomst and Natteblik, who 'Bor i Mørkeskoven' per cast.csv:25)
localization/gifts.csv - 125 rows, 5 distinct Danish texts: all 25 citizens' GIFT_<NPC>_LOVE_1_V = 'Du har fundet noget, jeg holder særligt af. Tak!' (gifts.csv:2…122)
localization/birthdays.csv - 20 rows, 2 distinct texts
localization/social_arch.csv - per slot across the 8 archetypes: GIFT_* 16 lines → 2 distinct, BDAY 16 → 2, BARK 48 → 6, SHOP 32 → 4 (e.g. :26-35 CHILD = :230-239 ELDER)
scripts/social/talk/social_talk.gd:76-78 - gift reaction cascade GIFT_<NPC>_ → SOC_ARCH_<ARCH>_GIFT_ → SOC_ANY_, so every citizen draws from the same 3 lines per taste
docs/copy/ARCHETYPES.md:3 - 'These sheets separate the eight social voices'
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_ui_people.png - Gartner Hoppe's bio shows the template
Also odd semantics: SOC_RASMUS_BIO_1 'Du møder mig ved min rygsæk', SOC_POSTMAN_PIP_BIO_1 'ved min posttaske', SOC_ARCH_*_BARK_2 'En nabo går forbi.' (an NPC narrating)
findings.description: The lint (C6) checks that every citizen has a FIRST/GIFT/BDAY/GREET cascade, but the rows that fill it are copies. The per-citizen gift rows are the same five sentences duplicated 25 times, and the archetype pools that were meant to separate voices hold identical text in all eight archetypes. Greetings (GREET_H0-H3: 24 distinct per band) and the ghost family are genuinely varied. Gifts, birthdays, barks, shop banter and the bio card on the People screen are not.
findings.player_impact: Giving gifts, a core loop of the social sim the owner requires, produces the same reaction from every citizen. Bios on the People screen read as one form letter, so citizens feel interchangeable.
findings.recommendation: Give each tier-A/B citizen one authored GIFT_<NPC>_<TASTE> line and one BIO line in their own voice and place (fix Hyggebyen/Mørkeskoven residents). Rewrite SOC_ARCH_*_{GIFT_*,BDAY,BARK,SHOP} per archetype using the ARCHETYPES.md verbal tics. Extend copy_lint.py with a rule that flags a Danish text shared by more than 3 keys in social/gift/birthday CSVs (allow-list choices). _V rows need regenerated placeholders; no human recordings are affected.
findings.verification: confirmed: Python check: gifts.csv has 125 rows and 5 distinct Danish texts; birthdays.csv has 20 rows and 2 distinct texts. In social_talk.csv all 30 *_BIO_1 rows (30/30, not 30/34) follow the 'Du møder mig ved X… der gør Trætoppen hjemlig' template, including Natteblik, Birk and the mayor. social_arch.csv distinct texts per slot: GIFT_* 16→2 each, BDAY 16→2, BARK 48→6, SHOP 32→4; GREET_H0-3 are 24/24 distinct. social_talk.gd:76-78 cascade is GIFT_<NPC>_<TASTE> → SOC_ARCH → SOC_ANY, so the per-NPC row always wins and is identical across all NPCs.

findings.title: Math quest shows its own answers in the tracker and journal; tracker format produces '.:' and '::'
evidence: lua/quests/math_harvest_puzzle.lua:8-31 - targets 12 / 21 / 8 are the answers to 3×4, 7×3, 4×2 (header comment: 'the objective TARGETS are the answers')
localization/quests.csv:83-85 OBJ_MATH_HARVEST_PUZZLE_* 'Høst gulerødder: 3 × 4', 'Skaf sten: 7 × 3', 'Skaf sjældne svampe: 4 × 2'
scripts/ui/hud.gd:221 - label.text = "%s: %d / %d" % [objective_text, current, target] → 'Høst gulerødder: 3 × 4: 0 / 12'
scripts/ui/components/quest_details.gd:26-27 - journal appends '  (%d / %d)' when target > 1 → 'Skaf sten: 7 × 3  (0 / 21)'
24 of 119 OBJ_ texts end in '.' (e.g. localization/ghostfamily_quests.csv:20 'Giv et æble fra Silke til Oak.') → tracker 'Oak.: 0 / 1'; 9 contain ':' (quests.csv:80-88) → double colon
hud.gd:221 format string is hard-coded, not a localization key
findings.description: The 'Tal-høsten' learning quest asks children to work out 3×4 and so on, but the HUD tracker and the journal print the target count beside the expression, so the answer is always visible. The same hard-coded tracker format also creates punctuation noise for objectives that already contain ':' or end with '.'. Objective punctuation is inconsistent overall.
findings.player_impact: The educational point of one of the three math quests is defeated. The HUD reads sloppily ('3 × 4: 0 / 12', '…Oak.: 0 / 1').
findings.recommendation: For quests with meta.tag 'LÆR' (or an objective flag hide_target = true), show only the current count, or '? ' until done, in hud.gd and quest_details.gd. Move the tracker format into a key (QJ_TRACK_FMT '%s · %d/%d'). Strip trailing '.' from OBJ_ rows, or have the tracker trim it, and add a copy_lint rule: OBJ_ texts contain no ':' and no final period.
findings.verification: confirmed: math_harvest_puzzle.lua:2 and :10-31 set targets 12/21/8. quests.csv:83-85 objective texts end in '3 × 4' etc. hud.gd:221 uses the hard-coded "%s: %d / %d", giving 'Høst gulerødder: 3 × 4: 0 / 12' (answer visible plus a double colon). quest_details.gd appends '  (%d / %d)' when target > 1. Recount: 119 OBJ_ rows, 24 ending in '.', 9 containing ':' (math_wizard_quiz targets are 1, so the answer is not leaked there). The answer-reveal undermines the learning quest; the punctuation part alone would be P3.

findings.title: 'Hakke' means both hoe and pickaxe: mining prompts name the wrong tool
evidence: localization/economy.csv:3 ITEM_HOE_WOODEN 'Hakke' (hotbar slot 1); :5 ITEM_HOE_IRON 'Jernhakke'
localization/economy.csv:11 ITEM_PICKAXE_WOODEN 'Spidshakke'; :13 ITEM_PICKAXE_COPPER 'Kobberhakke'; :15 ITEM_PICKAXE_IRON 'Jernspidshakke'
localization/forest.csv:18 FOREST_PROMPT_MINE 'Brug hakken' (EN 'Use the pickaxe'); :20 FOREST_TOOL_PICKAXE 'Vælg din hakke, og slå på stenen.'
localization/farm_site.csv:48 FARMSITE_MACHINE_PICKUP 'Brug hakke eller økse…' (means pickaxe)
localization/farm_tutorial.csv:16 TUT_HINT_HOE 'Vælg hakken med %s' (means hoe)
findings.description: The farm tutorial teaches that 'hakken' is the hoe in slot 1. The forest and machine prompts then say 'Brug hakken' / 'Vælg din hakke' when they mean the pickaxe (slot 4, 'Spidshakke'). The upgrade names make it worse: the copper pickaxe is 'Kobberhakke' while 'Jernhakke' is the iron hoe, so 'Kobberhakke → Jernhakke' looks like one upgrade line.
findings.player_impact: Children select the hoe for stones and ore, get no result or a 'too weak' whisper, and may buy the wrong upgrade at the smithy.
findings.recommendation: Use 'spidshakke' for every pickaxe reference: FOREST_PROMPT_MINE 'Brug spidshakken', FOREST_TOOL_PICKAXE 'Vælg din spidshakke, og slå på stenen.', FARMSITE_MACHINE_PICKUP 'Brug spidshakke eller økse…', ITEM_PICKAXE_COPPER 'Kobberspidshakke'. Add a glossary row (Hakke = hoe, Spidshakke = pickaxe) to docs/copy/GLOSSARY.md.
findings.verification: confirmed: economy.csv:3 Hakke (hoe), :5 Jernhakke (iron hoe), :11 Spidshakke, :13 Kobberhakke (copper pickaxe), :15 Jernspidshakke. forest.csv:18 FOREST_PROMPT_MINE 'Brug hakken' and :20 'Vælg din hakke…' are used by resource_node_2d.gd:90/97 for stone nodes. farm_site.csv:48 is used by farm_machine_2d.gd:21/32. TUT_HINT_HOE teaches hakken = hoe in slot 1. The collision is real.

findings.title: Debug 'Testmenu · F8' (cheats) is an unconditional row in the player pause menu
evidence: scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:47 - rows.append(["CheatButton", "CHEAT_TITLE", _transfer.bind(&"cheat_menu")]) with no OS.is_debug_build()/feature check
scripts/ui/testing/cheat_menu.gd:1-30 - no release gating; hotkey_action cheat_menu (F8)
localization/cheats.csv:2 CHEAT_TITLE 'Testmenu · F8'; :10 CHEAT_GOLD 'Giv 10.000 guld'
docs/review/pass3/shots/pass3_ui_pause.png - 'Testmenu · F8' second row, above Gem
findings.description: The pause menu always offers the developer cheat menu (gold, items, travel, clock) with developer copy. Nothing in f80e7aed gates it to debug builds, and release targets are macOS and Windows exports. The main checkout has uncommitted changes to pause_menu.gd that may address this; they are not on this commit.
findings.player_impact: Children will find 'Testmenu' and give themselves 10,000 gold and every item, which collapses progression and shows unfinished copy in the release build.
findings.recommendation: Append the CheatButton row only when OS.is_debug_build() or OS.has_feature("cheats"), and skip registering the cheat_menu hotkey and screen in game_ui otherwise. Add an export_presets.cfg check in tools/release that the release preset does not set the feature.
findings.verification: confirmed: pause_menu.gd:47 appends CheatButton/CHEAT_TITLE unconditionally. The only is_debug_build/has_feature checks in scripts/ are in lua_runtime.gd hot-reload. cheat_menu.gd sets hotkey_action cheat_menu (project.godot:59) and is listed in game_ui.gd:38. Correction to the description: the main checkout (branch codex/release-pipeline) has no uncommitted pause_menu.gd change. Committed 084321db edits pause_menu.gd but only adds a map_ui row, so the cheat row is still ungated on the release branch too, and export_presets/release.py contain no cheat gating. Severity could arguably be higher for a release build (10.000 guld, travel, clock).

findings.title: intro_done flag collision: the mayor's welcome scene can never play, and first meeting says 'Good to see you again!'
evidence: scripts/farm/steading/tutorial/tutorial_runner.gd:93 "GameManager.set_flag(&\"intro_done\", true)" at the end of the first morning (default flow, also on Esc-skip)
lua/dialogue/mayor_lyra.lua:8-9 "local intro_done = context.intro_done ... if not intro_done then" (welcome + lottery branch)
lua/dialogue/mayor_lyra.lua:46-60 fallback branch DLG_LYRA_HELLO + DLG_LYRA_FARM_STATUS
localization/dialogue.csv:26 DLG_LYRA_HELLO "Godt at se dig igen!"; :23 DLG_LYRA_FARM_STATUS "Din gård trives! Fortsæt det gode arbejde."
localization/social_talk.csv:2 SOC_MAYOR_LYRA_FIRST_1_V "Jeg er Hyldeblomst. Vi finder en plads til dig i Trætoppen." (prepended on first meeting by dialogue_bridge.gd:17-19)
lua/quests/intro_lottery.lua:66 sets intro_done on quest completion (the meaning mayor_lyra.lua expects)
localization/quests.csv:66-67 OBJ 'Gå over broen til Trætoppen' then 'Tal med borgmester Hyldeblomst' (she lives in Hyggebyen, npcs.lua:45, one bridge further; the objective does not say where)
findings.description: intro_done is used for two different things. TutorialRunner sets it as soon as the first morning ends. mayor_lyra.lua uses it to mean 'intro_lottery finished', so it can decide whether to play the welcome and lottery scene. In a normal new game the flag is already true before the player reaches Hyggebyen, so the welcome branch (DLG_LYRA_GREET_1/2, DLG_LYRA_LOTTERY, INFO_LOTTERY) is unreachable. The real first conversation with the mayor, which is also the objective that completes the intro quest, reads: 'Jeg er Hyldeblomst. Vi finder en plads til dig i Trætoppen.' / 'Godt at se dig igen!' / 'Din gård trives! Fortsæt det gode arbejde.' That is on day 1, usually with one seed planted. A ghost hero gets a fourth greeting on top (DLG_GHOST_MAYOR). The intro objective also only says 'Tal med borgmester Hyldeblomst' after sending the player to Trætoppen, while she lives one bridge further in Hyggebyen. Separately, prior S-L is still open: Lyra repeats the same two lines for the rest of the game.
findings.player_impact: The first story NPC the player is sent to meets them with contradictory, canned lines ('I am Hyldeblomst' followed by 'good to see you again'). The intro's payoff ('Velkommen til Trætoppen!') falls flat, and the authored welcome is dead content.
findings.recommendation: Rename the tutorial's flag (for example first_morning_done) in tutorial_runner.gd:22 and :93 and in tests/lib/flow.gd and farm_first_morning.gd. Leave intro_done to intro_lottery.lua:66, or have mayor_lyra.lua read quest_done_intro_lottery instead. Rewrite DLG_LYRA_GREET_2/LOTTERY for a player who already lives on the farm. Give OBJ_INTRO_LOTTERY_TALK_TO_MAYOR a location ('…i Hyggebyen, én bro længere'). Add one or two state-dependent Lyra lines (garden restored, Mum's trail finished) to close S-L.
findings.prior_ref: S-L (mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18) static Lyra dialogue is still open; the flag collision itself is new
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-checked. tutorial_runner.gd:93 sets intro_done at the end of the first morning, and also on the Esc path (lines 85-95). farm_tutorial.lua:13 has enabled = true. npc_dialogue.gd:8 copies GameManager.world_flags into the dialogue context, so mayor_lyra.lua:8-9 sees intro_done == true and always takes the HELLO/FARM_STATUS branch. GREET_1/2, LOTTERY and INFO_LOTTERY are unreachable in a default new game; the only path that reaches them is the letter-only fallback (enabled=false). DialogueBridge.decorate (dialogue_bridge.gd:17-19) prepends SOC_MAYOR_LYRA_FIRST_1_V on first meeting, because mayor_lyra has friendship = true (npcs.lua:40-52). RaceReactions.apply adds DLG_GHOST_MAYOR for ghost heroes. That gives the stated sequence 'Jeg er Hyldeblomst…' / 'Godt at se dig igen!' / 'Din gård trives!'. intro_lottery's talk_to_mayor objective (on=dialogue_started) completes on this conversation. OBJ_INTRO_LOTTERY_TALK_TO_MAYOR (quests.csv:67) gives no location, while home_area = hyggebyen and intro_lottery.lua:3 says Hyggebyen is one bridge further. Side note: intro_lottery.lua:76 is_available also reads intro_done, so the flag carries a third meaning. Prior S-L (static Lyra lines) is still open.

findings.title: rune_vandring (and skovlift_intro) get stuck forever if the runestones were lit before accepting
evidence: scripts/dungeon/floors/dungeon_floors.gd:220-226 activate_stone(): "if first: EventBus.game_event.emit(&\"dungeon_runestone_activated\",payload)" fires only the first time a stone is lit
lua/quests/rune_vandring.lua:5-20 rune_5/rune_9 bind to that event with min_level 5/9 and have no completed_flag; :53-55 is_available returns true from day 1 with no forest gate
lua/quests/skovlift_intro.lua:13-18 light_rune binds to the same first-only event
lua/config/dungeon.lua:157,205,257,312,362 stones only on floors 3,5,7,9,11 (the hub rune is the picker, moerkeskoven.map:34)
scripts/autoload/quest_manager.gd:1002-1005 a catch-up path for already-earned achievements exists (completed_flag) but neither quest uses it
no abandon or cancel action in quest_manager.gd or quest_journal.gd (rg 'abandon' finds nothing)
findings.description: Both quests wait for the event that fires the first time a runestone is lit, and a stone is never lit twice. rune_vandring needs a new first activation on floor 9 or deeper. Stones exist only on floors 9 and 11 at that depth, and the player has to go through floors 9 to 12 for mother chapters S06 to S08 and for the home tier 6 gate (crystal_cave, floors 10 to 12). So anyone who opens Fru Ugle's unprompted quest after reaching floor 11 can never finish it. It stays 'active' in the journal for ever, and since it is not repeatable it cannot be offered again. skovlift_intro ('Første tur ned') has the same fault, but it only triggers if all five stones are lit before the player talks to Oak.
findings.player_impact: A permanently unfinishable adventure quest that sits in the journal for good, and its key/gem-bag reward is lost. This undercuts the story's promise that 'En tidligere sejr gælder stadig'.
findings.recommendation: Give these objectives the same catch-up as bossernes_vej: either a state query 'runestone_lit_at_least' that reads DungeonFloors.stones, or a completed_flag backed by per-stone flags such as dungeon_stone_<n> written in activate_stone(). Evaluate it on accept and on load. As a backstop, add a quest-abandon action for non-story quests.
findings.verification: confirmed: dungeon_floors.gd:220-226 emits dungeon_runestone_activated only when `first` is true. `stones` is only cleared on a new game (line 56), not by _clear_day (74-79), and it is saved (278/289). Stones are on floors 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 only (dungeon.lua lines 157/205/257/312/362; floors 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 have stone=false; max_floor 12). The other emitter, runestone_2d.gd:46, goes through the same activate_stone. rune_vandring.lua: rune_9 has min_level 9 (matched as payload.level >= n, quest_manager.gd:913-915), no completed_flag, and is_available returns true. Fru Ugle offers it whenever it is offerable (appraiser_fru_ugle.lua:6,98). If floors 9 and 11 are both lit before the player accepts, the quest can never finish. skovlift_intro.light_rune has no min_level, so it sticks only if all five stones are already lit. The catch-up at quest_manager.gd:1002-1005 needs a completed_flag, which neither quest has. There is no abandon or cancel path (rg finds only climb_lane's _abandon).

findings.title: The opening does not establish the main premise: the mother line is an unsigned P.S. after the king's signed letter, and Esc skips it
evidence: lua/dialogue/fairy_king.lua:9-16 intro page = DLG_KING_LETTER then FM_OPENING_LEAD, both shown under the speaker name 'Fekongen'
localization/dialogue.csv:21 DLG_KING_LETTER ends "…Kærlig hilsen Fekongen." and says "Følg broen til dit nye hjem" although Pip delivers it at the farm

findings.description: The GM-06 fix landed as a single line attached after the king has already signed off ('Kærlig hilsen Fekongen'). It is shown with his name, and it tells the player what they feel ('Du leder også efter din mor') instead of showing a loss. For animal, fairy and hobbit heroes this means the lottery king somehow knows about a private search, and that winning a farm right above the forest where Mum disappeared is pure coincidence. Only ghost heroes get a reason, because Dyne rigged the lottery (ghostfamily.csv:112-113). Pressing Esc during Pip's greeting skips the letter altogether. After that, nothing before the garden says the hero has a missing mother: the Hoppe offer is a neighbourly gardening request, and the journal tab 'Mors spor' assumes the premise. The letter also says 'Følg broen til dit nye hjem' while the player is already standing at that home.
findings.player_impact: The main motivation is easy to miss or reads as a non sequitur. Children who skip or rush the opening meet 'Mors spor' and 'leder efter spor efter mor' with no setup, which weakens every later beat.
findings.recommendation: Move the premise out of the king's letter into a short moment that belongs to the hero: for example a second line from Pip ('Der var også et gammelt brev… din mor?') or a keepsake in the starting backpack (a photo or Mum's seed tin lid). Make it survive Esc by having the skip path whisper it, or by showing FM_OPENING_LEAD as a one-time notification. Change DLG_KING_LETTER to 'Velkommen til dit nye hjem'. Add one line to QUEST_SECRET_GARDEN_OFFER tying the garden to Mum. Update ghost_lines.gd:101 to include FM_OPENING_LEAD.

findings.title: The mystery gives away its central 'why' in the first letter, and later chapters repeat it
evidence: localization/secret_garden.csv:38 SG_SCENE_READ_LETTER (clue 1, day 2): "Jeg satte en lygte ved stien under liften. Så kunne de andre finde hjem."

localization/forest_mother.csv:39 FM_E_LIFT_RECORD_TEXT (S02 journal): "Hun tog Skovliften ned for at kortlægge en vej hjem for andre." though Oak's spoken line (secret_garden.csv:62) only says "Jeg ved ikke, hvor hun gik hen bagefter"

forest_mother.csv:43 (S03) "Hun tegnede en vej ud af skoven"; :45 "et kort også skal vise vej for dem, skoven ikke vil slippe"; :51 (S04) "Mor gjorde plads til mennesker, som ikke længere kunne finde deres hjem"; :53 "Mor tegnede udgange"; :63 (S06) "Jeg så mennesker komme ud…"
docs/design/DARK_FOREST_STORY_ADDENDUM.md chapter table: S01/S02 only establish handwriting and lantern; 'Mother's work was about getting them home' is the S05 discovery
findings.description: The addendum spreads the answers out: S01/S02 tell us who and where, S05 tells us why she went (bringing people home), S06 what she promised, S08 what happened. In the shipped text the 'why' is already in the first garden letter, and it is stated outright in the S02 journal entry, which puts words in Oak's mouth that he never says. From then on, five of the next six chapters each repeat 'she made a way home for others'. Only the role/name idea (S05/S07) and her death (S08) are new. The story has very little build-up in the middle, and the journal claims more certainty than its own 'witness' and 'seen' labels allow.
findings.player_impact: From floor 1 to floor 11 the player mostly re-reads one idea. That flattens S03 to S06 and makes the 'Huset der husker' and 'Navne mellem rødderne' discoveries feel like repeats rather than reveals.
findings.recommendation: Make the letter personal and puzzling, for example 'Jeg satte en lygte ved stien under liften. Jeg kommer hjem, når den sidste har fundet vej.' (who is 'den sidste'?). Limit FM_E_LIFT_RECORD_TEXT to what Oak saw ('kort, lygte, opmålingsgrej; hun skrev ingen returtid'). Then give each chapter one new fact: S03 she charted paths no one else could see; S04 she sheltered travellers and who they were; S05 that the wood swaps names for roles; S06 the promise and its cost. Keep the 'routes home' idea as the S05 reveal it was designed to be.
findings.verification: confirmed: secret_garden.csv:38 (letter: '…Så kunne de andre finde hjem.') and forest_mother.csv:39 (FM_E_LIFT_RECORD_TEXT '…for at kortlægge en vej hjem for andre') are as quoted. Oak's actual line (SG_TALK_ASK_OAK / SG_RECALL_GUARD_OAK, secret_garden.csv:62-63) only says she took a map and lantern down and 'Jeg ved ikke, hvor hun gik hen bagefter'. The 'routes home for others' idea recurs in S03 (:43, :45), S04 (:51, :53), S05 (:57, Iva: 'før hun viste mig vejen hjem'), S06 (:59, :63) and S08 (:67). In the addendum (DARK_FOREST_STORY_ADDENDUM.md:50-57), S01/S02 establish handwriting, lantern and tools, and 'Mother's work was about getting them home' is the S05 discovery. Front-loading and repetition are accurately described.

findings.title: The finale promises 'give her her own name back', but the player never acts and never learns the name; the refusal is narrated before the button
evidence: localization/forest_mother.csv:30 FM_CHAPTER_S08_DESC "…giv hende hendes eget navn tilbage, og bær frøene hjem"
forest_mother.csv:72 FM_FINAL_BARGAIN already says "Du lægger brevet over titlen og følger mors egen underskrift" before any choice
scripts/world2d/story/mother_evidence_marker.gd:108-110,139,143 the finale's only choices are FM_REFUSE_ROLE or Farvel
scripts/world2d/story/mother_story.gd:57-62 own_name_restored is set automatically when the account is recorded
forest_mother.csv:121-125 (S05) the Iva frame is an actual choice: Iva / Gæsten / Vejholderen
localization/secret_garden.csv:62 Oak: "Her står hendes navn." The name is never shown anywhere in the copy
findings.description: S05 teaches a clear mechanic: the frame names a role, the player picks the person's real name, and the word visibly changes on the frame (_name_label in mother_evidence_marker.gd). The finale is about the same idea, the wood calling Mum 'Vejholderen', but does not reuse it. 'Restoring her own name' is a flag set behind the scenes. The bargain text already describes the refusal before the player clicks (prior S-I, still open). Her name exists in Oak's lift book on day 2, yet the game never tells it to us. So 'giv hende hendes eget navn tilbage' asks for something the player cannot know and cannot do.
findings.player_impact: The emotional climax is a one-button confirmation of something already narrated. The best set-up in the story (Iva's frame) gets no payoff at the moment it matters most.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the S05 work at the frame on floor 12. Show 'Vejholderen' on the frame and offer the choices 'Vejholderen' / 'Mor' / '[the name from Oak's record]' (or her signature drawn as a glyph), with the same gentle retry as FM_WORK_NAME_RETRY. Only after the correct pick, swap the label and show FM_REFUSE_ROLE. Move 'Du lægger brevet over titlen…' out of FM_FINAL_BARGAIN so it plays after the click. If Mum's name is meant to stay secret, change S08_DESC to 'giv hende hendes egen underskrift tilbage' and make the signature something the player can see.
findings.prior_ref: S-I (mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18) bargain narrates the refusal before the click is still open
findings.verification: confirmed: FM_CHAPTER_S08_DESC (forest_mother.csv:30) is as quoted. FM_FINAL_BARGAIN (:72) narrates 'Du lægger brevet over titlen og følger mors egen underskrift' as page text before the choice; prior S-I is still open. mother_evidence_marker.gd:139-143: the only choices for mother_fate are FM_REFUSE_ROLE and REL_TALK_GOODBYE. mother_story.gd:57-62 sets own_name_restored and role_refused automatically on record. The S05 frame is an interactive pick (FM_WORK_NAME Iva/Gæsten/Vejholderen, the RETRY row, and _name_label swapped in refresh() at marker line 91). Mum's name is never shown: Oak says only 'Her står hendes navn'. Small correction: the player does click a refusal line ('Hendes liv var hendes…'), so 'never acts' means only a one-click confirm. The shipped copy elsewhere frames the motif as her 'underskrift' (FM_E_LAST_JOURNEY_TEXT :65, FM_FINAL_TRUTH :71, FM_E_MOTHER_FATE_TEXT :67 'Vi gav hende hendes egen underskrift tilbage'), so S08_DESC's 'navn' is also inconsistent with the game's own wording. The finding's fallback recommendation fits that.
