rg 'forest_mother|legacy_home|mother_fate' scripts outside world2d/story and ui/story finds nothing: no audio, festival, mail or event reacts; there is no credits or epilogue at all
findings.description: After 8 chapters, 3 bosses and the death of the hero's mother, the ending is a dialogue page on floor 12, a walk home, a 'plant' button and three flower sprites. The chapters give no keepsake. Mum's lantern or seed tin never becomes an item, furniture piece or wearable, even though the pitch is built around rare and unique keepsakes. Hoppe and Brumme, who own and rebuilt the garden where her seeds are planted, never mention it. Neither do the mayor or the fairy king. No music cue, gathering, letter or 'Mors have' sign marks the moment. The journal shows an empty reward header on every chapter.
findings.player_impact: The game's emotional climax ends quietly and alone. Children get no lasting token of the story, and the town does not seem to notice.
findings.recommendation: Add a small authored homecoming. On the morning after legacy_home, Hoppe, Brumme, Pip and the Natlys family are at the garden for a one-page scene, plus one line each in their normal dialogue. Give S08 a unique keepsake (for example 'Mors lygte' as a unique/legendary furniture piece or lantern skin, or the seed tin as a placeable). Turn the planted spot into a persistent 'Mors bed' that blooms every season. Play a music sting on forest_mother_evidence id=legacy_home. Hide the journal's reward header when a quest has no rewards.

Post-legacy lines exist only for MotherStory.HELPERS (mother_story.gd:31,119). Hoppe and Brumme are in SecretGardenStory.HELPERS, but their recall lines (SG_RECALL_*) are not legacy-aware. gardener_hoppe.lua reads only weather/swap_day/total_day, carpenter_brumme.lua reads only quest_active_fix_roof and brumme_at_stall, and Lyra and the king have no story branches. findings.title: The story and the home/castle progression never meet; the fairy king has no story role and the de-facto ending is a furniture checklist
evidence: lua/dialogue/fairy_king.lua:9-16 the king's only story line is the opening letter; his other branches are moonstone_crown and slotsdroemmen
lua/quests/slotsdroemmen.lua:8-41 the final quest = 6 unique/legendary furniture + hygge 5 + feast + talk to the king; QUEST_SLOTSDROEMMEN_DESC (features_quests.csv:12) has no reference to the story
lua/data/home_tiers.lua:204,282,319,357 the home tier gates are side quests (crystal_cave, snurresvampen, moonstone_crown) plus friendship; none uses forest_mother_* or secret_garden
scripts/world2d/story/mother_story.gd:22-29 chapters have no day or season gating; they advance only with evidence and bosses on floors 4/8/12
findings.description: The pitch has two big lines: the lottery farm in Trætoppen that grows to a castle, and the forest. They run separately. The mother story can finish within a few game weeks of combat. Home tier 10 and slotsdroemmen need about 74k gold and hygge 4/5 and arrive around day 30 to 60 or later. That leaves a long stretch after the climax with no story at all. The final quest is a furniture checklist set by a king who never acknowledges the hero's search, though his letter mentions it. No home tier or castle beat refers to the garden, the seeds or Mum. With no day gating, a strong player can also burn through the whole emotional arc in the first week.
findings.player_impact: The game has two separate endings: a moving one that comes early, and a long tail that ends on 'place 6 treasures'. The lottery premise is never paid off.
findings.recommendation: Tie the two together lightly. Make slotsdroemmen's feast a gathering in Mum's memory, or require the planted 'Mors bed' or mother keepsake as one of the six treasures. Give the king a line after mother_fate that answers the lottery (for example 'Lotteriet vælger ikke tilfældigt, hvem der skal have et hjem…' while keeping it genuine per the addendum). Consider soft pacing: Natteblik or Fru Ugle 'need a night to think' between S05 and S06 and between S07 and S08. Optionally add one home tier perk that only exists after the garden (for example a moonflower bed at the castle).
findings.verification: partly: The structural claims hold. fairy_king.lua has no story branches beyond the intro page. slotsdroemmen.lua objectives are 6 unique/legendary furniture + hygge 5 + festival_held + talk to the king, and QUEST_SLOTSDROEMMEN_DESC (features_quests.csv:12) has no story link. Home tier gates (home_tiers.lua:204, 282, 319, and 356-357, where tier 10 needs friendship mayor_lyra 8 / fairy_king 2 and hygge 4) never reference forest_mother or secret_garden. Mother chapters S03-S08 are gated only by evidence and boss flags (mother_story.gd:22-29, 73-87); the secret garden has a bloom/watering wait. Tier gold indeed sums to 74,000. The pacing figure is wrong: docs/features/BALANCE.md:10,28-29,51 models the finished castle at about day 185 (dedicated), 345 (typical) or 919 (casual), not 'day 30 to 60'. The post-climax gap with no story is therefore much longer than stated, which strengthens the argument but corrects the fact.

findings.description: The style guide's guide quest and the owner's lost-cat example opens in the city with paw prints by the farm bridge. It can only be finished on dungeon floor 5 (Dybe Bregner), which is past the first boss (Snurresvampen, floor 4). The journal says only 'find him in Mørkeskoven' and lists the location as ZONE_CITY. A child who accepts it on day 1 will search floors 1-4 and never find him. The 'ask the neighbours' step also gives no clue, because none of the four neighbours mentions the cat.
findings.player_impact: The friendliest early quest becomes the hardest one. A young player spends a day searching shallow floors with no success and is told nothing about why. Morfar Mis also stays unbefriendable for up to 60 days.
findings.recommendation: Move the Mis anchor in lua/config/dungeon.lua from floor 5 to floor 1 or 2 (floor 2's spots, place = 'nook'), keeping mis_hjoerne's loot spot with it, or add requires_zone plus a floor hint to OBJ_LOST_CAT_FIND_CAT ('… i Skovbrynet'). Add a quest_active_lost_cat line to the dialogues of baker_maja, merchant_pip, mayor_lyra and farmer_rosa that points to the bridge ('Jeg så ham ved broen med en sardin!'), so the ask step gives real clues.
findings.dim: Side quests, NPC writing, cast consistency
findings.verification: partly: Every fact checks out. lua/config/dungeon.lua:218-221 has the only cat_morfar_mis anchor, on floor 5 (n=5, band dybe_bregner). Floor 4 (lines 174-196) has boss='snurresvamp', and the stairs on a boss floor are sealed until the dg_boss_clear flag is set (dungeon_export.gd:105-106, dungeon_verify.gd:141-143). lost_cat.lua meta (lines 63-70) has no requires_zone, unlike crystal_cave, dark_forest_mining, rare_mushroom_hunt and others, and location = ZONE_CITY. OBJ_LOST_CAT_FIND_CAT (quests.csv:70) gives no floor hint, and neither does Pippin's reminder DLG_PIPPIN_REMIND ('Prøv at spørge naboerne. Mis holder også af broen', dialogue.csv:44). The only player-visible floor hint is the furniture catalog hint ITEM_CHAIR_STUMP_HINT 'Morfar Mis sad her i Dybe Bregner'. The ask_neighbours any_of list is only counted: no lost_cat branch exists in the Maja, Kløvermynte, Lyra or Rosa dialogues (rg finds no matches). Pippin offers the quest from day 1 (pippin_boegeknop.lua:11-16, routine in hyggebyen). Severity: the quest is never blocked. It finishes as soon as the player clears the floor-4 boss, which they do anyway on the main dungeon path. So this is a long, unexplained wait in a journal entry, not a broken beat. P2, not P1. | partly: Most of the evidence checks out against the worktree at f80e7aed. (1) lua/config/dungeon.lua:220: the only cat_morfar_mis anchor is on floor 5 (n=5, band dybe_bregner, place='nook'; dungeon_gen.gd:9 calls nooks 'secret'). Floor 4 (lines 174-179) has boss='snurresvamp' and hulen=true. (2) The stairs down from floor 4 stay sealed until the boss is beaten: dungeon_verify.gd:136-144 checks this, and at runtime the boss_clear flag is reset in dungeon_floors.gd:183 and set only by _enemy_defeated/_restore_boss_flag (lines 243-261). Runestones (start_floors, line 214) only let you restart on floors you have already reached, so the first trip to floor 5 needs the floor-4 boss beaten. (3) lost_cat.lua:62-69 has no requires_zone/gate, location='ZONE_CITY', and Pippin offers it whenever the quest is not done (pippin_boegeknop.lua:11-16). (4) The hint text is vague. OBJ_LOST_CAT_FIND_CAT (quests.csv:70) says only 'i Mørkeskoven', and DLG_PIPPIN_REMIND (dialogue.csv:44) says 'spørg naboerne… broen'. The only text naming Dybe Bregner is a furniture hint (furniture.csv:55, ITEM_CHAIR_STUMP_HINT), not quest copy. (5) baker_maja/merchant_pip/mayor_lyra/farmer_rosa.lua have no cat or quest_active branch. ask_neighbours (lost_cat.lua:27-31) counts any conversation. Why only partly: this is a side quest, not main progression. There is no softlock: the cat can be found once the player beats the first boss, and Mis's befriend gate falls back to day 60 (citizens.lua:40). The claim that the player will 'never find him' is overstated. It is a real pacing/hint/UX problem (no floor or band hint, and the cat sits in a secret nook past a boss). That is P2, not P1.

findings.description: The greeting system runs on every NPC's first conversation of each day. All of its text is one sentence template with an NPC-specific noun swapped in. The same goes for biographies in the People book and topic answers. The heart events have personal prose, but all 10 share the same 8 choice buttons. The Mayor of Hyggebyen says 'Vi finder en plads til dig i Trætoppen' and closes with 'gør Trætoppen hjemlig', which mixes up the two towns. The owner wants a full social sim, but citizens speak in one voice. The template shows as soon as a player talks to two or three people.
findings.player_impact: Citizens feel like vending machines. 'Jeg tænkte netop på…' from every NPC every morning breaks the warm, characterful tone that the cast-v2 dialogue shows the team can write. It also undercuts gift hints, because every favourite thing 'reminds me of something nice'.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite SOC_<NPC>_GREET_H0-H3, BIO_1 and TOPIC_ANSWER_* in localization/social_talk.csv in each character's own voice. findings.verification: partly: The template claim holds, and a scan of every SOC_* key confirms it. GREET_H0 30/30, BIO 30/30 and TOPIC_ANSWER 30/30 non-ghost citizens match one sentence skeleton each, and GREET_H1 25/25, H2 10/10 and H3 10/10 do too. All 8 heart-event choice labels are reused exactly 10 times each (heart_events.csv). Two corrections. (1) The 'mixes up the two towns' claim is wrong: by the owner's own pitch, Hyggebyen is the shopping district INSIDE the treetop city Trætoppen, so 'plads til dig i Trætoppen' and 'gør Trætoppen hjemlig' from Hyggebyen residents is correct. (2) Each citizen has only one own GREET_H<band> key, and SocialTalk.pick (social_talk.gd:55-99) skips the last-used key. So on alternate days the greeting falls back to the SOC_ARCH_<arch>_GREET_H* pool, which has 3 skeletons, not only 'Kom, der er plads ved…' (social_arch.csv:70-81). On non-clear-weather or season-roll days the greeting comes from single shared SOC_ANY_WX_* or SOC_ANY_SEASON_* lines (1 key each). That makes the sameness worse, but the description should say so. The prior game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md:125 note (25 citizens share bark lines) exists, so the prior_ref is valid. Severity: this is copy quality in a system that works, so P2. P1 overstates it. | partly: The templating is real. In social_talk.csv:2-45 and 158-170, Lyra, Maja, Kløvermynte and Thorin share identical GREET_H0-H3, CHAT_H2-H10 and BIO_1 frames with only a noun or place swapped. TOPIC_ANSWER_* is word-for-word 'X minder mig om noget rart. Det er en af mine yndlingsting.' (lines 13, 15, 17, 34, 36, 38; it is also ungrammatical in English: 'The strawberries reminds'). BARK_1-3 are identical for every citizen. social_arch.csv: the 96 SOC_ARCH_*_GREET_H lines are one 3-frame x 4-suffix template per archetype. heart_events.csv: 8 distinct choice labels, each used exactly 10 times (counted). dialogue_bridge.gd:20-23 puts a GREET line in front of every first conversation of the day. Two corrections. (a) SocialTalk.pick (social_talk.gd:61-75) also mixes in birthday, festival, weather (60% roll) and season (20% roll) greetings from SOC_ANY_*/SOC_ARCH_*. These are shared generic lines, so they add some variety but no individual voice. (b) The town 'mix-up' claim is refuted. GLOSSARY.md:44 says 'Trætoppen is the settlement. Hyggebyen is its shopping district', so Hyldeblomst saying 'plads til dig i Trætoppen' and 'gør Trætoppen hjemlig' is correct. Severity: the social sim works (hearts, gifts, topics, heart events with personal prose, routines), so this is a copy/story quality gap, not a broken core system or a missing requirement. That makes it P2, not P1. There are 33 citizen rows in citizens.lua, not 30.

evidence: Objective summary of lua/quests/*.lua: animal_products, birthday_cake, cookie_delivery, crystal_cave, dark_forest_mining, fix_roof, flower_necklace, forest_patrol, ghostfam_garn, ghostfam_lygtemager, moonstone_crown, night_flower, rare_mushroom_hunt, supply_run, sword_upgrade and ugles_noegle are all 'item_gained have=true ×N then talk to giver' (16 of 26 non-spine quests)

Figurer v2 Brumme card: 'Løfter bjælkerne, når feerne skal have nyt tag'. lua/quests/fix_roof.lua has giver mayor_lyra, an E-press repair at a quest_spot and rewards friendship to baker_maja only; Brumme's only part is the flavour line DLG_BRUMME_ROOF (lua/dialogue/carpenter_brumme.lua:6-20)
lua/config/npcs.lua - carpenter_brumme, bathkeeper_sofus, mapseller_natteblik and beekeeper_birk have no quests_offered, and no quest names them as giver
Repeatables replay their story every few days: rare_mushroom_hunt (cooldown 4, 'Lilys lille ven er syg'), cookie_delivery (3, out of carrots again), supply_run (2), flower_necklace (4)
findings.description: The examples that work best (Pip's tour, Blund's hide-and-seek, Hoppe's swap) are social or systemic, but most side quests are 'gather N, hand in'. In the owner's roof-repair example the player gathers wood and moss and presses E on a marker. The bear carpenter whose sketch describes this exact job is not involved. Brumme, Sofus, Natteblik and Birk were added in Figurer v2 but have no side quests. The repeatable errands repeat one-off emergencies (a sick friend, an empty cupboard) indefinitely.
findings.player_impact: Fetch fatigue sets in by the second week. The new cast members feel like shopkeepers only. Repeating 'my friend is sick' every 4 days makes the story feel careless.
findings.recommendation: Make fix_roof a two-hander: deliver the goods to Brumme (dialogue_started npc=carpenter_brumme with needs, then he climbs up), give him friendship hearts, and put him in the reward. Give each of Brumme, Sofus, Natteblik and Birk one non-fetch quest: Birk a 'follow the bees' route, Sofus a bath-house invitation round, Natteblik a night map-marking of 3 spots. Reword repeatable OFFER/DESC keys so they suit repetition (QUEST_RARE_MUSHROOM_HUNT_*: Lily collecting glowing mushrooms for her lantern collection rather than medicine).

findings.title: No keyboard binding for tools or attacking: a keyboard-only player cannot do the first tutorial step or fight
evidence: project.godot:152 use_tool={...} and :158 attack={...}: only InputEventMouseButton (left) and InputEventJoypadButton (X), no InputEventKey (decoded the whole [input] section)
tests/tools/input_contract.gd:33-34 pins "use_tool": {"mouse": [MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT], "joy": [JOY_BUTTON_X]} and the same for attack, so the missing key is locked in by a test
scripts/world2d/player_2d.gd:194-201: farming (use_selected) and combat.request(&"slash") are reached only through these two actions
localization/farm_tutorial.csv:6 DLG_FARMINTRO_PIP_BYE_1 'Vælg den med %s, og brug %s på jorden' resolves to 'Venstre klik' on keyboard (ui_hints.gd glyph falls back to the mouse)
docs/design/UI_NAVIGATION.md §3.2 table row `use_tool` / `attack` = LMB | X
docs/PLAYING.md:61 claims 'Keyboard and controller attacks retain the precise movement direction', but no keyboard attack exists
findings.description: Every other world action has a key (E, Space, Q, R, F, 1-8). Using the selected tool (hoe, can, seeds, axe, pickaxe, scythe, bin-adjacent tools) and attacking in Mørkeskoven are bound only to the left mouse button and gamepad X. The owner requires full keyboard play. The opening ends with Pip's instruction to use the hoe, which a keyboard-only player cannot follow. The same block stops the whole farming loop and all combat.
findings.player_impact: A child playing on keyboard alone (laptop without a mouse, or a player who prefers keys) gets stuck on the very first instruction of the game and can never farm or fight.
findings.recommendation: Add a physical key to both actions in project.godot, for example K or J-adjacent. A natural fit is to reuse X, which already does pickup_item only in Indretning, plus Enter as a fallback. Update input_contract.gd:33-34 and the cross-action table at :111-113, UI_NAVIGATION.md §3.2, and the PLAYING.md controls table. The UiHints glyphs will then show the key automatically.
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-verified at HEAD f80e7aed in the worktree. project.godot:152-163: use_tool and attack each have only InputEventMouseButton button_index 1 and InputEventJoypadButton 2. There is no InputEventKey on either. tests/tools/input_contract.gd:33-34 pins this, and :111 lists LMB as shared by attack and use_tool. player_2d.gd:194-201: hoeing, watering and planting go only through use_tool -> use_selected(), and slash goes only through attack. try_interact (player_2d.gd:324-329) on E/Enter only harvests READY cells, so it cannot hoe, water or plant. UI_NAVIGATION.md:161 and :877 document LMB/X only. The uncommitted main-checkout diff adds only `map` (M), not a tool or attack key. No prior review raises this. Small nuance: PLAYING.md:61 'Keyboard and controller attacks retain the precise movement direction' is better read as aiming with keyboard movement than as a claim that a key attack exists. The controls table at PLAYING.md:14 honestly says 'Left mouse button'. The accessibility finding stands as stated. | partly: The facts hold in the worktree (f80e7aed). project.godot binds use_tool and attack only to InputEventMouseButton button_index 1 and InputEventJoypadButton 2, with no InputEventKey. tests/tools/input_contract.gd:33-34 pins exactly that. player_2d.gd:194-201 reaches use_selected()/combat.request(&"slash") only through those actions. No runtime rebinding exists: rg finds no action_add_event in scripts/, and ui_hints.gd:4 only mentions rebinding 'in a later version'. Two claims are weaker than stated. (1) Some keyboard paths exist. try_interact (E/Enter) harvests READY crops (player_2d.gd:327-328). resource_node_2d.gd:93-95 calls player.use_selected() on E when the matching axe/pickaxe is selected. Weapon combat goes through use_selected's 'weapon' branch -> combat.swing (about player_2d.gd:388-389). Even with a mouse, LMB in an action area is consumed by the use_tool elif before the attack elif is reached. So the hoe, watering can, seeds, scythe and weapon swing still need LMB or pad X, and a mouse-free player cannot till or fight. (2) Mouse use is a documented, deliberate design choice, not an oversight. See UI_NAVIGATION.md:161, :179 ('Shared bindings are intentional... LMB use_tool+attack'), :877 and PLAYING.md:14. The 'keyboard-only flow' acceptance spec (UI_NAVIGATION.md:756) covers menus/shop/journal/dialogue, not farming. On the macOS/Windows release targets a mouse is always there, so this is not a blocker: a keyboard+mouse or gamepad player can do every step. It is a real accessibility and owner-requirement gap ('full keyboard play'). PLAYING.md:61 ('Keyboard ... attacks retain the precise movement direction') is inaccurate. I rate it P2. Raise it to P1 only if the owner means mouse-free gameplay rather than keyboard-navigable UI.

evidence: lua/farm/farm_tutorial.lua:32 the bin hint fires on crop_harvested; :37 expand needs gold>=800 and day>=3
lua/quests/forste_dage.lua:6-12: harvest (target 1) is the natural LAST objective; mail is possible from day 2, while turnips need 4 watered days (game_balance turnip stages=4)
scripts/farm/steading/tutorial/tutorial_hints.gd:30-36: hints only run while forste_dage is active, and on its completion tut_done=1 and queued.clear()

scripts/autoload/quest_manager.gd:157 QuestManager (an autoload) connects crop_harvested before TutorialHints (attached in world _ready, tutorial_hints.gd:23); completion is synchronous (quest_manager.gd:704-708 _check_completion -> complete_quest)
tests/sections/farm_first_morning.gd:150-163 tests the reverse order (harvest emitted before day-2 mail), so the natural order is never exercised
docs/PLAYING.md:31 'Follow the first-days quests to learn planting, watering, harvesting and shipping.'
findings.description: In the normal order (read the mail on day 2, first harvest about day 5), the harvest that triggers the bin hint also completes forste_dage. That turns the hint system off before the hint can be queued or shown. The expand hint has the same window problem: it needs 800 g while the quest is still running, and rewards push gold past 800 only on completion. The core money action, putting crops in the salgskasse, is not taught anywhere else.
findings.player_impact: A child harvests the first turnips, never learns that the bin exists or that it pays the next morning, and may sell nothing, or try to sell only through shops.
findings.recommendation:
Use one of these three:
- Add a `ship` objective (on = game_event shipped / item_shipped, target 1) to forste_dage after harvest, so the quest itself teaches the bin.

findings.title: All 40 heart scenes come from one template; choices have no real consequences, skipping picks the best option, and 10-heart points are always lost
evidence: tools/social/content/build_hearts.py:14-19 hard-codes CHOICES per heart level for every NPC: 4 'Vis mig det hele.'/'Lad os begynde her.', 6 'Vi gør det sammen.'/'Vis mig dit trick.', 8 'Jeg bliver lidt endnu.'/'Det tager jeg med mig.', 10 'Her er også plads til dig.'/'Vi mødes igen snart.'

build_hearts.py:31 asserts exactly 5 or 3 lines per scene; :36 the same when string for all; :38-48 a fixed step list with options {id='stay',points=20},{id='remember',points=10}; :49 always rewards {points=40}
lua/events/hearts/*.lua: after swapping NPC names, items and marks, all 10 files normalise to the same md5 (c16e1e93…). No scene has a walk, flag, reply_key, time, sfx, clip or a second speaker.
scripts/social/events/event_runner.gd:65 and :76: on skip the choice defaults to choices[0], which is always the +20 'stay' option, so skipping earns the maximum

event_runner.gd:108-111: _choice reads only points/flag/reply_key. No code reads the option ids 'stay'/'remember', and no heart scene writes a flag. Nothing else consumes completion either: no quest uses heart_event_finished, and only people.gd:208 shows a count.

social_manager.gd:276-278 (hearts = floor(p/100), cap 10) and :325-328 (gained = min(delta, cap - before); returns at 0): every _h10 scene requires hearts:<npc>:10, i.e. 1000 points = cap, so its 40 + 20/10 points are always discarded
findings.description: The scenes are 'authored' only at the level of line text. Structure, beat order, choice placement, choice labels, point values and rewards are identical for all 10 citizens and set in the generator. The two options per scene differ only by 10 points. The NPC's next line is the same whichever option is picked, because there is no reply_key. No flag is set and nothing downstream reads the choice. Skipping always applies the better option. At 10 hearts the points are discarded because the player is already at the cap, so the climactic scene's choice has literally zero mechanical or narrative effect.
findings.player_impact: Players soon learn that choices do not matter and that skipping is optimal. After two or three citizens the scenes feel interchangeable. The 'full social sim' promise is undercut at its emotional peak.
findings.recommendation: Extend hearts.json so each scene can author its own choices (per-NPC text_key and a reply_key line per option) and an optional flag, e.g. flag='heart_maja_h6_trick'. Have 'build_hearts.py' stop forcing CHOICES, the line counts (:31) and the fixed step list. Read at least some flags back: a later scene step 'when=flag:…', a GREET line variant, or a social_topics entry. Make skip apply a neutral option (add a 'skip_option' or use the lowest-points option) rather than choices[0]. For _h10, replace points with a non-point payoff (see the payoff finding), or let the choice set a flag that a later line or the relationship flow reads.
findings.dim: Heart-event scenes and their runner: content, triggers, choices and payoff (10 NPCs, about 4,000 Lua lines, never read)
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-verified in the worktree (f80e7aed). `build_hearts.py --check` passes, so the lua/events/hearts files are exactly what the generator emits. CHOICES are hard-coded at :14-19. The line counts are asserted at :30 (cited as :31). The `when` string is built at :35. Options are {stay,20}/{remember,10} at :48, and rewards are {points=40} at :53. In event_runner.gd, :65 and :76 default to choices[0] when skipping. :108-111 `_choice` reads only points and flag; reply_key is read only at :71, and no heart option has one. A grep for 'stay'/'remember' in scripts finds nothing that consumes the option ids. heart_event_finished is supported by quest_manager.gd:73, but the only Lua mention is a comment (lost_cat.lua:15); no quest uses it. In social_manager.gd, hearts = min(floor(p/100), 10) and add_points computes gained = min(delta, 1000 - before) and returns early at 0. Because _h10 needs hearts:<npc>:10, p is already 1000, so the 40 + 20/10 points are discarded. One addition: `_commit` caps event points at 100 per NPC (event_runner.gd ~:233), and 60 stays under that cap. The scene gift is still granted at 10 hearts, so only the choice and the points are without effect.

findings.description: The owner asked for marriage-style relationships. The mechanics exist: tokens, consent, stage rs 1-3, wedding festival, chores. The story backing is minimal. Becoming heartfriends shows two lines, and for three of the seven tier-A candidates those lines are archetype filler shared with background NPCs. findings.title: A Lua content or balance change makes saves fail to load: the validators check records against the live catalogue, and the auto slot has no backup
evidence: scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:702-707 - the whole payload is rejected as 'invalid' if FarmGrid.validate_dict(world.farm / greenhouse_farm) or FarmEquipment.validate_placed(world.placed) fails
scripts/world2d/farm_grid.gd:372 - `if crop != "" and not definitions.has(crop): return false` (crop ids come from lua/config/game_balance.lua via crop_definitions(), line 38-39)

scripts/world2d/farm_grid.gd:376 - a plot marked regrowing whose crop now has regrow_days <= 0 rejects the save (lua/config/game_balance.lua:53-54 strawberry/glow_berry regrow_days = 4 is a balance knob)
scripts/farm/farm_equipment.gd:120 and :135 - a placed item whose def no longer has placeable="farm", or a batch whose crop or output_prefix changed, rejects the save
scripts/farm/animal_husbandry.gd:826, 844, 850-853 - an unknown species or building_type, or a building tier above 1+upgrades.size(), rejects the save

scripts/dungeon/floors/dungeon_floors.gd:316 - deepest and floor are hard-capped at 12 (`_whole(data.get("deepest",0),0,12)`), while max_floor is data (lua/config/dungeon.lua:15). Raising max_floor makes every save past floor 12 invalid, even in the same build
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:196-198 and 389-401 - the auto slot has no .bak, so 'corrupt' means no save at all; Continue skips it (get_latest_slot 445-456)

Contrast: social_manager.gd:1385-1398 keeps unknown NPCs in an orphans bucket (pinned by tests/sections/social.gd:1332-1351); no test pins content drift for crops, machines, animals or the dungeon floor cap
findings.description: Several pure validators treat 'not in the current Lua catalogue' as file damage. Validation is slot-wide, so one plot, machine or animal record that refers to renamed or retuned content flags the whole slot as corrupt. The .bak usually has the same record, so it fails too. The game never makes a manual save on its own (current_slot starts as NO_SLOT), so a player who relies on Continue has only the backup-less auto slot. This is latent today but very likely to fire as content is renamed and balance is retuned in Lua between builds.
findings.player_impact: After an update that renames or retunes a crop, animal, building upgrade or farm machine, or raises the dungeon floor cap, the save shows as 'Beskadiget' and Continue skips it or finds nothing. Every bit of progress is lost with no way to recover it.
findings.recommendation: Keep validate_dict to structural and type checks only. Move catalogue checks into from_dict as repairs with push_warning, as SocialManager does. FarmGrid.from_dict: an unknown crop becomes a TILLED plot, and regrowing is cleared when regrow_days is 0. FarmEquipment: drop an unknown placed piece and refund it to the backpack; a bad batch refunds its input crop. AnimalHusbandry: keep unknown species and buildings in an orphans dict and clamp tier to max_tier. dungeon_floors.gd:316: use int(cfg.max_floor) instead of 12. Add a test such as save.survives_content_drift that renames a crop, an animal species and a machine in a fixture config and asserts load_game succeeds.
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: partly: The mechanism is accurate, and I re-read every cited line. validate_payload (save_manager.gd:682-707) rejects the whole payload with 'invalid' when a section's validate_dict, FarmGrid.validate_dict (world.farm and greenhouse_farm) or FarmEquipment.validate_placed fails. farm_grid.gd:372 rejects an unknown crop and :376 rejects regrowing when regrow_days <= 0. farm_equipment.gd:120 requires placeable=='farm', and :135 requires the batch crop and output_prefix to match. animal_husbandry.gd:826/844/850-853 rejects an unknown species or building_type and a tier above 1+upgrades.size(). dungeon_floors.gd:316/322 hard-code 12, while _valid_floor (line 71) reads cfg.max_floor, so the two disagree inside the same file. The auto slot has no backup (backup_path returns "" at 196-198). The only manual save path is save_load_ui.gd:145; every other caller uses autosave(). get_latest_slot (445-456) skips corrupt slots. Wardrobe and furniture from_dict quietly drop unknown ids (furniture_manager.gd:246 FurnitureCatalog.contains, and wardrobe slot_of), and SocialManager uses orphans. So the inconsistency is real. Small citation error: SocialManager is scripts/social/social_manager.gd:1386-1392, not under autoload. Severity: this is latent. Nothing in the current content triggers it. The project also has a stable-id convention (lua/config/npcs.lua:7 'Ids are STABLE (D11)'; dungeon_v2_workpackages 'ids are stable'), which makes renames less likely than 'very likely' suggests. Retuning (regrow_days to 0, fewer upgrade tiers, a removed placeable flag, a higher max_floor) is still possible. Today nothing is broken; it is a future-update data-loss risk, so P2 rather than P1. | partly: I checked every mechanism the finding cites, and each one is accurate. save_manager.gd:702-707 rejects the whole payload when FarmGrid.validate_dict fails (on farm or greenhouse_farm) or FarmEquipment.validate_placed fails. Registered and core sections are also checked through node.validate_dict at :695. farm_grid.gd:372 returns false when a crop is not found in crop_definitions(), which is read live from GameData.cfg('crops'). farm_grid.gd:376 indexes definitions[crop].regrow_days for a plot marked regrowing. farm_equipment.gd:120 requires placeable=='farm', and :135 requires batch.output == output_prefix + input with the input crop still defined. animal_husbandry.gd:826/844/850-853 rejects an unknown species or building_type and a tier above 1+upgrades.size(). The dungeon section is registered at loot_service.gd:980. dungeon_floors.gd:316 hard-codes deepest/floor <= 12 and :324 hard-codes stones/seen/reveal <= 12, while _valid_floor at :70-71 reads cfg max_floor. backup_path returns '' for AUTO_SLOT (save_manager.gd:196-198). inspect_slot then reports 'corrupt' (:396-401), and get_latest_slot skips the slot (:445-456). current_slot starts as NO_SLOT (:100/166). Every automatic save path I found (world_2d.gd:786, runestone, festival, event_runner, etc.) calls autosave(); only save_load_ui.gd:145 writes a manual slot. Why I lowered it from P1: nothing fails in the current build. Lua is bundled with the build, so a save can only go stale when a later build renames or removes content or retunes regrow_days, upgrades or max_floor, without adding a step to the existing _migrate() chain (save_manager.gd:717+). That makes it a latent robustness and tech-debt gap that developers can control, not a broken core loop today. The impact when it does fire is severe: the save is silently lost and Continue skips it. Fail-soft loading (dropping or orphaning unknown records the way social_manager does) or a content-drift test would close it. A fair rating is P2, or P1 only if content renames between builds are planned before release.

findings.title: The day-end autosave after a 02:00 pass-out saves the collapse moment (02:00, the spot where the player fell), not the 06:00 wake-up at home
evidence: scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:527-531 - _roll_day: day_ended.emit, then _step_calendar, _announce_new_day, then game_event midnight_passed (the hour is left at the restart hour 02:00)
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:262-274 - day_ended queues _run_queued_autosave.call_deferred(), which runs at the end of the same frame

scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd:687-695 and 698-706 - midnight_passed starts _sleep_sequence(true), which awaits a 0.7 s fade before GameManager.sleep_until_morning() and _enter(_wake_area()); the deferred autosave has already run by then
scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:502-509 - sleep_until_morning with hour < wake_hour only sets hour=6; no end_day, so no day_ended and no corrected autosave
scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:598 - from_dict keeps hour 2 (clamped to day_roll_restart_hour()..25), so a load resumes at 02:00
Contrast: the defeat path autosaves after the wake-up (world_2d.gd:785-786), and bed sleep sets hour=6 synchronously in end_day (game_manager.gd:489-495) before the deferred save runs
findings.description: At a pass-out, advance_time rolls the day and the deferred day-end autosave writes the auto slot in that same frame. That is before the pass-out sequence moves the player home and sets the clock to 06:00, and nothing autosaves after the wake-up. Until the 5-minute timer or a pause-menu quit writes again, the auto slot holds day N+1 at 02:00 with the player standing where they collapsed. Combined with the known window-close-without-save issue, Continue often restores exactly this snapshot.
findings.player_impact: After passing out and closing the game, Continue starts at 02:00 in town or the forest instead of waking at home. It also hands out 4 free night hours (02:00-06:00) before the next pass-out, and the 'wake at home' rule is skipped.
findings.recommendation: Autosave after the wake-up instead of on the roll. One option: in world_2d._sleep_sequence, after _restore_player(), call SaveManager.autosave() when passed_out, as the defeat path does at 785-786. Another: in SaveManager._on_day_ended, skip the deferred save when GameManager.hour < day_start_hour() and let the world save once sleeping is false. Add a check such as clock26.pass_out_autosave_wakes_at_home: advance from 01:59 past 02:00, wait for the sequence, then assert the auto slot has hour 6 and area == wake_area.
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: confirmed: Re-traced the code. advance_time (game_manager.gd:463-480) sets hour to the restart hour and calls _roll_day (527-531): day_ended, then _step_calendar, _announce_new_day and midnight_passed. After that the hour settles at about 2 (day_end_hour=26 in game_balance.lua:86). SaveManager._on_day_ended (262-267) queues a call_deferred autosave, which runs at the end of that frame. world_2d._on_game_event (687-695) starts _sleep_sequence(true) (698+), which awaits a 0.7 s tween before sleep_until_morning(). That sets hour=6 with no day_ended (502-509) and no autosave, and then the player is moved home with _enter(_wake_area()). No other autosave follows: the next is the 300 s timer (save_manager.gd:72, 159) or a pause-menu quit (pause_menu.gd:110). world.to_dict (859-874) saves the current area and player_pos. GameManager.from_dict (598) clamps the hour to 2..25, so a load resumes at 02:00 on day N+1 at the collapse spot. The defeat path does autosave after the wake-up (world_2d.gd:785-786). Accurate as stated.

localization/ghostfamily.csv:63-64, 80-81, 97-98 - the CHAT_4/CHAT_8 beats of Gnist, Silke and Blund (Blund's 'kat, der nyser' setup for the Bu scene)

findings.description: The addendum's lean social layer (6.3) carries the family's arc through heart-gated chat beats and barks. The runtime only ever picks FIRST and GREET lines, so no SOC_<NPC>_CHAT_* or *_BARK_* row is shown, for the family or any other citizen (social_talk.csv has 80 CHAT rows). For the family this removes the middle of every arc: Dyne's tier-A 'story of the family' ladder (age, who Silke and Gnist are, why the family left the forest, 'du lyser', the 10-heart line), Gnist's line about the unsold lantern that sets up his h4 scene, Blund's line about practising 'bu' that sets up the h8 'Bu' scene and the welcome-evening joke, and all signature barks. Gnist, Silke and Blund are tier B with no 10-heart content, so their arcs end at the 8-heart scene.
findings.player_impact: Relationships with the family jump from greetings straight to scenes. Players never learn the family's basic facts (that Silke is Dyne's daughter and Gnist her husband, why they live in the Gæstehytten), and later scenes allude to setups the player never saw. Two recorded voice lines are wasted.
findings.recommendation: Add a CHAT slot to SocialTalk.pick (families own+"CHAT_H<n>" plus the family's "CHAT_<n>" style, i.e. normalise the keys: the family uses SOC_GHOSTFAM_DYNE_CHAT_2_1, others SOC_<NPC>_CHAT_H2_1). Show the highest unseen beat <= hearts once per week, either as a second line of the weekly first conversation or as a 'Snak' choice in DialogueBridge.decorate. Surface barks as a short-lived world bubble when the player passes within about 200 px (Npc2D._update_bubble already has the label). Rename the ghostfam CHAT keys to the _H<n> convention so one rule covers all citizens.

findings.title: Hidden Blund's talk prompt appears outside the find radius, and pressing E then silently does nothing
evidence: scripts/world2d/player_body_2d.gd:235-262 - the E query is a circle of interaction_range (45 ground px, lua/config/game_balance.lua:26) centred on the FACING CELL (target_global), not on the player
scripts/world2d/npc_2d.gd:100-103 - Blund's interact area is an ellipse with reach 60
scripts/ghostfam/seek/hide_seek.gd:106 - before_talk returns false when the player is more than find_px 72 from Blund
scripts/world2d/npc_2d.gd:212 - interact() returns with no feedback when the hook returns false
tests/sections/ghostfam_seek.gd:81-82, 236-238 - tests call seek.before_talk / actor.interact directly at 73/65/55 px; no test exercises nearest_interactable() at 72-200 px
scripts/world2d/npc_2d.gd:79-86 + scripts/world2d/iso.gd:50 (MASK_WALKING includes LAYER_NPC) - the hidden Blund keeps a solid body; hide_seek.gd:83 only sets alpha 0
findings.description: The player picks an interactable with a 45 px circle about one cell (90-128 ground px) ahead, and Blund's interact ellipse adds 60 px. So the HUD shows 'Tal med Lille Blund' while Blund is roughly 72-195 ground px away. In that band before_talk refuses the find, interact() returns silently, and no 'come closer' whisper appears. Separately, the invisible Blund keeps his 14x8 collision body, so the player bumps into an unseen obstacle at the hiding spot.
findings.player_impact: At the climax of the minigame (the 'Psst! Du er lige ved siden af mig!' whisper at 140 px), the prompt appears and E does nothing. Players will think the find is broken or needs something else. Bumping into an invisible object is confusing and gives the hiding spot away. This is inferred from the query geometry, not seen in play.
findings.recommendation: Make the two radii agree. Either disable Blund's InteractArea (_interact.collision_layer = 0) while ghostfam_hiding is true and his ground distance is above find_px, or raise find_px to about 130 and keep the prompt. When before_talk rejects a find, emit a whisper ('Tættere på ... hihi') instead of returning silently. Clear Npc2D._body's collision layer while hiding and restore it in _exit_tree/_refresh. Add a test that moves world.player to 100 px with facing toward Blund and asserts nearest_interactable() and the find result agree.

findings.description: The keepsake guard is correct, but the fallback choice undercuts the ladder. The fairy lantern is in a weekly-respawning boss pool of four items with a 6-kill pity timer, on a boss the quest line sends the player to. Any player who visits the dungeon will very likely own it long before 80 finds (about 20 game weeks). For those players the climax of a two-year chase is a shop-buyable rare candelabra they already got at 24 finds. The unique step similarly turns into a 700 g shop lamp. At minimum, make the step-5 fallback a different item from step 3 (for example chandelier_gold, or a non-shop rare from loot). findings.description: Six of the eight heroes (fox, fairy, hobbit looks) get no introduction to the counted game. There is no quest, letter or journal entry, and Blund's stranger meeting does not mention the card or prizes. Blund is invisible exactly when the game runs, so a non-ghost player only learns of it by stumbling on the shimmer, asking Silke 'Hvor gemmer Blund sig?' or reading Pip's post list. findings.description: LifeFlow.ask emits EventBus.dialogue_started with the portrait id it borrows. QuestManager treats that as a real conversation with that NPC. Concrete cases: (a) Opening the notice board completes intro_lottery's 'Tal med borgmester Hyldeblomst' without meeting her. That also unlocks home tier 2 (lua/data/home_tiers.lua:58). (b) With supply_run active and 10 wood + 6 stone carried, pressing E on any fast-travel post in Trætoppen hands the goods to Kløvermynte and completes the quest. (c) With cookie_delivery active and 12 carrots carried, reading a farm-mailbox letter from Maja (birthday_cake / math_bakery_counts), or picking a Maja quest on the board, takes the carrots and pays the reward even if the player answers 'Måske senere'. The same leak gives remote progress to animal_products (Rosa), flower_necklace (Lily), the Thorin turn-ins and lost_cat's 'ask the neighbours'. People-book 'last talked' (scripts/ui/social/people.gd:63-65) is also overwritten.
findings.player_impact: Story beats and the help-a-citizen loop can be skipped by accident: the intro meeting with the mayor and in-person deliveries happen invisibly at a signpost or mailbox. Players also see the wrong character's name and portrait on objects. Quest completion feels random.
findings.recommendation: Give LifeFlow.ask a 'speaker' that is only a portrait/name and emit dialogue_started only for real NPC conversations. Split it as LifeFlow.ask(owner, portrait_id, lines, choices, emit_talk := false) and pass false from NoticeBoard2D, Rejsestolpe2D, PostBox2D and LifeFlow.offer. Use a neutral speaker for the board (clerk_fjerpen, who keeps the board in int_raadhuset.json:35) and none for the signpost (a sign card with no portrait). Add a test in tests/sections/city_life.gd: with supply_run active plus its goods, interact with a Rejsestolpe2D and assert the quest is still active and the goods are still in the backpack. Do the same for intro_lottery with the board.

findings.description: The only progression-critical NPC meeting on day 1 has no correct pointer. The quest text leads the player to Trætoppen. Trætoppen has the Town Hall, but she never works there on day 1, and only works there on Tue/Wed/Thu 09:30-15:00. The journal says the quest is on the farm. The locator at Postkontoret omits her until the player already has a heart with her, which they cannot have earned before the first meeting. She is visible only outdoors in Hyggebyen between 10:30 and 18:30; a player who arrives in the evening finds a locked house. This matches the first-hour report that the mayor cannot be found on day 1, and it blocks the first home upgrade.
findings.player_impact: New players wander Trætoppen and the Rådhus looking for the mayor, cannot finish the intro quest on day 1, and cannot start the home-upgrade track. This hurts the first-hour experience the most.

findings.description: Answer to question 1: a typical walking loop (farm porch → Trætoppen → Hyggebyen shop → Skovlift → forest → farm) costs about 160 game-min of the 20 h day (06:00-02:00), and running cuts that by about a third. The day is not travel-starved. Fast travel unlocks early (ft_farm on the first crossing, day 1) but adds little: it never connects the farm, Hyggebyen or the forest hub, only four points inside one area, and each use triggers a full rebuild of Trætoppen. It is also hard to discover: there is no visible post, no first-use explanation, the menu labels promise areas the player does not reach, and the first interaction is an empty menu.
findings.player_impact: Most players will never knowingly use fast travel. Those who do will be confused when 'Hyggebyen' leaves them in Trætoppen, and the feature does not shorten the trips that actually take time (farm ↔ Hyggebyen ↔ Skovlift ends).

findings.title: All music, ambience and SFX are one-algorithm synth placeholders; boss, festival and farm music are indistinguishable
evidence: assets/audio/music/synth-manifest.json "status": "synthesized placeholder" (same for sfx/ and amb/)

tools/voice/synth_common.py:39-44 every music track = 'sparse pentatonic placeholder', the same 8-note pattern [0,7,12,14,9,7,4,2] at 1.5 s per note; only the root pitch (seeded from the name) differs
tools/voice/synth_common.py:31-38 every ambience = low-pass noise plus a chirp at 2100 Hz (day) / 1400 Hz (night); town_day and farm_day differ only by seed
tools/voice/synth_common.py:26-30 every non-noise SFX = the same 3-partial tone, so loot_legendary vs pickup_soft differ only in pitch
docs/qa/mechanics/audio/waveforms.json: all 14 music files RMS -35.8..-36.1 dBFS, peak -23.4..-24.0, 47 s mono 22.05 kHz
docs/game_design.md:124-126 'Music: Orchestral + Nordic folk (soft strings, flute, harp)… Voice: Warm Danish narration'
lua/config/audio.lua:9-10 Hyggebyen and Trætoppen share city_theme and town_day/town_night
findings.description: The whole soundtrack comes from deterministic pure-Python placeholder recipes. All 14 music tracks are the same arpeggio at the same tempo and envelope, transposed. boss/boss_final have no more tension than farm_theme, and festival tracks have no festive character. All ambiences are the same filtered noise with a periodic chirp. The two towns (fairy shopping district vs treetop city) share one theme and one ambience. The loops are only 47 s (music) and 24 s (ambience), so they repeat constantly over an 06:00-02:00 day.
findings.player_impact: Music does not mark area, mood, danger or celebration. A boss floor sounds like the farm. The 47 s loops become grating within minutes, and there is a release pipeline (macOS/Windows) in flight.
findings.recommendation: Treat audio as a release blocker workstream. Commission or license real stems for at least farm, city (separate Hyggebyen and Trætoppen), forest/dungeon acts, boss and the festival set, as ≥2-3 min loops at 44.1 kHz stereo. Replace the files at the same ids under assets/audio/{music,amb,sfx}; the pipeline already supports drop-in replacement (docs/voice_lines.md:43). Until then, add at least a tempo, instrument and mode variation per recipe in synth_common.py so boss/festival/farm are distinguishable.
findings.dim: Audio direction: music, ambience, SFX feedback and Danish voice playback
findings.verification: confirmed: Checked tools/voice/synth_common.py:16-49. Every music track uses the same notes=[0,7,12,14,9,7,4,2] at 1.5 s per step and the same envelope; only base=110*2**((seed%12)/12) and the start offset (seed%8) differ. Ambience is smooth noise*3 plus a pulse at 2100 Hz (day) or 1400 Hz (night), with special cases only for rain, shop_interior and cave_drip, so farm_day and town_day differ only by RNG seed. Non-noisy SFX are the same 3-partial tone (loot_legendary and pickup_soft both tonal, so they differ only in pitch). Durations are 48-1 = 47 s for music and 25-1 = 24 s for ambience after the 1 s overlap; synth-manifest status is 'synthesized placeholder'. waveforms.json: all 14 music files RMS -35.8..-36.1 dBFS, 47 s. game_design.md:124-126 asks for orchestral/Nordic folk. audio.lua:9-10: hyggebyen and traetoppen share city_theme and town_day/town_night (the maps' @music headers also both say city_theme). docs/voice_lines.md:43 confirms drop-in replacement. P1 is defensible: the entire score contradicts the stated audio direction and would block a release. | partly: The facts check out in the worktree (f80e7aed). All three synth-manifest.json files say "status": "synthesized placeholder". In tools/voice/synth_common.py:39-44, every music track uses the same notes=[0,7,12,14,9,7,4,2] at 1.5 s per step, the same envelope and a drone. Only base=110*2**((seed%12)/12) changes, so each track is a transposition plus a rotated start note. Ambience (:31-38) is the same low-passed noise with a chirp at 1400 Hz (night) or 2100 Hz (day); only rain, shop_interior and cave_drip have their own recipes. Non-noisy SFX (:28) is the same 3-partial tone at base*3. Durations are 48 s for music and 25 s for ambience, minus a 1 s crossfade (:46-50), giving 47 s and 24 s loops. lua/config/audio.lua:9-10 maps hyggebyen and traetoppen to the same town_day, town_night and city_theme, and interior (:12) uses city_theme too. docs/game_design.md:124-126 asks for orchestral and Nordic-folk music. I lowered it from P1 because the audio pipeline itself works: area, day/night, festival and dungeon-act routing (audio_director.gd:52-71, cues.gd:36-42) picks the right track, so only the asset content is missing. The tracks are openly labelled placeholders, and no gameplay system or core loop breaks. Audio content is also not among the owner's stated hard requirements. This is real asset and production debt, but it is P2, not a major broken system.

findings.description: Of the requested core actions, only harvest (pickup_soft), buy and sell (coin_clink through gold_changed delta>0), gift (gift_sparkle), heart up, quest accept/complete and dungeon hit/hurt/loot make a sound. Cover: crop_planted→seed_plant, crop_watered→water_pour, a hoe/till event, resource_node_hit→chop/pick by node_type, recipe_crafted→craft_done, home_upgraded→a fanfare plus a music sting, furniture_placed→furniture_thunk, garment_equipped→cloth_rustle, enemy_defeated→poof. Handle dungeon_boss_defeated in cues.gd: play a victory sting, then music/rune_rest or the act track. Remove the floor>0 gate for ordinary pickups (keep rarity cues). Fade music and ambience out in _sleep_sequence and _on_player_defeated, and play a soft wake chime on day_started.

The music id is 'festival_'+GameManager.season. Festival areas and seasons, verified in lua/festivals/fixed/*.lua: aarsskiftet, vinterlysene (traetoppen) and bagedagen (hyggebyen) are all vinter; badedagen and midsommerlanterner are sommer; blomsterfesten and honningdagen are foraar; hoestfesten and maanemarkedet are efteraar. findings.title: No night, late-night, season or snow/fog audio states; rain cuts in and out abruptly
evidence: lua/config/audio.lua:6-12 each area has one 'music' key; only ambience has day/night variants, so the same track runs 06:00 → 02:00
scripts/audio/audio_director.gd:57 ambience by is_night() only; no season input anywhere in the director
tools/voice/synth_common.py:34-35 day ambience = chirps at 2100 Hz, so 'birdsong' also plays in winter
lua/config/game_balance.lua:94-98 vinter: sne 0.45, taage 0.25; audio_director.gd:61 only regn/torden trigger audio, so snow and fog are silent
scripts/autoload/audio_manager.gd:263-277 play_rain() starts at a fixed -22 dB and stops with player.stop(), no fade, while area ambience crossfades for 1.5 s (:246-255)
scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd:698-713 pass-out/sleep: no audio change under the black fade; no morning cue on wake
findings.description: Night changes only the ambience bed, and only on the farm/town/forest presets. Music is identical at 10:00 and 01:30, and there is no wind-down before the 02:00 pass-out. Seasons do not change any audio outside festival days, and winter mornings play the same bird chirps as spring. Snow (45% of winter days) and fog have no ambience. Entering or leaving a shop in the rain hard-starts or hard-cuts the rain loop, the one abrupt cut in an otherwise crossfaded system.
findings.player_impact: The day/season cycle that drives a Stardew-like game is mostly invisible to the ear. Late night has no audible 'go to bed' pressure, and the rain cuts are noticeable.
findings.recommendation: Allow 'music_night' (and optionally 'music_<season>') keys in lua/config/audio.lua and pick them in refresh(). Fade music out from about 00:00 (raw 24) and silence it near pass-out. Add 'amb/<area>_winter' or a season multiplier, plus 'amb/snow_wind' and 'amb/fog' overlays keyed by TimeManager.weather. Give play_rain a 1.0-1.5 s volume tween in and out like _fade_ambience.
findings.dim: Audio direction: music, ambience, SFX feedback and Danish voice playback

The synth day ambience chirp is at 2100 Hz (synth_common.py:35). game_balance.lua:94-99: vinter has sne 0.45 and taage 0.25, and only regn/torden trigger audio (director :61). play_rain (audio_manager.gd:263-277) uses a fixed -22 dB player volume, starts with play() and stops with stop() with no tween, while ambience crossfades (:225-255). world_2d.gd _sleep_sequence has no audio change. Night is hour >= 20 or < 5 (time_manager.gd:99-102). Accurate.

findings.title: Greenhouse seed shelf: open 24/7 with 99 of every seed, cheaper than town, and the only source of two winter crops
evidence: lua/shops/greenhouse_seeds.lua:3-18 every seed incl. moonflower and glow berry at stock 99 / restock 99, buy_multiplier 1.0
lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:32 moonflower_seeds = { stock = 8, restock = 4 }; lua/shops/magic_store.lua:13,24 glow berry x1.1, stock 8 / restock 4

lua/buildings/hyggebyen.lua:16 froebutikken hours = { open = 8, close = 18, closed = { 6 } }; greenhouse_seeds is claimed by no building, so ShopHoursGate.open_override returns null and the shelf is always open (shop_hours_gate.gd open_override)
lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:27-36 sells frost_kale but neither snow_turnip_seeds nor snowdrop_seeds
localization/farm_site.csv:58,62 snow seed descriptions: 'Dyrkes om vinteren eller hele året i drivhuset'
data/maps/greenhouse.map:21 '@marker S greenhouse action=seeds' (shelf only inside the greenhouse)
findings.description: The greenhouse shelf is meant as a self-service convenience (farm-completion REVIEW.md:12). In practice it replaces the town seed shop and the magic store's glow-berry stall. It is open every hour of every day (including Sunday, when Kløvermyntes Frø is closed) and restocks 99 of every seed. It ignores the deliberate scarcity of moonflower (8/4) and glow berry (8/4), and it sells glow berry about 10% cheaper than the magic store. It is also the only place that sells snow_turnip and snowdrop seeds. Their descriptions say they grow outdoors in winter, but a player without a greenhouse cannot buy them, so outdoor winter farming is frost_kale only (5.4 g/day).
findings.player_impact: After the greenhouse is built there is no reason to visit Hyggebyen's seed shop or Zephyr for seeds, so town shop hours and stock design stop mattering for farming. Early-winter players read about two winter crops they cannot find in any town shop.
findings.recommendation: Limit greenhouse_seeds.lua to a small stock (e.g. 10/5 per seed, moonflower and glow berry 2/1), or to the greenhouse-exclusive crops only. Add snow_turnip_seeds and snowdrop_seeds to seed_shop.lua (e.g. 20/20 and 15/15) so winter outdoor farming does not depend on the greenhouse. Optionally tie shelf restock to Kløvermynte's open days.
findings.verification: partly: The data is confirmed: greenhouse_seeds.lua:3-18 stocks all 11 seeds at 99/99 x1.0. No building claims the shelf, so it has no hours. Snow_turnip and snowdrop seeds are sold only there (seed_shop.lua:27-36 has frost_kale only), while their copy (farm_site.csv:58,62) implies outdoor winter growing. However, the 24/7 no-hours behaviour is deliberate. docs/design/towns_farm_social_workpackages.json:3799 and :4923 say the shelf has 'no opening hours' so the seed shop's closed day cannot stop winter planting. The all-crop shelf is also asserted by tests/sections/farm_automation.gd:23-27 and :203 (seed_shelf_open_after_midnight). The design doc originally scoped the shelf to winter seeds only, so the expansion to all seeds at 99 does undercut the 8/4 scarcity of moonflower and glow berry; that impact is already counted in FARM-01. The winter-seed sourcing gap was already noted in docs/review/game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md:115. Frost kale is ~6.4-7.5 g/day (seed 30, sell 60, 4 days), not 5.4. A workaround exists (frost kale outdoors, greenhouse at tier 2), so P3.

findings.title: Kitten and puppy produce an item with no use, and their copy promises behaviour that does not exist
evidence: lua/config/husbandry.lua:65-94 cat/dog product = friendship_token, product_interval = on_bond, building = house
lua/items/resources.lua:170-178 friendship_token category = special, sell_price = 0
scripts/social/gifts/gift_rules.gd:13,78 NEVER_GIVEN_CATEGORIES includes 'special', so giftable() refuses it
scripts/autoload/economy_manager.gd:49 UNSELLABLE_CATEGORIES ['quest','special']; no recipe or quest consumes friendship_token (rg over lua/recipes, lua/quests: rewards only)
scripts/farm/animal_husbandry.gd:705-713 bond level only grants products for ON_BOND species; nothing else reads bond_level
localization/da.csv:68 kitten 'følger dig rundt'; :70 puppy 'vogter din gård'; scripts/farm/animal_yard.gd:17-34 every animal only wanders the yard
lua/items/animals.lua kitten/puppy buy_price 350 and they share the 3-slot house with owl/fox (husbandry.lua:151,166)
findings.description: The two pet species cost 350 g each and take house slots that could hold an owl (about 133 g/day) or a fox (about 80 g/day). Their only output is friendship_token, which cannot be sold, gifted, crafted or turned in. Bond level, the animal 'hearts', has no other effect for any species, so caring for a pet changes nothing in the game. The item copy promises a kitten that follows you around and a puppy that guards the farm. Neither exists: all animals only wander the shared yard.
findings.player_impact: Players who adopt a kitten or puppy get a care chore with no reward and a growing stack of dead tokens, and can feel misled by the descriptions.
findings.recommendation: Give friendship_token a sink: make it giftable (giftable = true on the def, or remove 'special' from it) as a neutral-plus gift worth friendship, or let Pip and the furniture fairies trade it for something cosmetic. Or have pets give an actual perk at bond levels 2/4/6 (e.g. dog: +1 forage find on the farm per day; cat: small happiness aura for coop animals). Rewrite da.csv:68/70 to match what is implemented.
findings.verification: partly: Confirmed: cat/dog produce friendship_token on_bond (husbandry.lua:65-94). The token is category special with sell_price 0 (resources.lua:170-178). Bond level only matters for ON_BOND products (animal_husbandry.gd:705-713). Every animal only wanders the yard (animal_yard.gd), with no follow or guard behaviour (no 'follow' code in scripts/farm). The copy at da.csv:68/70 promises those behaviours. The kitten and puppy cost 350 (animals.lua). The owl (~133 g/day happy) and fox (~80 g/day) figures match docs/qa/game-mechanics/balance.json. Correction: the token is not wholly without use. lua/quests/fairy_friendship.lua:17-23 has the objective earn_friendship: own 5 friendship_token (have=true, a repeatable 600 g quest), and lua/config/traetoppen.lua:48 includes it in Kiki's caches. It is not consumed, though, and many quests already reward it (fix_roof, birthday_cake, enchanted_garden, etc.), so pets add little. The main defect is the misleading copy plus a weak 350 g purchase: P3 rather than P2.

findings.title: Catnip is still a dominated crop with no use, and its description says cats love it but cats cannot eat it

evidence: localization/economy.csv:53 ITEM_CATNIP_SEEDS_DESC 'Elskes af katte'; :55 ITEM_CATNIP_DESC 'Duften får hver kat til at spinde'
lua/config/husbandry.lua:73 cat feed_types = { animal_treats, milk }

Its seed is the only one whose description gives no growing information. Instead it promises cats love it, but the cat's feed list excludes catnip, so the care screen never offers it.
findings.player_impact: Players buy catnip expecting to treat their kitten, find it cannot be fed, and earn about a third of what carrots pay.

Make it the cat's favorite_feed (bonus 25) and add it as a love for one or two NPCs in gift_tastes.lua. Change the seed description to growth info, e.g. 'Kattens livret. Høst efter 5 dage'.

The feed check rejects other foods (animal_husbandry.gd:397-398). The only catnip references in lua/ are the shops, the crop row, preserve_catnip/juice_catnip (farm_equipment.lua:23-24) and the lost_cat seed reward (lost_cat.lua:58); there is none in lua/social. findings.title: Fertilizer is still a no-decision purchase, and its description hides what it does
findings.prior_ref: mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18 E2 'Fertilizer is a dominant, decision-free purchase' (still open, re-verified)
evidence: lua/items/crops.lua:176-186 fertilizer buy_price 15
lua/config/game_balance.lua:36-37 harvest_yield = 1, fertilizer_bonus_yield = 1
scripts/world2d/farm_grid.gd:239-240 +1 crop on the next harvest; :222-223 can be reapplied after every regrow harvest
localization/economy.csv:61 ITEM_FERTILIZER_DESC 'Bedre høst'
findings.description: Unchanged: 15 g doubles the next harvest, worth +45 to +180 g. With regrowing crops it can be reapplied after every harvest (glow berry: +150 g per 15 g every 4 days). The only limit is the 30-per-day seed-shop stock. The description 'Bedre høst' does not say it doubles one harvest.
findings.player_impact: There is no decision to make: always fertilize. It also doubles the glow-berry imbalance (59 g/day per plot).
findings.recommendation: Either make it a percentage, e.g. a 50% chance of +1 with price 25, or scale the price to crop tier. At minimum, change the copy to 'Giver én ekstra afgrøde ved næste høst'.
findings.verification: confirmed: Fertilizer costs 15 (crops.lua:176-186), with fertilizer_bonus_yield=1 (game_balance.lua:37). Harvest adds +1 and clears the flag (farm_grid.gd:239-240, 253). apply_supply allows reapplying on a regrowing plot because the state is PLANTED or WATERED, not READY (farm_grid.gd:209-223). Copy is 'Bedre høst' (economy.csv:61). Minor: it is also sold at festival_markets.lua:64, so the 30/day seed-shop stock is not the only source. Prior E2 is still open.

findings.title: Keg is a worse preserves jar for 9 of 11 crops; recipe home-tier gates are bypassed by the seed shop
evidence: lua/config/farm_equipment.lua:6-7 preserves_jar days = 2, keg days = 3
lua/items/farm_equipment.lua:2 'Preserves sell for 2x crop value + 50; juice for 3x crop value'; :9-10 preserve_turnip 140 vs juice_turnip 135
lua/items/farm_equipment.lua:7-8 jar buy 350, keg buy 500
lua/recipes/farm_equipment.lua:4,6 quality_sprinkler and keg min_home_tier = 3; :5 jar min_home_tier = 2
lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:44-46 quality_sprinkler, preserves_jar, keg stocked from day 1 with no tier gate
findings.description: Value added per machine-day is (c+50)/2 for a jar and 2c/3 for a keg. The keg only wins when the crop is worth more than 150 g: pumpkin (106.7 vs 105) and moonflower (120 vs 115). It ties glow berry (100 vs 100) and loses clearly for the other 8 crops. For turnip the juice even sells for less than the jam (135 vs 140). Yet the keg costs more (500 vs 350), takes a day longer and its recipe needs home tier 3. Those recipe gates (keg and quality sprinkler at tier 3) also mean nothing, because Kløvermynte sells all of them from day 1.
findings.player_impact: Players who invest in kegs earn less, and the 'craft at tier 3' progression step is invisible because the shop skips it.
findings.recommendation: Make juice 2.5c + 60 or shorten the keg to 2 days, so it is the better choice for mid-value crops and the jar for cheap ones. Either gate quality_sprinkler and keg in seed_shop.lua behind the same home tier (if ShopSystem supports a tier field), or drop the min_home_tier from the recipes so the two sources agree.
findings.verification: partly: Numbers verified (farm_equipment.lua items and config). Value added per machine-day, jar against keg: turnip 47.5/30, carrot 57.5/43.3, strawberry and catnip 52.5/36.7, sunflower 60/46.7, frost_kale 55/40, snow_turnip 65/53.3, snowdrop 80/73.3, glow 100/100, pumpkin 105/106.7, moonflower 115/120. So the keg loses for 8 crops, ties for 1 and wins for 2 ('worse for 9' counts the tie). Turnip juice 135 < jam 140 is true. Recipe tiers are 3/2/3 (recipes/farm_equipment.lua:4-6), and seed_shop.lua:44-46 sells the items with no gate; ShopSystem has no tier field (no min_home_tier in shop_system.gd). Corrections: per crop input, the keg returns more for every crop worth over 50 g (3c > 2c+50), so it is a real throughput-versus-yield trade-off. docs/review/game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md:119 already frames it that way. Also, the recipe gates are not meaningless: they gate the cheap crafted route, while the shop is a pricier gold route.

findings.title: 'Fe-støv til marken' costs 900 g for 3 days on one plot, sold beside a 300 g permanent sprinkler
findings.prior_ref: mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18 F3 'fairy_dust_water is a luxury sink' (still open, re-verified)
evidence: lua/items/crops.lua:187-197 fairy_dust_water buy_price 900, sell_price 200
lua/config/game_balance.lua:38 auto_water_days = 3
lua/items/farm_equipment.lua:5 sprinkler buy_price 300, waters 4 plots every morning forever
lua/shops/seed_shop.lua:34,43 both on the same shelf
findings.description: Re-verified: one use auto-waters one plot for 3 days, which is 3 waterings worth about 4.5 energy. The same shop sells a sprinkler at a third of the price that waters 4 plots every day indefinitely. Its only real niche is that the hourly auto-water does satisfy a moonflower's night window, but that is not explained anywhere.
findings.player_impact: It is a trap purchase. Buying 3 on day 1 costs more than the 500 g starting money, and new players may buy it because it is the guide's line item.
findings.recommendation: Reprice to 40-60 g, or make it a 7-day effect on a 3x3 area at about 250 g. If its intended niche is moon crops, say so in ITEM_FAIRY_DUST_WATER_DESC ('Vander ét felt i 3 dage – også om natten').
findings.verification: confirmed: buy 900 (crops.lua:187-197) and auto_water_days=3 (game_balance.lua:38). apply_supply waters immediately, and the night roll decrements the counter and re-waters at 06:00 (farm_grid.gd:225-226, 336-339). That covers the application day plus 2 more. The can costs 1.5 energy per use (tools.lua watering_can_copper), so 3 waterings ≈ 4.5 energy. The sprinkler costs 300 and waters 4 plots every morning (farm_site.csv:50), and both are on seed_shop. The moonflower niche is real: the hourly _auto_water(hour) re-waters inside 20-06 (farm_grid.gd:296-311). Copy 'Vand ét felt i 3 dage' (economy.csv:63) does not mention night. Prior F3 is still open.

findings.title: Shipping bin always ships the whole selected stack, with no amount choice and no take-back
evidence: scripts/farm/steading/objects/shipping_bin_2d.gd:17-18 amount = EconomyManager.count_item(id)
scripts/farm/steading/objects/shipping_bin_2d.gd:27-28 consume_backpack_items({id: amount}) then the stack is only a flag (bin_<id>) until the morning payout (farm_stage.gd:50-74)
lua/quests/birthday_cake.lua turn-in needs 3 turnips + 1 moonflower; NPC loves include carrot, strawberry, moonflower, sunflower (lua/social/gift_tastes.lua:76-97)
findings.description: Pressing E at the bin with a crop selected ships every unit in the backpack. There is no confirmation, no partial amount, and no way to take items back before the morning roll.
findings.player_impact: Players lose quest or gift crops (e.g. the moonflower for the birthday cake, a loved strawberry) with one key press.
findings.recommendation: Ship one unit per tap, with hold or a modifier to ship the stack. Or show a quantity confirm like the shop's sell dialog. Let the last shipped stack be taken back until 02:00 (the bin_<id> flag makes this easy).
findings.verification: confirmed: shipping_bin_2d.gd:17-28 sets amount = EconomyManager.count_item(selected) and consumes all of it. The bin then only holds the bin_<id> area flag until the morning payout (farm_stage.gd:58-71). There is no quantity prompt and no withdraw path. The whisper FARMSITE_BIN_PUT reports the count only after the fact.

findings.title: Every farm animal from all three buildings wanders the same 3-cell yard

scripts/farm/animal_yard.gd:17-34 spawns an Animal2D for every animal in AnimalHusbandry.animals and picks targets within radius 3

lua/config/husbandry.lua:178-199 max capacities coop 12 + barn 18 + house 9 = 39 animals

findings.player_impact: A fully upgraded farm becomes a stacked pile of animals where it is hard to target the right one, and buildings don't visibly hold their own animals. Not runtime-verified (Godot not launched).
findings.recommendation: Give each building slot its own animal_yard marker, or have AnimalYard filter by building_type, and spread the radius by capacity. Alternatively cap the number of visible actors and offer the care screen's animal list for the rest.
findings.verification: partly: Confirmed: farm.map:30 has a single '@marker c animal_yard r=3'. findings.title: STILL OPEN: the tier-6 gate (crystal_cave, floors 10-12) is deeper than the tier-8/9 gates

lua/quests/crystal_cave.lua: explore_cave = zone_entered crystal_cave; lua/config/dungeon.lua:87 zone crystal_cave = floors 10-12 (past the floor-4 and floor-8 bosses)

A player who cannot beat the floor-8 boss is capped at tier 5 however rich they are, while the tier 8 and 9 gates are easier. Combined with the material wall above, the mid-ladder is lumpy: hard at tier 6, easy at 8-9, then a material trickle at 8-10.

findings.verification: partly: Still open and accurate as a fact. home_tiers.lua:204 gates tier 6 on crystal_cave, whose explore_cave needs zone_entered crystal_cave = floors 10-12 (dungeon.lua:85-87). Bosses sit on floor 4 (dungeon.lua:179) and floor 8 (dungeon.lua:286), and start_floors only offers floor 1 plus activated runestones (dungeon_floors.gd:214-219). Tier 8 is snurresvampen (floor 4, :282). However, prior review game-review-2026-10-18.md:52-55 established that this ordering is authored: the HOME_TIER_6_GATE copy narrates Krystalgrotten, and validator rule S13 pins snurresvampen at tier 8 and moonstone_crown at tier 9. findings.title: Tier 5 needs 4 copper plates, but the copper-plate forge only unlocks at tier 5
evidence: lua/data/home_tiers.lua:165 tier 5 materials include `copper_plate = 4`
lua/recipes/materials.lua:71-76 forge_copper_plate: station smedje, min_home_tier 5 (the forge_bench unlock of tier 5, home_tiers.lua:178)
lua/shops/home_shops.lua:221 copper_plate only in the weekly fine-goods slot (4 of 8 ≈ 50%/week); lua/data/loot_tables.lua:414 dybe_bregner uncommon pool (floors 4-6)
findings.description: The plate needed to build the forge tier can only be crafted after that tier is built. Before it, the player must wait for a week in which the yard happens to roll copper plates (median 1 week, 90th percentile about 4 weeks) or find them on floors 4-6. Brass bar and gold leaf have the same tier-5 lock but are not needed until tiers 7-9.
findings.player_impact: A confusing 'come back next week' wait right after the first-animal gate, with nothing explaining where plates come from.
findings.recommendation: Lower forge_copper_plate's min_home_tier to 4 (or give it the snedkerbord station), or pin copper_plate as a fixed builder_yard row (stock 12, restock 4).
findings.verification: confirmed: home_tiers.lua:165 tier 5 needs copper_plate = 4, and :178 tier 5 unlocks forge_bench. materials.lua:71-77 forge_copper_plate has station smedje and min_home_tier 5, and crafting_system.gd:78-81 enforces min_home_tier. Before tier 5, copper_plate comes only from the weekly ugens_fine_varer (4 of 8, qty 12, home_shops.lua:214-221) or loot: the dybe_bregner uncommon pool (loot_tables.lua:414) and the crystal-cave pool (:642). The waiting estimates (median 1 week, about 4 weeks at the 90th percentile) are consistent with a 50% weekly chance.

findings.title: Refining recipes are worth less than their raw ore, and iron_sword is a sell-price outlier
evidence: lua/recipes/materials.lua:71-77 forge_copper_plate: 3 copper_ore (sell 14 each = 42) → 1 copper_plate (buy 36, sell 14); tier 8 needs 30 plates (home_tiers.lua:280)
lua/recipes/materials.lua forge_brass_bar: 2 copper + 1 iron (43 sell) → brass_bar sell 19; twist_rope: 3 moss → rope (sell 2)
lua/recipes/guide_recipes.lua lantern_post / scarecrow: inputs sell 46/18 → outputs 30/12

lua/items/tools.lua:151-161 iron_sword uncommon buy 750 / sell 300 (ratio 0.40) vs lua/config/rarity.lua uncommon weapon_sell_ratio 0.12 (wpn_dagger_flint 70, wpn_club_oak 105); every rare weapon sells for 205 or less
lua/quests/dark_forest_mining.lua:44 iron_sword in every weekly repeat reward
findings.description: Smelting or weaving destroys value compared with selling the raw ore and buying the product, which teaches 'never refine'. Wool to fabric was already reported as prior E1. The legacy iron_sword keeps an old 0.4 sell ratio, so a loot or quest iron sword outsells every rare weapon. The weekly mining quest hands one out every time.
findings.player_impact: Crafting the home's copper plates feels like a loss. Selling price does not follow rarity.
findings.recommendation: Set copper_plate sell to at least 45 (or the recipe to 2 ore). Set brass_bar sell to at least 45, rope sell to at least 4 or twist_rope to 2 moss, and iron_sword sell_price to 90 (rarity rule). Add a validator check that a processing recipe's output sell value is at least its input sell value for building materials.
findings.verification: partly: Correct: forge_copper_plate takes 3 copper_ore (sell 14 each = 42) for 1 plate (buy 36, sell 14), so refining is worse than selling the ore and buying the plate. twist_rope takes 3 moss (sell 9) for rope (buy 6, sell 2). iron_sword (tools.lua:151-161) is uncommon with buy 750 / sell 300, while rarity.gd:34 sets uncommon weapon_sell_ratio 0.12 (wpn_dagger_flint sells for 70). The highest weapon sell price in weapons.lua is 205. iron_sword is in the dark_forest_mining reward (:46), in the uncommon loot weapon pool and on the smithy shelf. Wrong: brass_bar inputs sell for 43 (2x14 + 15), but brass costs 48 to buy, so refining does NOT lose value against sell-ore-and-buy. The guide-recipe numbers are off: lantern_post inputs sell for 44 (not 46) and give 30; scarecrow inputs sell for 16 (not 18) and give 12. Those are functional placeables, so a sell-value comparison is a weak argument there. The copper_plate, rope and iron_sword points hold.
