findings.title: Legendary and unique loot comes slowly and is mostly post-game; the first boss kill pays only a rune and most repeat boss chests are empty
evidence: scripts/dungeon_loot/reward_rules.gd:14-19: first kill = first_kill_items (+extra) only; pool not rolled
scripts/dungeon_loot/reward_rules.gd:21: repeat kill within respawn_days(7) -> empty result
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:846,855-857,868-870: legendary_bp 1600/1600/800, pity_kills 6/6/10, Konge pool = sword_moon, staff_star, gem_moon_heart
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:4: 'legendary items never come from chests'; scripts/dungeon_loot/container_rules.gd:42 filters ordinary rolls to normal/uncommon/rare
lua/config/dungeon_loot.lua:31: `unique = { cooldown_days = 7 }` gates all hunted uniques (19 band spots incl. 3 lake chests + 8 wanderers = 27)
scripts/loot/loot_markers.gd:127-128 + localization/features_ui.csv:47: an empty boss chest whispers 'Intet andet end støv og et lille hjerte af mos.' though nothing is given
Analytic model of loot_tables odds (scratchpad dive.py): a full 12-floor dive yields ~0.24 rare furniture, ~0.24 rare clothing, ~0.12 rare weapons
findings.description: The owner's pitch is that adventuring yields rare, unique and legendary loot. In the data, a full dive gives about 0.6 rare furniture, clothing or weapons in total. Uniques are limited to one per 7 days across all 27 hunted sources, so a complete dungeon collection takes at least 27 weeks (about 189 days, nearly 7 seasons). Legendaries come only from boss pools, and only on repeat kills spaced 7 days apart: on average about 4 weekly kills per Glødesvamp item and about 7 per Svampekonge item, so roughly 21 weeks for the Konge's three items after the first kill. The first kill of each boss, the emotional peak, drops a single key-rune, and the first boss's chest contains only that rune. When a boss is beaten again within its 7 days, the sealed chest opens to a generic 'nothing' whisper that also claims there is a 'little heart of moss'.
findings.player_impact: The climactic boss victories feel unrewarded. Players who dive for legendaries go months of game time without one, and the repeat-boss loop teaches them that bosses are not worth fighting.
findings.recommendation: Make the first kill roll the boss pool once (guaranteed one item from `pool`), or pay a konge chest on the first kill as well. Shorten respawn_days to 3–4 or raise legendary_bp (for example Konge 1600, pity 6). Scope the unique cooldown per band rather than globally, or cut it to 3 days. Give the not-ready boss chest its own copy (for example 'Svampekongen har intet mere i denne uge – kom igen om %d dage') and remove the false 'hjerte af mos' wording, or make that line actually grant a moss item.
findings.verification: partly: Accurate parts: reward_rules.gd:14-19 pays only first_kill_items plus extra on a first kill (rune; plus moonstone x2 for Glød and Konge). :21 returns an empty plan on a repeat kill within respawn_days 7. That empty result reaches loot_chest_2d.gd:293 -> loot_markers.gd:127-128, which whispers FIND_UI_NOTHING 'Intet andet end støv og et lille hjerte af mos.' (features_ui.csv:47), a false 'heart of moss' for a sealed boss chest. Pity math checks out: about 4.06 expected kills per Glød or Snurre item (p 0.16, pity 6) and about 7.07 per Konge item (p 0.08, pity 10). 27 hunted unique sources (19 band spots + 8 wanderers) share the 7-day cooldown (dungeon_loot.lua:31). Inaccurate parts: 'the first boss kill pays only a rune' and 'legendaries come only from boss pools'. The first Snurresvamp kill completes the snurresvampen quest (loot_tables.lua:846 first_kill_quest; quests/snurresvampen.lua:33-35), which pays 1200 gold, the LEGENDARY hat_mushroom_spinner (clothing.lua:511-516) and 3 fairy dust, plus +1 heart (dungeon_run.gd:57). Dungeon-themed quests also pay legendaries: moonstone_crown -> circlet_moon_crown, slotsdroemmen. The slow unique pace is a documented design choice (dungeon_loot.lua:29-31). The '0.6 rare per dive' model could not be reproduced here. Corrected severity: P3. The confirmed bug is the empty or false boss-chest whisper; the pacing point is a design opinion.

findings.title: Runestones give unlimited full heals and oil; the oil-refill config is unused and a second visit the same day starts with leftover oil
evidence: scripts/dungeon/markers/runestone_2d.gd:45-48: every interaction calls heal_full() and restore_oil() (not only the first)
scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:166-173,191-194: enemies disengage within 520 px of a lit stone
lua/config/dungeon.lua:23: `oil = { refill_new_floor = true, refill_runestone = true }` - no script reads these keys (rg finds none)
scripts/dungeon/floors/dungeon_floors.gd:188-193: oil refills only on the FIRST entry of a floor per seed day; begin_dungeon_run (player_2d.gd:486-489) does not refill
lua/config/race_perks.lua:135 comment: 'lantern oil per visit of the forest'
scripts/dungeon_run/picker_lines.gd:13-17 sets `warn` flags that scripts/ui/rune_picker.gd:43-46 discards (plain text only)
findings.description: Floors 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 each have a safe zone where pressing E fully heals and refuels any number of times, which makes oil and tonics on those floors meaningless. The design flags that should control refills are dead data. Because the calendar is paused in the forest, players often leave to sell and come back the same day. Those floors are then already marked 'seen', so the lantern starts at whatever was left (possibly 0) and bites the player down to 1 heart, contrary to the 'per visit' comment. The rune picker computes warning flags for a weak weapon, no oil or a nearly full backpack but shows them as plain text, with no warning style.
findings.player_impact: The resource pressure feels inconsistent: free healing on odd floors, and an unexpectedly empty lantern after a same-day re-entry.
findings.recommendation: Read dungeon.oil.refill_* in DungeonFloors and Runestone2D, make runestone rest once per floor per day (or heal only), refill the lantern in begin_dungeon_run if the design means 'per visit', and style rows with `warn` in the rune picker (for example honey label plus icon).
findings.verification: confirmed: runestone_2d.gd:45-48 calls heal_full() and restore_oil() on every interaction; only the quest, autosave and whisper key depend on `first`. Lit stones make enemies within 520 px go idle (enemy_2d.gd:166-173,191-194). Stones sit on alternating floors (dungeon.lua `stone = true` entries). `dungeon.oil.refill_new_floor` and `refill_runestone` are read nowhere: rg across scripts, lua and tests finds only the definition. dungeon_floors.gd:188-193 refills oil only when the floor is not in `seen`. `seen` is cleared only by _clear_day or reset (:57,:78). start_run clears the day only when `seed_day != total_day` (:82), and begin_dungeon_run (player_2d.gd:486-489) does not refill. So a same-day re-entry into seen floors keeps the leftover oil, which contradicts race_perks.lua:133 ('lantern oil per visit of the forest'). The default assist_auto_refuel = 1 softens this when the player carries lantern_oil. picker_lines.gd:13-17 sets `warn`, and rune_picker.gd:43-46 keeps only `text`.

findings.title: The first band has three Danish names: 'Mørkeskoven', 'Skovkanten' and 'Skovbrynet'
evidence: lua/config/dungeon.lua:30: band skovkant `name_key = "ZONE_DARK_FOREST"` -> localization/core.csv:52 'Mørkeskoven' (also the name of the whole dungeon)
localization/core.csv:53: ZONE_FOREST_EDGE 'Skovkanten' (the hub, docs/copy/GLOSSARY.md:51)
localization/finds.csv:4: FIND_AREA_SKOVKANT 'Skovbrynet'; localization/dungeon_items.csv:55 'Ukendt sten (Skovbrynet)'
English: hub and FIND_AREA_SKOVKANT are both 'The Forest Edge'
findings.description: Floors 1–3 show the zone chip 'Mørkeskoven · 1', the same name as the dungeon as a whole. The hub is 'Skovkanten', and the finds and rough stones of those same floors say 'Skovbrynet'. In English the hub and band 1 share one name.
findings.player_impact: Players cannot tell from the item names or the rune picker which part of the forest a stone or find came from.
findings.recommendation: Give band 1 its own glossary name (for example 'Skovkanten' for the band and 'Skovporten' for the hub, or keep the hub and use 'Skovbrynet' everywhere for the band). Add a ZONE_SKOVBRYNET key, point dungeon.bands.skovkant.name_key at it, and record it in docs/copy/GLOSSARY.md.
findings.verification: confirmed: dungeon.lua:29-30 band skovkant name_key = ZONE_DARK_FOREST maps to core.csv:52 'Mørkeskoven'. The hub title is ZONE_FOREST_EDGE 'Skovkanten' (dungeon.lua:16, core.csv:53, GLOSSARY.md:51). finds.csv:4 FIND_AREA_SKOVKANT is 'Skovbrynet', and dungeon_items.csv:55 reads 'Ukendt sten (Skovbrynet)'. In English, 'The Forest Edge' is used for both the hub and band 1. The band name_key also feeds warp labels and the map title (dungeon_export.gd:109,131,245) and the rune picker's floor rows (rune_picker.gd:40).

findings.title: iron_sword sells for 300, more than any rare weapon
evidence: lua/items/tools.lua:151-161: iron_sword uncommon, buy 750, sell 300 (40 %)
lua/config/rarity.lua:34,49: weapon_sell_ratio uncommon 0.12 / rare 0.10
lua/items/weapons.lua: uncommon peers sell 70-105; rare weapons sell 145-205
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:12: duplicate weapon finds are auto-sold at sell value
findings.description: The legacy iron sword ignores the weapon sell ratio. Every duplicate iron_sword from a chest (it is in every band's uncommon weapon pool) auto-sells for 300, which beats any rare weapon, and buying one at 750 to sell back loses less than any other weapon.
findings.player_impact: It is a small economy oddity, and it makes rare weapon finds feel less valuable than a common sword.
findings.recommendation: Set iron_sword sell_price to about 90 (0.12 × 750) and sword_rusty to about 15, in line with weapons.lua.
findings.verification: confirmed: tools.lua:151-161 sets iron_sword to uncommon, buy 750, sell 300. Uncommon peers in weapons.lua sell for 70-105 and rare weapons for 145-205 (dagger_moonshard 145, sword_forest_steel 180, spear_thistle 180, staff_light 200, club_mushroom 205). iron_sword is in every band's uncommon weapon pool (loot_tables.lua:280,424,533,651), and duplicate weapons auto-sell (loot_tables.lua:12). weapon_sell_ratio is not enforced: it appears only as reference data in scripts/data/rarity.gd, so the item's own sell_price is what pays out. The suggested ~90 matches 0.12 × 750. sword_rusty sells for 20, against a normal ratio of 0.15 × 100 = 15.

findings.title: A festival with closes = "all" shuts every shop in both towns, even where the keeper is not attending
evidence: scripts/social/social_manager.gd:783-794 shop_closed_by_festival - no area check; every shop not in stays_open is closed from one hour before the start until the end
scripts/towns/hours.gd:125-128 - Hours.state returns reason 'festival' for any building whose shop is closed by the festival

scripts/social/social_data.gd:285-300 - only home citizens of the festival's own area (plus ghost guests) attend, so Kvak, Sofus, Ugle and Natteblik never attend Hyggebyen festivals and the Hyggebyen keepers never attend Trætoppen ones

Example: blomsterfesten (Hyggebyen, Sunday 12-20) closes Torvekroen, Badehuset, Uglehulen and Brumme's Sunday stall from 11:00 while their routines keep them at their counters; maanemarkedet/midsommerlanterner (to 23) leave Natteblik's 20-23:30 window open for only 30 minutes
findings.description: The rule comment says shops close because 'the keepers walk to the festival then', but the closure applies to every building in both towns, while the roster only takes citizens from the festival's own town. The other town's keepers stay at work behind doors that say 'closed for the festival'.
findings.player_impact: On 9 days a year the player finds shops shut in the other town for no visible reason, with the keeper standing inside. The days are predictable, so this is minor, but it is a visible inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Limit the closure to the festival's own area: in shop_closed_by_festival, pass the building and return false when Hours.building(id).area != meta.area (the hoestfesten stays_open = { bakery } workaround then becomes unnecessary). Alternatively, send non-attending keepers home for the window.
findings.verification: confirmed: shop_closed_by_festival (social_manager.gd:783-794) has no area check, and Hours.now_ctx wires it in for every building (hours.gd:44-46, 124-127). Routines pass str(b.shop or building_id), so Torvekroen (no shop field) is closed too. The roster only takes home citizens of meta.area plus guests (social_data.gd:285-300). blomsterfesten is hyggebyen on foraar 7 (Sunday) with closes all and stays_open {}, which matches the example. maanemarkedet runs 18-23 with closes all, so Natteblik's 20-23:30 window is open only 23:00-23:30. Natteblik's home area is not traetoppen or hyggebyen, so he never attends. Note: TOWNS_FARM_SOCIAL_ADDENDUM.md:442 specifies 'shops are closed unless in stays_open' globally, so this is a spec-level inconsistency rather than a code deviation. The player-visible contradiction is real.

findings.title: Festivals are attended by one town only, so a partner or spouse from the other town never comes to half of them
evidence: scripts/social/social_data.gd:285-300 - the pool is home_area == meta.area; guests are only the ghost family
lua/config/npcs.lua - partner candidates Hoppe, Brumme, Postman Pip, Sofus, Rasmus, Kiki and Bertil live in traetoppen; Maja, Merchant Pip, Birk and Bodil live in hyggebyen

scripts/social/events/festival_stage.gd:156-161 - the 'dance' partner is the attending citizen with the most hearts; scripts/social/relationships/farm_visits.gd:36-43 - a spouse's home_area does not change after marriage
findings.description: In-game Hyggebyen is a district of the treetop city, yet festival crowds are split by home district. A player engaged or married to Hoppe will never see Hoppe at blomsterfesten, honningdagen, maanemarkedet or bagedagen. The dance there picks the highest-hearts Hyggebyen resident instead.
findings.player_impact: The romance and community payoff at festivals is missing for half of the calendar, depending on who you befriend.
findings.recommendation: Add the player's partner (stage >= 1) and spouse to meta.guests at runtime in SocialManager.festival_roster (the wedding already appends a dynamic `first`). Optionally add the top 2-3 highest-hearts friends from the other town as guests, within the 20-visual cap.
findings.verification: confirmed: festival_roster pools only home_area == meta.area, and the guests are the ghost family (social_data.gd:285-300; social_manager.gd:886-895 adds no partner or spouse). There are 4 hyggebyen festivals (blomsterfesten, honningdagen, maanemarkedet, bagedagen). The dance (festival_stage.gd:156-161) picks the highest-hearts citizen present from the roster. Only bryllupsfesten injects the partner (relationship_flow.gd wedding_definition sets meta.first). The partner home areas match npcs.lua. This is a valid design opinion and accurately stated.

findings.title: The ghost-family lost-property errand can only be finished through the gift system, so it is blocked by the weekly gift limit
evidence: scripts/ghostfam/quests/family_quests.gd:49-56 - the errand only completes on the game_event gift_given for the chosen owner and item
scripts/social/gifts/gift_flow.gd:123-128 - refuses with reason 'today'/'week' when gifts.per_day 1 / per_week 2 are used up (lua/social/social.lua gifts)
lua/quests/ghostfam_hittegods.lua - repeatable, cooldown_days = 7; the owners (oak, pippin, lily, brumme, sofus, ugle) are popular gift targets
findings.description: Handing the owner their lost item counts as a normal gift. If the player has already gifted that owner twice this week (or once today), the return is refused with the weekly gift-limit message, and the errand cannot be finished until the limit resets. It also uses up one of the player's gift slots and awards taste points as if it were a present.
findings.player_impact: A child who gifts their favourite NPC and then takes the lost-property errand gets a confusing 'you've given enough gifts' refusal with no hint that the errand needs to wait.
findings.recommendation: In GiftFlow.give_gift, skip the day/week limits (and the weekly ledger) when GhostFamilyQuests reports a pending return for this npc+item (e.g. a static is_return(npc, item)). Alternatively, add a dedicated 'Aflever hittegods' dialogue choice (like the seek card) that calls QuestManager.complete_manual directly.
findings.verification: confirmed: family_quests.gd:49-56 completes the errand only on gift_given with the matching owner and item. GiftFlow.give_gift (gift_flow.gd:123-128) refuses with 'today' when per_day 1 is used up, and with 'week' when per_week 2 is used up (social.lua:27-29); the week limit is skipped on a birthday. The lost items are ordinary goods (apple, cookie, wild_flower, rope, honey; lua/config/ghostfam_quests.lua). They are not protected, because item_in_use only checks have/needs/recipe objectives and the 'return' objective is on=manual. The return therefore also takes a gift slot and gives taste points. The quest has no deadline, so the player is only delayed until the limit resets, not blocked. P3 is right.

findings.title: The pass-out's day-end autosave captures the 02:00 moment before waking, not the morning
evidence: scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:479-482 each roll sets hour = restart (02:00) and then _roll_day; :527-531 day_ended is emitted, then midnight_passed
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:262-274 the day_ended autosave is deferred only to the end of the same frame
scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd:698-711 the pass-out awaits a 0.7 s fade before GameManager.sleep_until_morning() and the _enter(wake area)
scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd:502-508 the pass-out branch of sleep_until_morning sets 06:00 without day_ended, so no save follows the wake-up; save_manager.gd:247 the save resets the 300 s timer
findings.description: For the bed, end_day sets 06:00 before the deferred autosave runs, so the auto slot holds the morning at home. For a pass-out, the deferred save runs in the same frame as the roll, before the 0.7 s fade, the jump to 06:00 and the move to farm:from_home. The auto slot therefore holds raw hour 2 at the spot where the player collapsed, for example inside a shop or in the street, and it is not refreshed for 300 real seconds. A Continue in that window (after a crash, or after the window close that does not save) wakes the player at 02:00 in the dark at the collapse spot, awake, with 4 extra hours before the day's 26:00 end.
findings.player_impact: Rare but confusing: after Continue the player is standing in a dark closed shop at 02:00 instead of waking at home.
findings.recommendation: In world_2d.gd _sleep_sequence, after _restore_player(), call SaveManager.autosave() when passed_out is true (as _on_player_defeated does at :788-789). Or have _run_queued_autosave skip while world.sleeping is true and re-queue it at the end of the sleep sequence.
findings.dim: Core loop, time, energy, heroes, save/load

findings.title: On Windows, startup deletes stale .tmp saves, which can remove the only good copy after an interrupted replace
evidence: scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:1006-1007 replace uses DirAccess.rename_absolute(temp, target)
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:150 and :941-944 `_remove_stale_temp_files()` deletes every *.tmp in user://saves at startup without checking it
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:6 'the auto slot has no backup'
findings.description: On POSIX (macOS) the rename is atomic. Godot's Windows DirAccess.rename removes an existing destination before _wrename (engine behaviour, not tested here). A crash or power loss between those two steps leaves save_auto.json missing and a fully verified save_auto.json.tmp on disk. At the next start, _remove_stale_temp_files deletes that .tmp, so the auto slot, which has no .bak, is lost. Windows is a release target.
findings.player_impact: Rare but total loss of the autosave (and therefore of Continue) after a badly timed crash on Windows.
findings.recommendation: In _remove_stale_temp_files, when the matching primary is missing (or fails _read_json_file and validate_payload) and the .tmp validates, rename the .tmp to the primary instead of deleting it. Optionally give the auto slot the same .bak rotation as the manual slots.
findings.dim: Core loop, time, energy, heroes, save/load
findings.verification: confirmed: The code facts are confirmed. _write_atomic writes .tmp, reads it back, then calls _replace_file, which is DirAccess.rename_absolute (save_manager.gd ~:990-1010). _remove_stale_temp_files deletes every *.tmp at _ready without validating it (:941-944; called at :150). The header confirms that the auto slot has no backup. The Windows remove-then-_wrename behaviour is engine-side and was not verified against 4.7 here, as the finding itself hedges. The window is tiny (between two syscalls), but the outcome is the loss of the auto slot, so P3 tech-debt is appropriate.

scripts/autoload/quest_manager.gd:633-648 claim_rewards keeps any item that fails can_add_item in pending_rewards and retries it forever; no duplicate sale
lua/quests/fix_roof.lua:38 hat_chef_white (also sold in tailor rotation, home_shops.lua:154, and found in skovkant/dybe_bregner)
lua/quests/ghostfam_garn.lua:26-28 shirt_knit_blue (tailor rotation, dungeon find)
lua/quests/lost_cat.lua:58 hat_cat_ears (rare dungeon pool in dybe_bregner and skovkant)
lua/dialogue/ghostfam_dyne.lua:23 api.add_item('shirt_knit_cream', 1) (normal, tailor fixed stock)
lua/data/loot_tables.lua duplicates = {action = 'sell', message_key = FIND_UI_DUPLICATE_FMT}, which applies only to the loot path
findings.description: If the player bought or found one of these garments before finishing the quest or kin scene, the reward can never be delivered. It sits in the save's pending_rewards, is retried on every inventory change and load, and gives no gold or message. Loot duplicates, by contrast, are auto-sold with a toast.
findings.player_impact: A promised reward visibly fails to arrive, with no explanation and no compensation.
findings.recommendation: In QuestManager.claim_rewards (and the Lua add_item API), apply the loot duplicate rule: when the item is clothing, or a one-of-a-kind piece already owned, pay sell_price and post FIND_UI_DUPLICATE_FMT, then clear it from owed. Alternatively, swap these four rewards for pieces that can only come from that quest.
findings.verification: confirmed: WardrobeManager.can_add requires count_total(id)==0 (wardrobe_manager.gd:39-40). EconomyManager.can_add_item routes clothing to that store (economy_manager.gd:265-275). QuestManager.claim_rewards (quest_manager.gd:633-648) skips items that fail can_add_item and keeps them in pending_rewards, retrying on inventory change and load (:651-660), with no gold and no message. The quest_rewards.gd resolver has no duplicate handling. Rewards verified: fix_roof.lua:38 hat_chef_white (also in tailor pool lua/shops/home_shops.lua:154 and loot pools loot_tables.lua:249/:367); ghostfam_garn shirt_knit_blue (home_shops:154, loot :374/:601); lost_cat.lua:58 hat_cat_ears (loot :255/:386). The dialogue path is worse: ghostfam_dyne.lua:23 api.add_item goes to lua_runtime.gd:298-301, which calls EconomyManager.add_item and ignores the false result, so it is never retried. Minor nuance: a quest reward is delivered later if the player ever sells or loses their copy, so 'lost forever' holds only while the copy is kept. The loot duplicates rule (loot_tables.lua:12) applies only to LootService. loot_tables.lua:835-844 quest_rewards lists these as quest rewards but is not used to exclude them from shops or loot.

findings.title: The 'two best sets' wardrobe cap is applied per perk kind, so three sets can count at once
evidence: lua/data/wardrobe_rules.lua:3,24 'at most this many outfit sets give a bonus at the same time (the two best)', max_sets_counted = 2
scripts/wardrobe/wardrobe_manager.gd:133-142 gear_points takes the top-2 bonus VALUES separately for each kind across all active sets
findings.description: Example of a legal outfit: earrings_glowcap + shoes_slippers_pompom (svampesamleren 2), bracelet_string + hat_chef_white (bageren 2), and necklace_dewdrop + pants_trousers_moss + shirt_knit_thornberry (nattevandreren 3). That is three active sets. Luck takes .01 + .01 (svamp + natte), discount .01 (bageren) and speed .01 (natte), so all three sets contribute, not two.

findings.recommendation: Rank the sets once, by total bonus or by a priority, and take the best max_sets_counted sets. Then sum their bonuses per kind.
findings.verification: confirmed: wardrobe_manager.gd:133-142 maps set_bonuses() to one value per kind, sorts, and takes the top max_sets_counted (2) for each kind independently. Perks.gear (perks.gd:8, :105) uses gear_points directly. The example outfit is legal: 7 distinct slots, no exclusions. Set definitions in lua/data/sets.lua: svampesamleren 2 pieces gives luck .01; bageren 2 pieces (bracelet_string, hat_chef_white) gives discount .01; nattevandreren 3 pieces (necklace_dewdrop, pants_trousers_moss, shirt_knit_thornberry) gives luck .01 and speed .01. findings.title: Toasts posted while a modal is open expire unseen (quest accepted/completed, hotbar assignment, crafting)
evidence: scripts/ui/hud.gd:58 - `EventBus.modal_changed.connect(func(_stack): toasts.visible = not GameManager.is_modal_open())`
scripts/ui/forest_hud.gd:151 - same hide-while-modal rule for the forest stack
scripts/ui/components/notification_toast.gd:46-50 - each toast runs its own 0.15 s + 4 s + 0.4 s tween and then calls queue_free, with no pause while hidden
scenes/ui/hud.tscn:670 - ToastStack `process_mode = 3` (ALWAYS), so the tween keeps running behind modals and pause
scripts/autoload/quest_manager.gd:475-479 (NOTIF_QUEST_ACCEPTED) and :601-605 (NOTIF_QUEST_COMPLETED) fire during dialogue; scripts/ui/dialogue_ui.gd:24 `modal_name = &"dialogue"`
scripts/ui/inventory_ui.gd:223 - STORE_ASSIGNED toast is posted from inside the backpack (inventory_ui.gd:21 `modal_name = &"inventory"`)
scripts/ui/components/workshop_panel.gd:134 - WORKSHOP_CRAFTED toast is posted from inside a modal panel
tests/sections/hud.gd - no check covers a toast posted under a modal
findings.description: Both HUD toast stacks are hidden whenever any modal is open, but each toast's 4.55 s lifetime keeps running while it is hidden. Many important notifications are posted while a modal is open: accepting a quest from a dialogue choice, completing a quest during the turn-in conversation (together with its reward/item toasts), assigning a hotbar slot from the backpack, and crafting at a workshop. If the player stays in the modal for more than about 4.5 s, which is normal with typewriter dialogue or browsing the backpack, the toast is created and destroyed without ever being visible.
findings.player_impact: The player often misses 'Ny opgave!', 'Opgave fuldført' and the reward and confirmation feedback. The hotbar-assign confirmation from the backpack is effectively never seen. A 10-year-old target player gets no confirmation that a quest started or paid out.
findings.recommendation: In ToastStack, hold new entries in `_queue` while `not is_visible_in_tree()` and drain it on `visibility_changed`. Alternatively, start the toast tween only when the toast first becomes visible, or pause it with `_tween.set_paused(true)` while hidden. Another option is to give quest and item toasts their own CanvasLayer above the modals. Add a test `hud.toast_survives_modal`: push_modal, post, wait 5 s, pop_modal, then assert the toast is visible.
findings.verification: partly: The mechanism is real. hud.gd:58 and forest_hud.gd:151 hide the stack while any modal is open. ToastStack sets PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS (toast_stack.gd _init). Each toast's tween (notification_toast.gd:46-50) keeps running while hidden and then calls queue_free; nothing queues or pauses it (the _queue is used only for fifo overflow). The headline examples are wrong, though. NPC dialogue quest accept and turn-in run AFTER the dialogue modal has closed: dialogue_ui.gd _finish calls super.close() before session_finished.emit (lines ~181-193), and npc_2d.gd:233-242 calls NpcDialogue.action only after await _page/_end_talk (npc_dialogue.gd:70 says 'Called after the dialogue's modal has ended'). The journal accept_quest calls (quest_journal.gd:233/259) are fixture-only. Toasts that really are posted under a modal: the hotbar-assign toast (inventory_ui.gd:223), the workshop craft toast (workshop_panel.gd:134, hosted in inventory_ui.tscn), shop-side EconomyManager 'no gold' and 'inventory full' toasts, and any quest auto-completion triggered from inside a modal (QuestManager._check_completion via recipe_crafted/item_gained, quest_manager.gd:166/154/708). In most of these cases the modal itself shows the result (the hotbar or recipe status refreshes, and shop rows are disabled when unaffordable), so the impact is lower than described.

findings.description: The forest HUD stacks three widgets in the same top-centre band: the boss bar (y 40-94), the toast stack (from y 96) and the floor-arrival banner (y 120-200). On the first entry to a new zone (floor 1, 7 and 10) the zone-unlock toast and the floor banner fire together, and the toast covers 'Etage N'. During boss fights any toast lands between the boss bar and the arena, where telegraphs need to be read.

findings.recommendation: In the forest HUD, move the toast stack out of the centre: either right-aligned under the loot feed (anchor right, offset_top about 262 + feed height), or bottom-left above the whisper (offset_bottom -110). Alternatively, defer forest toasts while `floor_banner.visible` or `boss_box.visible`. Add a dungeon_hud check that the toast rect does not intersect floor_banner or boss_box.
findings.verification: partly: The floor-banner overlap is confirmed. The toast stack starts at offset_top 96 (toast_stack.tscn), floor_banner sits at (400,120) 480x80 (forest_hud.gd:98-101), and the toasts are added later, so they draw on top. unlock_zone posts NOTIF_ZONE_UNLOCKED on area entry (world_2d.gd:478, game_manager.gd:448). pass3_dungeon_f1_hud.png shows the 'Nyt område!' toast covering the 'Etage 1' title with only the 'Mørkeskoven' subtitle visible. This only happens on the first entry of each zone. The boss-fight part is weakly evidenced: the two toasts in bosses_boss_telegraph_shot.png ('Tilbage fra skoven', 'Skovens hjerte vokser ×3') are leftovers from a test sequence. The forest stack has item_toasts=false, so few toasts actually fire mid-fight. The geometry (boss_box y 40-94 right above the toast lane) is correct. Downgraded to polish because the overlap is transient and only on first zone entry.

findings.title: HUD text is as small as 10-14 px at 720p with no text-size setting
evidence: scenes/ui/hud.tscn theme - HotkeyDigit font_size 10 (slot digits), HudDateLine font_size 14 IBM Plex Mono (weekday · clock · weather)
scripts/ui/hud.gd:141 - the clock lives in that 14 px line
scripts/ui/settings_ui.gd:109,114,126 - the only stored settings are audio, fullscreen and window size; there is no text or UI scale and no key rebinding
project.godot:42-45 - base 1280x720, stretch canvas_items (720p is the native size)
Style Guide text: 'Tal i Caprasimo … Penge, tid og antal står altid i display-skriften' and 'Kun i store størrelser, aldrig under 20 px'; 'Æ, ø og å står tydeligt ved 18 px'
pass3_farm_day_hud.png - the time '10:00' is the smallest text in the top-left chip; the tiny ability placeholders in pass3_dungeon_f1_hud.png
findings.description: The owner chose the Miljøer v2 HUD, so the time sits in 14 px mono and the slot digits in 10 px. This conflicts with the style guide's own numerals rule. At the default 1280x720 window these sizes are rendered at native pixels. The clock is the most-glanced value of a time-pressured day and the smallest text on the HUD. The game offers no text-size or UI-scale option to compensate.
findings.player_impact: Children and players on laptop screens or from the couch will struggle to read the time and the slot numbers. That matters most in the late hours before the 02:00 pass-out, which has no other on-HUD warning (CLOCK_26 Q7 chose no nudge).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Tekststørrelse' setting (Normal / Stor / Ekstra stor) that sets `get_tree().root.content_scale_factor` (1.0 / 1.15 / 1.3), or a theme default_font_size multiplier. Within the sketch layout, raise HudDateLine to 16 px and HotkeyDigit to 12 px. Record the guide-vs-sketch numerals conflict as resolved in UI_NAVIGATION.md.
findings.verification: partly: The facts are accurate. hud.tscn:99 sets HotkeyDigit to 10 px and hud.tscn:103 sets HudDateLine to 14 px. settings_ui.gd only stores audio (109), fullscreen (114) and window size (126): there is no text or UI scale and no rebinding. The base is 1280x720 canvas_items (project.godot) and the default is windowed at size index 0 (settings_ui.gd:67-72). The guide's 'Tal i Caprasimo' and 'aldrig under 20 px' rule is quoted correctly (Style Guide.dc.html:67,417). However, the 14 px IBM Plex Mono date line is exactly what the owner-chosen Miljøer v2 sketch specifies ('font-size:14px' on 'Tirsdag · 10:20 · Solskin'). canvas_items stretch also scales everything up in fullscreen or larger window sizes (1.5x at 1080p), so a workaround exists. This is valid accessibility polish, not a P2.

findings.title: Rarity (an owner requirement) is shown inconsistently across panels
evidence: Text rarity name only in the backpack: inventory_ui.gd:135-136 %DetailRarity.
The shop detail shows only the tile (shop_ui.gd:257-258). The scene defines CatalogRarity_* label styles (shop_ui.tscn:43-52), but the script never sets a rarity label.
Garderobe _select (garderobe.gd:397-) shows name, description and status, but no rarity.
Indretning drawer rows (indretning_ui.gd:113-117) and the home chest list rows (home_chest_ui.gd:64-68) have no rarity tile or name at all.
findings.description: Five rarity tiers are central to furniture, clothing and weapons. They appear as a coloured tile plus pips in the shop, gift and garderobe grids, as a named label only in the backpack, and not at all in the furniture drawer and chest lists, even though Indretning filters by rarity.
findings.player_impact: Players can't tell what a 'Sjælden' or 'Unik' piece is where it matters most (decorating, wardrobe), and colour-only tiles are hard for colour-blind players.
findings.recommendation: Add the RARITY_* name line, styled CatalogRarity_<r>, to the shop, garderobe and gift details. Use RaritySlot (tile plus pips) in the Indretning and chest rows.
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. inventory_ui.gd:135-136 is the only detail that sets a RARITY_* name with a CatalogRarity_* style. shop_ui.gd:257-258 sets only the DetailIcon rarity, although shop_ui.tscn:43-52 defines CatalogRarity_* styles that the script never uses. garderobe.gd _select (:397-414) sets name, description, stats and buttons but no rarity. indretning_ui.gd:113-117 and home_chest_ui.gd:64-68 rows have no rarity tile or name. shop_item_row.gd:62 does set a rarity tile on list rows.

findings.description: Numbers are formatted with GDScript defaults, so Danish screens show English decimal points next to Danish thousands points. Requirement lines skip Fmt.thousands. Count strings have no singular form, giving '+1 hjerter', 'om 1 dage' and 'Alder 1 dage'. Recipes join a number with a capitalised singular item name.
findings.player_impact: Stats are hard to read and look buggy. Frequent toasts such as '+1 hjerter' and 'om 1 dage' are ungrammatical for Danish readers learning to read.
findings.recommendation: Add Fmt.decimal(x, 1), which uses ',' in da, and use it in equipment_details/forest_hud and the WEFFECT/GEMFX rows (pass the pre-formatted string as %s). Route every gold or amount in build_menu_ui/husbyggeri through Fmt.thousands. Add a plural helper that tries KEY_ONE when n == 1 (e.g. REL_GIFT_HEARTS_ONE '+1 hjerte', HUD_CONSTRUCTION_ONE 'færdigt i morgen'). Change WORKSHOP_MISSING to 'Mangler: %s × %d' and the toast to '×'.

findings.description: The lints check structure, not language. A handful of visible rows have wrong gender agreement, wrong possessive, misspelled compounds, an intransitive verb used transitively, an imperative where a description is needed, and a split compound in the King's title. Legacy da.csv toasts (gained item, zone unlocked, wrong food) read as literal translations. TimeManager.date_text capitalises the weekday, which is wrong mid-sentence in Danish.

findings.title: Mother-story climax exceeds length budgets and reading level; the length lint does not cover FM_/SG_/FEST_ rows
evidence: localization/forest_mother.csv:67 FM_E_MOTHER_FATE_TEXT = 259 chars; :71 FM_FINAL_TRUTH = 256 chars (STYLE_SHEET R2: dialogue page ≤ 240)
scripts/world2d/story/mother_evidence_marker.gd:109 - FM_FINAL_TRUTH is shown as a dialogue page
tools/copy/copy_lint.py slot_of() - only DLG_/DIALOGUE_/SOC_ keys get the 240-char check, so FM_, SG_, FEST_ and GHOSTFAM rows are unchecked
Vocabulary: forest_mother.csv:67 'uafsluttede fortællinger', 'beretning', 'ekko, ikke som en levende fange', 'afviste at overtage rollen'; :72 'Rodskriveren … titlen Vejholderen'
Narrator shift: :67 'Vi gav hende hendes egen underskrift tilbage' (first-person plural) vs :69 'Du planter…' (second person)
10 rows use ';' (e.g. :35, :47, :65, :115) - semicolons are hard for young readers
findings.description: The emotional peak of the main story is the densest, most abstract copy in the game, and the longest pages slip past the R2 budget because the lint's slot detection ignores story families. The voice also switches between 'vi' and 'du' inside the evidence journal.
findings.player_impact: Young players may not understand what happened to their mother at the payoff moment, which weakens the strongest part of the game.
findings.recommendation: Split FM_E_MOTHER_FATE_TEXT and FM_FINAL_TRUTH into two pages each of ≤ 2 short sentences. Replace the abstract nouns with concrete ones ('Mor hjalp de fortabte hjem. Det kostede hende livet.'). Use 'du' consistently. Replace semicolons with full stops. Extend copy_lint.py slot_of() so any row shown via dialogue_ui (FM_, SG_, FEST_*_OPEN/END, DLG_GHOSTFAM_) gets the dialogue limit.
findings.verification: confirmed: Measured: FM_E_MOTHER_FATE_TEXT is 259 chars and FM_FINAL_TRUTH 256 chars (FM_FINAL_BARGAIN 208). STYLE_SHEET.md:25 sets the dialogue page limit at ≤240. mother_evidence_marker.gd _lines() shows FM_FINAL_TRUTH as a dialogue page. copy_lint.py:64-69 slot_of only maps DLG_/DIALOGUE_/SOC_ to the dialogue slot, so FM_ rows are unchecked. 'Vi gav hende…' at :67 vs 'du' elsewhere is confirmed. Semicolon rows counted at 9 (lines 18,35,47,57,65,73,83,115,116), not 10; minor.

findings.title: Bosses have three different story framings and are never named in the mother story; snurresvampen does not count earlier victories
evidence: localization/forest_mother.csv:31-33 FM_OBJ_CHECKPOINT_S0x "Åbn det første/andet/sidste dybdepunkt"; :99-101 FM_LEAD_CHECKPOINT_* "Gå gennem dybdepunktet… En tidligere sejr gælder stadig."
localization/dungeon_services.csv:43-49 bossernes_vej: "skovens tre svampevogtere", Overvind Snurresvampen/Glødesvampen/Svampekongen
localization/features_quests.csv:9-10 snurresvampen: "Larmen fra Dybe Bregner… få Snurresvampen til at holde op"
lua/quests/snurresvampen.lua:16-21 defeat_snurresvampen has no completed_flag (bossernes_vej.lua:11,19,27 has one)
lua/quests/snurresvampen.lua:46 / home_tiers.lua:282 snurresvampen gates home tier 8
findings.description: The same three fights are called 'depth checkpoints' in the main story, 'guardians' in Oak's road quest, and 'a racket to stop' in the tier 8 gate. The mother story never says that a 'dybdepunkt' is a boss. Its climax is fighting Svampekongen, who has no connection to the Root Scribe or to Mum, and the story's word for him is vague. Also, bossernes_vej and the mother chapters count earlier victories, but snurresvampen (home tier 8 gate, offered only after the first forest visit) does not. A player who already beat the floor-4 boss for S03 has to beat it again.
findings.player_impact: Children may not understand what 'Åbn det første dybdepunkt' asks for, and the hardest fights carry no story weight. Being made to repeat a boss for tier 8 contradicts 'En tidligere sejr gælder stadig'.
findings.recommendation: Name the boss in the checkpoint text ('Overvind Snurresvampen, som vogter dybdepunktet på etage 4'). Add a one-line story hook on the Svampekongen kill (for example the crown's rune shard opening Rodskriverens ramme, which fits ITEM_DNG_RUNE_KONGE_HINT). Add completed_flag = "dungeon_boss_snurresvamp" to snurresvampen.lua's defeat objective.
findings.verification: confirmed: FM_OBJ_CHECKPOINT_S03/05/07 (forest_mother.csv:31-33) and FM_LEAD_CHECKPOINT_* (:99-101) use 'dybdepunkt'. rg finds no 'svamp', 'vogter' or 'boss' anywhere in forest_mother.csv, and 'dybdepunkt' appears in no other file. bossernes_vej copy (dungeon_services.csv:43-49) says 'svampevogtere'; snurresvampen (features_quests.csv:9-10) says 'Larmen… holde op'. snurresvampen.lua:16-21 defeat_snurresvampen has no completed_flag, whereas bossernes_vej.lua:11 uses completed_flag dungeon_boss_snurresvamp. requires_zone dark_forest is set. Bosses reset daily (done cells are cleared in _clear_day, dungeon_floors.gd:74-79), so the re-fight is possible: this is redundancy, not a softlock. P3 is right.

findings.title: Small contradictions in clue text: where the letter is, what Pip said, wick vs stitches, lygte vs lampe
evidence: localization/secret_garden.csv:34 SG_SCENE_SEE_BLOSSOMS letter lies "Mellem bladene"; :36 OBJ "Læs brevet i frøkassen"; forest_mother.csv:35 FM_E_LETTER_WATERMARK_TEXT "i havens frøkurv" (title 'Brevet i frøkurven')
secret_garden.csv:60 Pip: "Frøkassen kom op med Skovliften, men brevet må være ældre" vs forest_mother.csv:37 FM_E_POST_ROUTE_TEXT "Brevet kom gennem skovposten"
forest_mother.csv:117 FM_WORK_LAMP "Bind hvert sting… så lampen kan lyse" vs :47 FM_E_MEMORY_LAMP_TEXT "Du retter vægen og lukker glasset"
forest_mother.csv:41 FM_E_GARDEN_TRAIL_TEXT "Sporet ved frøkassen" uses 'frøkassen' for the Skovkanten box too
findings.description: The same letter is found in three places (among the leaves, in the seed box, in the seed basket). The journal summary of Pip's account says the opposite of what Pip actually said. The S04 lamp task has the player tie stitches, but the recorded memory describes straightening a wick and closing the glass. Within one chapter 'lampe' and 'lygte' are mixed. 'Frøkassen' means both the garden box and the forest-edge box.
findings.player_impact: Small trust breaks in a clue-reading game, where children compare journal entries with what they did.
findings.recommendation: Settle on 'frøkassen' (garden) and 'kassen ved Skovkanten' (forest). Rename FM_E_LETTER_WATERMARK to '…i havens frøkasse'. Rewrite FM_E_POST_ROUTE_TEXT to match Pip ('Kassen kom op med liften; brevet er ældre end turen'). Make FM_E_MEMORY_LAMP_TEXT start with 'Du binder de tre sting…'. Use 'lygte' throughout.
findings.verification: partly: Letter location is confirmed in three phrasings: secret_garden.csv:34 'Mellem bladene', :36 'i frøkassen', and SG_COMPLETE :55 'i frøkassen', against forest_mother.csv:34-35 'frøkurven' / 'frøkurv'. The lamp is confirmed: FM_WORK_LAMP (:117) is about tying stitches 'så lampen kan lyse', while FM_E_MEMORY_LAMP_TEXT (:47) says 'Du retter vægen og lukker glasset'; titles and texts use 'Lygten'. FM_E_GARDEN_TRAIL_TEXT (:41) calls the Skovkanten box 'frøkassen', where Oak calls it 'En kasse med tre lyse sting… ved Skovkanten'. Overstated: Pip's line (secret_garden.csv:60) 'Frøkassen kom op med Skovliften, men brevet må være ældre' does not contradict FM_E_POST_ROUTE_TEXT 'Brevet kom gennem skovposten'. The journal adds a 'forest post' claim Pip never makes, which is an embellishment or inconsistency, not 'the opposite'.

findings.title: Lore wording: 'mennesker' in a world with no humans; ghost-specific line shown to every race; 'Mor Silke' clashes with 'Mors spor'
evidence: localization/forest_mother.csv:51,53,63,67,125 'menneske(r)' 5 times; rg finds the word in no other localization file
forest_mother.csv:71 FM_FINAL_TRUTH "Heller ikke Natlys-familiens spøgelser kan hente hende tilbage" shown to every race (mother_evidence_marker.gd:108-110)
localization/ghostfamily.csv:5 NPC_GHOSTFAM_SILKE "Mor Silke"; docs/copy/GLOSSARY.md:39; forest_mother.csv:2,9 FM_NAME/FM_TAB "Mors spor"; FM_FAMILY_KIN :76 "Din mor var … Silkes søskende"
findings.description: The cast is foxes, fairies, hobbits and ghosts, but the main story alone talks about 'mennesker' (Mum's motto 'Et menneske er mere end den rolle…'). The finale's ghost-specific reassurance also appears for a fox hero, whose mother has nothing to do with the Natlys ghosts. Silke's name tag 'Mor Silke' ('Mum Silke') appears in dialogue next to a tab called 'Mors spor'. For a ghost hero, Silke is the aunt, which is confusing.
findings.player_impact: Small immersion breaks, and real confusion for young readers about which 'Mor' is meant.
findings.recommendation: Use 'nogen', 'folk' or 'væsner' ('Man er mere end den rolle, nogen giver én'). Show the Natlys sentence only when character_type == GHOST, or reword it for everyone ('Ingen magi kan hente hende tilbage'). Rename Silke's tag to 'Silke' or 'Natvagten Silke' in ghostfamily.csv and the GLOSSARY.
findings.verification: confirmed: 'menneske(r)' appears in forest_mother.csv rows 51, 53, 63, 67 and 125, and rg finds it in no other localization file. FM_FINAL_TRUTH (:71) contains the Natlys-ghosts sentence, and mother_evidence_marker.gd:107-108 (_lines for mother_fate) has no race branch, so every hero sees it. NPC_GHOSTFAM_SILKE is 'Mor Silke' (ghostfamily.csv:5, GLOSSARY.md:39), used as the speaker name in ghostfam_silke.lua. FM_NAME/FM_TAB are 'Mors spor' (:2, :9). FM_FAMILY_KIN is at :77, not :76, and makes Silke the ghost hero's aunt. The names follow Blund's point of view ('Mormor Dyne' happens to also fit the hero), so 'Mor Silke' next to 'Mors spor' is a fair confusion point.

findings.title: The fairy king's first in-person meeting skips the welcome and asks a question that cannot be accepted
evidence: lua/dialogue/fairy_king.lua:89-115 when moonstone_crown is not done, the page is QUEST_MOONSTONE_CROWN_OFFER with a quest_accept choice
lua/quests/moonstone_crown.lua:39 requires_zone = "dark_forest"
scripts/world2d/npc_dialogue.gd:52 non-offerable quest_accept choices are removed
localization/features_quests.csv:7 "Åh, kære hjælper! Min krone mangler sin månesten. Vil du lede efter en i Mørkeskoven?"
findings.description: The king who drew the hero's name never welcomes them in person. Before the first forest visit, his conversation is the moonstone request ('Vil du lede efter en…?'), and the only button left is 'Farvel', because the accept choice is filtered out. He calls the hero 'kære hjælper' before they have helped with anything.
findings.player_impact: The figure behind the whole premise is a puzzling dead end at first meeting.
findings.recommendation: Add a first-meet or pre-forest branch to fairy_king.lua ('Så er det dig, der vandt! Hvordan trives gården?'), and only show moon_offer when context.quest_offer_moonstone_crown is true, the same way guard_oak.lua handles its offers.
findings.verification: partly: Real issue: before the first forest visit, fairy_king.lua:89-115 returns the moon_offer page ('Åh, kære hjælper!… Vil du lede efter en i Mørkeskoven?'). moonstone_crown has requires_zone = dark_forest (line 39), so npc_dialogue.gd:52 filters out its quest_accept choice, and the page asks a question it cannot accept. Factual errors: the king does welcome the hero in person. fairy_king has friendship = true (npcs.lua:124), so DialogueBridge.decorate (dialogue_bridge.gd:17-19) prepends SOC_FAIRY_KING_FIRST_1_V 'Velkommen. Dit nye hjem er begyndelsen på en god historie.' (social_talk.csv:274) on first meeting. Farvel is also not necessarily the only button: the bridge adds gift/topic/event choices when available (dialogue_bridge.gd:42-48). Remaining defect: the unanswerable question and the premature 'kære hjælper'.

evidence: localization/quests.csv:34-36 QUEST_ENCHANTED_GARDEN 'Den fortryllede have… kan vækkes med de rette frø' (mayor Lyra)
localization/secret_garden.csv:2,7-9 'Den hemmelige have' (Hoppe), also woken with moonflower-like seeds ('små månelyse blomster')
lua/quests/enchanted_garden.lua:66 sets enchanted_garden_unlocked; rg finds no reader

findings.title: Hero twin rule missing for Birk (and Kløvermynte): the player can meet an NPC with the same name and identical sprites
evidence: lua/config/characters.lua:69-76 - heroes include kloevermynte (skin fairy_meadow) and birk (skin fairy_birk)
localization/cast.csv:12 HERO_KLOEVERMYNTE_BLURB 'Driver frøbutikken i Hyggebyen…'; :15 HERO_BIRK_BLURB '… Passer bierne i Hyggebyen.' - the hero cards describe the NPCs' jobs
lua/routines/core/beekeeper_birk.lua:6-10 - no hero_twin, while lua/routines/ext/{rasmus,lamplighter_kiki,bertil,bodil}.lua all set it
scripts/towns/npc_director.gd:19 - the comment says the twins are 'rasmus, kiki, bertil, bodil, birk', but the data does not make Birk one
assets/isometric_characters/fairy_birk/idle.webp and fairy_birk_npc/idle.webp have the same md5 (4970e6ea…); hover, talk, interact and celebrate are identical too
localization/core.csv:21 NPC_MERCHANT_PIP 'Butiksfe Kløvermynte' - the seed-shop keeper has the same name as the default fairy hero
localization/dialogue_cast.csv DLG_BIRK_FAMILY 'Du ligner nogen fra min familie!' (shown to any fairy player)
findings.description: Design rule DT9 says a citizen who has the player's own look is absent while the player is that hero. It is enforced for Rasmus, Kiki, Bertil and Bodil but not Birk, even though the NPC Birk's idle, hover and talk sprites are byte-identical to the hero's. A fairy player who picks the 'Birk' card meets a second Birk at the hives. Their own hero card says that Birk keeps the bees. Picking 'Kløvermynte' leaves the seed-shop fairy Kløvermynte in place. She cannot be hidden, because she runs a shop.
findings.player_impact: Confusing identity for fairy players ('is that me?'). The NPC Birk can even be courted (partner = true), so the player can marry someone who looks exactly like them.
findings.recommendation: Add hero_twin = "birk" to lua/routines/core/beekeeper_birk.lua, and give the bee duties (Honningdagen host) a fallback. Or re-bake fairy_birk_npc with a distinct palette or outfit. For Kløvermynte, rename the hero card (e.g. 'Engfe', which already exists as SKIN_FAIRY_MEADOW) and rewrite HERO_KLOEVERMYNTE_BLURB and HERO_BIRK_BLURB so they describe the player's look, not an NPC's job. Correct the comment at npc_director.gd:19.
findings.dim: Side quests, NPC writing, cast consistency
findings.verification: partly: The main premise misreads the design. DT9 (docs/design/TOWNS_FARM_SOCIAL_ADDENDUM.md:975) says the twins are rasmus, lamplighter_kiki, bertil and bodil, and that 'Birk and Kløvermynte (also playable) are never absent'. Q3 (line 1512) accepts that 'a player who chose Kløvermynte meets her namesake'. GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM.md:101 repeats that the citizen twins are only those four. beekeeper_birk.lua:6-20 deliberately shows DLG_BIRK_FAMILY when context.race == 'fairy', as a sibling acknowledgement. So the missing hero_twin on Birk, and Kløvermynte staying in her shop, are both intended. What is real: (a) the fairy_birk and fairy_birk_npc idle, talk, hover, interact and celebrate webps are byte-identical (verified with md5; only the portrait differs). The work package (dungeon_v2_workpackages.json:442) specified a distinct male-fairy build for fairy_birk_npc, so the 'sibling' looks like a clone. (b) The npc_director.gd:19 comment wrongly lists birk as a twin. (c) HERO_KLOEVERMYNTE_BLURB (cast.csv:12) is a dev-facing note on a player card ('Samme grundfigur bruges, når spilleren vælger at være fe'), and both blurbs describe the NPCs' jobs. The fix is the art distinction plus copy, not hero_twin.

findings.prior_ref: mechanics-story-deep-dive-2026-10-18 S-H - the original instance is fixed; this one is still open
findings.dim: Side quests, NPC writing, cast consistency
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. social_talk.csv:218 SOC_GUARD_OAK_FIRST_1_V reads 'Jeg er Eg. Jeg passer på broen…', but guard_oak's routine posts him at traetoppen.b_lift (lua/routines/core/guard_oak.lua:13-18), not a bridge. social_talk.csv:210 has 'Jeg er Lilje' against NPC_FAIRY_LILY 'Fe-barnet Lily'. farm_site.csv:42 FARMSITE_SEED_GREETING says 'Pip har fyldt hylden…', and it is actually shown: there are no KEEP_GREENHOUSE_SEEDS_* keys, so greeting_for_shop falls back to greeting_key (social_talk.gd:129, shop_ui.gd:136-139), with keeper merchant_pip. findings.title: Cast collisions: three 'Pip's, two postmen, and a mouse with the halflings' surname
evidence: lua/config/npcs.lua - merchant_pip (shown as Kløvermynte), postman_pip (hedgehog Pip), pippin_boegeknop (mouse Pippin), penguin_postman (role postman, one line in lua/dialogue/penguin_postman.lua)

He shares the halfling family's surname without being related to them (family exclusion and dialogue never link them).
findings.player_impact: Confusion over who delivers the mail and who is related to whom. The Bøgeknop siblings could even be told apart from Pippin by the marriage-exclusion rule only by accident.
findings.recommendation: Rename the mouse's surname (e.g. 'Pippin Knapnål'), or add family = "boegeknop" plus one line acknowledging the link. Retire penguin_postman as a citizen (keep him as an ambient courier with friendship = false), or give him a distinct job. Fix the merchant_pip voice_key to voice/merchant_pip/greet. Correct the lost_cat.lua header to say Mis is Pippin's cat.
findings.dim: Side quests, NPC writing, cast consistency
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified. merchant_pip.lua:15 has voice_key 'voice/pip/greet', and DUNGEON_V2_ADDENDUM.md:531 says Pip's path is voice/postman_pip/, 'never voice/pip/'. Ghost heroes then also get localization/ghost_dialogue.csv:3 DLG_GHOST_KING_INTRO 'Et spøgelse! Hvor dejligt… Svæv bare ind, kagen står på bordet.', a letter reacting to seeing the reader (intro_sequence.gd:20-22)

tutorial_runner.gd:8 and :135-139: Esc, or closing any opening page, skips the whole sequence; :92 sets intro_letter_seen. FM_OPENING_LEAD is used nowhere else (rg finds only fairy_king.lua:14), so there is no reread in the journal
tests/sections/farm_first_morning.gd:186 pins escape_skips_whole_sequence
findings.description: Prior GM-06 is partly fixed: a mother lead now exists. But it is delivered as an afterthought in the King's letter, and the letter tells the player to travel to the home they are standing in. One Esc press, which children use a lot, removes both the lottery premise and the mother premise for good.
findings.player_impact: The player may never learn why they are searching or where to start (Hoppe and the garden), and ghost players get a nonsensical reaction.
findings.recommendation:
- Change the letter to 'Din nye gård er din nu…'.
- Give the mother lead its own speaker or a narrator name_key, or move it to Pip's goodbye.
- Make DLG_GHOST_KING_INTRO a P.S. written in the letter ('P.S. Jeg hører, du er et spøgelse…').
- Store the letter as a readable item or a journal 'Mors spor' intro entry, so a skip does not lose it, or let Esc skip only the walk animation and not the letter.
findings.prior_ref: GM-06 (game-mechanics-2026-10-17.md) - partially fixed; still open as described
findings.verification:
partly: These parts are accurate:
- dialogue.csv:21 letter 'Følg broen til dit nye hjem' is read on the farm (tutorial_runner.gd:38).
- fairy_king.lua:12-14 FM_OPENING_LEAD has no own speaker. intro_sequence.gd:20 shows all lines under name_key NPC_FAIRY_KING.

Overstated: 'permanently drops both premises'.
- After a skip, intro_lottery is still auto-accepted (tutorial_runner.gd:83-86). Its journal description, quests.csv:5, restates the lottery premise.

findings.title: Choices placed by line index break sentences in two and put a goodbye mid-scene (Lyra, Rosa, Brumme, Sofus, Thorin, Hoppe)
evidence: build_hearts.py:39: choice_at = 3 for 4/8 hearts and 1 for 6/10 hearts, regardless of content

localization/heart_events.csv:277-280 Rosa 10: 'De små husker ikke altid, hvem der gjorde hvad.' → player 'Vi mødes igen snart.' → 'Men de husker, hvordan det føltes…' (the 'Men…' continuation is cut by the player's goodbye)
heart_events.csv:53/56 Brumme 10: 'En god samling skal kunne give sig lidt.' → choice → 'Så holder den…'; :193/196 Sofus 10: '…fortjene en pause.' → choice → 'Og du behøver ikke…'

heart_events.csv:137-140 Lyra 10: 'Når vi står her, behøver jeg ikke være borgmester hele tiden.' → player 'Her er også plads til dig.' (said to the mayor in her own square) → '…Hyldeblomst, der er glad for dit besøg.'

heart_events.csv:229/232 Thorin 4: 'En hammer kan larme meget uden at gøre noget godt.' → 'Vis mig det hele.' / 'Lad os begynde her.' → 'Jeg prøver at huske forskellen. Du hjælper mig med det.' (non-sequitur); :5/8 Hoppe 4: '…brug for ro.' → 'Vis mig det hele.' → 'Du har også givet dig tid til at slå rødder her.'
findings.description: The shared choice labels were written without seeing the NPC lines, and they are inserted at a fixed index. In all ten 10-heart scenes the player can say 'Vi mødes igen snart.' (a farewell) after line 1. The NPC then carries on talking and hands over a gift. In four of those scenes, line 2 continues line 1's sentence ('Men…', 'Og…', 'Så…'), so the player's line interrupts it. Several 4-heart scenes answer 'Vis mig det hele.' with a line that responds to something else.
findings.player_impact: The dialogue reads as stitched together exactly at the emotional climax of each friendship, so the Danish writing comes across as machine-assembled.
findings.recommendation: Author choices per scene in hearts.json and let the author pick the insertion point (e.g. 'choice_after': 2). As a minimum, move the 10-heart choice to after line 2 and replace 'Vi mødes igen snart.' with a reply that fits a mid-scene beat. Re-review the four 'Vis mig det hele.' scenes (Thorin, Hoppe, Birk, Sofus 4). Add reply_key lines so each option gets its own NPC response.
findings.dim: Heart-event scenes and their runner: content, triggers, choices and payoff (10 NPCs, about 4,000 Lua lines, never read)
findings.verification: partly: The mechanism is real. build_hearts.py:38 sets choice_at = 3 for 4/8 hearts and 1 for 6/10 hearts, and the runner shows the choice right after the grouped lines. The CSV rows cited for Rosa (:277-280), Brumme (:53/56), Sofus (:193/196), Lyra (:137-140), Thorin (:229/232) and Hoppe (:5/8) all match. Correction: only 3 of the 10-heart scenes have line 2 continue line 1's sentence: Rosa 'Men…', Brumme 'Så…' and Sofus 'Og…'. The other 10_02 lines, e.g. Thorin 'Nu ved jeg…' and Birk 'Jeg bliver glad…', are standalone sentences, so 'four' is wrong. Birk 4_03→4_04 ('Jeg behøver ikke styre dem…' → choice → 'Jeg sørger bare for…') is a further 4-heart example of the same split. Severity: this is a dialogue-copy flow problem with no mechanical impact, so it falls under P3 copy polish rather than P2.

findings.title: Pending heart scenes cannot be discovered: scene titles are never shown and the People book's 'Klar til en snak' count is almost always 0
evidence: lua/events/hearts/*.lua meta.title_key (e.g. mayor_lyra.lua:12) and 40 HEART_*_TITLE rows in heart_events.csv: no script reads meta.title_key (searched scripts/social, scripts/ui/social, scripts/ui/social_events; event_overlay.gd shows only SOC_EV_SKIP_HINT)
social_manager.gd:1133 people_rows → events_ready(id), which requires world.area == meta.area (:1146-1149), hour:8-18 and at:<npc> (NPC live in the player's current area)
scripts/ui/social/people.gd:208 + localization/rel_ui.csv:20 'Oplevet: %d · Klar til en snak: %d'
No player-facing copy or docs/PLAYING.md text explains where or when scenes trigger (searched localization for 'på hjerte'/'øjeblik': only REL_TALK_EVENT and SOC_EV_*)
findings.description: The only cue for a ready scene is the rose ♥ bubble, visible when the player is already in the right area at the right time with the NPC on screen. The People book's 'Klar til en snak' count runs the same strict check, so opened from the farm or anywhere else it reports 0 even when the next scene only needs the player to walk into the bakery. The 40 hand-written scene titles ('Ovnen vågner', 'Et navn mellem venner'…) are dead strings: no title card, no memories list.
findings.player_impact: Players who rarely visit a given shop, area or time of day can miss scenes indefinitely without knowing they exist. The People book gives a misleading 'ready: 0'.
findings.recommendation: In people_rows, add an 'events_next' field that evaluates only hearts, after, once and cooldown (no area, at: or hour terms), and show it as 'Næste øjeblik: <tr(title_key)> · <area name>'. Show tr(meta.title_key) in the event overlay's top cinematic bar when a heart scene starts, and list seen titles in the People detail panel as memories.
findings.dim: Heart-event scenes and their runner: content, triggers, choices and payoff (10 NPCs, about 4,000 Lua lines, never read)
findings.verification: confirmed: No script reads meta.title_key. A grep for title_key in scripts/ finds only unrelated UI helpers (gift_picker, ui_confirm, area_banner). people_rows → events_ready (social_manager.gd:1133/1139-) requires world.area == meta.area, the after chain and cooldown, and then eval_when, which covers hour:8-18 and at:<npc> via the director's is_present. people.gd:208 shows REL_PEOPLE_EVENT_COUNT ('Oplevet: %d · Klar til en snak: %d', rel_ui.csv:20). The other cues are the npc_2d.gd:388 ♥ bubble and the talk option (social_talk.gd:137 / REL_TALK_EVENT), and both need the same strict check. 'Almost always 0' is slightly strong, since the count is non-zero when the book is opened in the right area while the NPC is present, but the substance holds.

findings.title: Staging: the player is never placed in the scene, and outdoor scenes teleport the NPC to a fixed mark far away on another platform level
evidence: build_hearts.py:38: the only positioning step is {'act':'stand','who':npc,'mark':author.mark,'facing':'S'}; no scene places or faces the player

data/towns/routes.json ground distances: Brumme's weekend post t_stall (level 3) → c_logs (level 2) = 1838; Hoppe t_fire_n/t_fire_s (level 3) → a_bench (level 0) = 3050/3405; u_terrace (level 4) → a_bench = 1934; Birk blossom_bench2 → bees1 = 962

lua/routines/core/carpenter_brumme.lua stall plan (weekday 5,6): t_stall 9.5-16, the widest window for his traetoppen scene, so the most likely trigger point is 1.8k units and one level away from c_logs

tests/sections/social_heart_content.gd:123 hand-places the player next to Hoppe ('world.player.global_position = actor.global_position+Vector2(110,55)') before the native capture, because the runner does not
event_runner.gd:189-194: stand/face use a fixed 'S' facing, not the player's position
findings.description: In interiors this works, because the player is at the talk cell in front of the counter and the NPC is put on the 'counter' post facing S. Outdoors, the NPC fades out where the player talked to him and reappears at a fixed mark, possibly on another tree-platform level. The camera follows the NPC, so two-person beats ('Vil du holde enden, mens jeg måler?') probably play with the player out of shot. This is inferred from the distances; I could not run the game to check the framing.
findings.player_impact: Scenes outdoors will likely feel like disembodied cutaways rather than shared moments. It is jarring when an NPC appears to vanish from a busy market stall.
findings.recommendation: Add a player 'stand' to the template at a per-NPC 'player_mark' authored in hearts.json, or teach the runner a 'stand who=player near=<npc>' that uses _clear_stage. For outdoor citizens, use a mark on the same level as the NPC's current post: e.g. use t_stall for Brumme on weekends, or stage his scene in int_brummes_vaerksted. Make 'face' accept 'target':'player'.
findings.dim: Heart-event scenes and their runner: content, triggers, choices and payoff (10 NPCs, about 4,000 Lua lines, never read)
findings.verification: confirmed: The template's only positioning is the NPC 'stand' at author.mark (build_hearts.py:37, cited as :38). npc_2d.gd:363-367 event_stand sets global_position directly, so the NPC teleports. _clear_stage only adjusts the point on the mark's own platform. Player2D.camera_focus moves the camera offset to the NPC and never moves the player. I recomputed the distances as euclidean distances on routes.json pos: t_stall→c_logs 1838 (level 3→2), t_fire_n/t_fire_s→a_bench 3050/3405 (3→0), u_terrace→a_bench 1934 (4→0), blossom_bench2→bees1 962. Birk's and Lyra's scenes disappear on rainy days for 3-4 weekdays a week. Nothing tells the player this (see the discoverability finding). findings.title: Heart-scene payoff is token-level and uneven (3 stone or 2 rope at 10 hearts); 8 of the 10 tier-A citizens give no friendship item at any level
evidence: lua/events/hearts/smith_thorin.lua:381-382 _h10 gives stone x3 (lua/items/resources.lua:24 sell 1); carpenter_brumme.lua:381-382 rope x2 (sell 2); mayor_lyra.lua:381-382 wild_flower x2 (sell 2); postman_pip.lua:381-382 apple x2 (sell 5)
By contrast gardener_hoppe.lua and merchant_pip.lua _h10 give moonflower (crops.lua:87 sell 180), and bathkeeper_sofus.lua honey_cake (sell 90)
tests/sections/social_heart_content.gd:41 asserts that heart-scene gifts are 'normal' or 'uncommon' rarity, a deliberate cap
lua/data/loot_tables.lua:812-819 friend gifts: only farmer_rosa (4 hearts) and baker_maja (5 hearts) among the 10 tier-A citizens have a heart-gated item
findings.description: The rarity cap is intentional (the addendum caps items at normal), but the gifts themselves read as random pantry items. Value varies up to 60x between NPCs at the same milestone. Thorin's best-friend gift (3 stone) is the same item he already hands out as his everyday 'sample' (citizens.lua: sample=stone). For 8 of the 10 citizens, nothing else in the game marks reaching 10 hearts: no furniture, clothing or recipe, even though the owner's pitch is built around collectible rarity-tier furniture and clothing.
findings.player_impact: Maxing a friendship feels anticlimactic, and some citizens look stingy next to others.
findings.recommendation: Keep the scene gifts small, but give the _h10 scene (or a loot_tables.lua gifts row at hearts=10) a personal keepsake for each tier-A citizen, e.g. a signature furniture or clothing piece in 'uncommon'/'rare' granted through LootService.check_friend_gifts, which allows keepsakes. Even out the in-scene gifts to a similar value band. Thorin's _h10 could give iron_ore or a smithing recipe instead of stone.
findings.dim: Heart-event scenes and their runner: content, triggers, choices and payoff (10 NPCs, about 4,000 Lua lines, never read)
findings.verification: confirmed: Verified from hearts.json. The _h10 gifts are: Thorin stone x3 (sell 1); his _h6 is also stone x3, and stone is his citizens.lua sample. Brumme gives rope x2 (sell 2), Lyra wild_flower x2 (sell 2) and postman apple x2 (sell 5). Hoppe and merchant_pip give moonflower (sell 180) and Sofus honey_cake (sell 90). 60x is right: 180 vs 3 stones worth 3. The test at :41 asserts 'normal'/'uncommon' rarity. The runner's _commit also drops any one-of-a-kind item, so scene gifts cannot be keepsakes; the recommendation to route keepsakes through check_friend_gifts (loot_service.gd:350) holds. loot_tables gifts: among tier-A citizens only farmer_rosa (4) and baker_maja (5) appear. No other heart-gated reward exists for the other 8: the friend_discount shops' keepers are tier-B fairies and pippin.
