findings.title: Section versions are handled inconsistently: most sections ignore "v", unknown sections are silently dropped, and furniture and wardrobe reject data only during apply, which bypasses the backup
evidence: scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:15-16, 26 - each section 'carries its own v' while PAYLOAD_VERSION stays 2, so the payload-level 'newer' check (678-679) never sees a section bump

Version written but never read in from_dict: home_manager.gd:708 vs 724-767; social_manager.gd:1359 vs 1368-1404; shop_system.gd:434 vs 438-461; economy_manager.gd:736 vs 741-799; quest_manager.gd:1204 ('v': 2) vs 1282-1310; game_manager.gd:568 ('version') vs 590-614; world_2d.gd:863 ('v': 1) vs 880-905; time_manager.gd:245-262 writes none
Rejected during validation (state 'corrupt', .bak tried): loot_service.gd:1063-1065, animal_husbandry.gd:817, dungeon_floors.gd:314

Rejected only during apply: wardrobe_manager.gd:168-169 and furniture_manager.gd:241-242 return false from from_dict for v != 1 or a wrong shape, and neither has validate_dict. inspect_slot therefore reports 'ok', get_latest_slot (445-456) picks the slot for Continue, load_game fails with 'apply' (300-302) without trying the .bak, and _roll_backup (1023) still treats the file as valid

save_manager.gd:682-698 - validation and apply only loop over registered entries: a payload key with no registered node (for example 'dungeon' when host_dungeon_floors() returns false, loot_service.gd:964-969) passes validation, is ignored on load and is missing from the next gather_payload (581-593)
findings.description: There is no single policy for section version skew. A save from a newer build with a bumped section is silently read with old code in 8 of 13 payload parts (12 sections plus world), rejected as 'corrupt' (not 'newer') in 3, and rejected only during apply in 2, which bypasses the backup. Sections the build does not know are silently lost on the next save. The codex review's suggestion to try the backup after an apply failure (codex-review.txt finding 1, fix note) is still not implemented.
findings.player_impact: Rare today because no section is past v1/v2. Once a section is bumped, though, a downgrade or a partially failing feature can quietly lose that feature's progress, or show 'Beskadiget' when the real reason is 'made by a newer version'. Continue keeps choosing a slot that cannot load.
findings.recommendation: Give every section a SECTION_VERSION and a pure validate_dict that returns a distinct 'newer' verdict. In validate_payload, map it to code 'version', so the slot becomes 'newer' and the .bak is not used, as already pinned by bak_not_used_for_newer_version. Add validate_dict to WardrobeManager and FurnitureManager mirroring their from_dict guards. Keep unknown top-level payload keys in a passthrough dict that gather_payload writes back. Add a test that bumps 'home'.v to 99 and asserts inspect_slot == &"newer".
findings.prior_ref: docs/reviews/codex-review.txt finding 1 (fix suggestion: 'Consider a backup attempt after an apply failure') - still open for apply-time rejections
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: confirmed: Counted the parts: 12 sections (6 core in CORE_SECTIONS at save_manager.gd:84-91, plus home, furniture, wardrobe, loot, dungeon and social, registered at home_manager.gd:74, furniture_manager.gd:19, wardrobe_manager.gd:14, loot_service.gd:102/980 and social_manager.gd:120), plus world, gives 13. validate_dict exists only for husbandry (816, which checks v <= SAVE_VERSION), loot (1063-1064), dungeon (314) and quests (1216, which does not check v). Wardrobe (wardrobe_manager.gd:168) and furniture (furniture_manager.gd:241) reject v != 1 only in from_dict and have no validate_dict. That gives 'apply' at load_game 300-302 with no .bak attempt, and _roll_backup (1012-1033) still uses validate_payload, so it counts the file as valid. The 8/3/2 split is correct. The codex-review.txt finding 1 fix note (lines 53-54, 'Consider a backup attempt after an apply failure') is still not implemented. One caveat: the 'dungeon' example of an unknown key is close to unreachable in a shipped build, because host_dungeon_floors returns false only when dungeon_floors.gd is missing (loot_service.gd:966-971). The general point stands, though: unknown payload keys are ignored by the validate and apply loops and are not regathered by gather_payload (581-593).

findings.title: A section whose to_dict fails is silently left out of the save, then reset on load, so that feature's progress is erased
evidence: scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:587-591 - a to_dict that returns a non-Dictionary only push_errors and 'continue's; the save is still written and reported as successful
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:697-698 and 915-917 - optional sections that are missing are not an error; on load the node's reset() runs
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:1012-1033 - the next manual save rotates the previous good file into .bak and the one after overwrites it, so two saves after the bug the old progress is gone
tests/sections/save.gd:792 - section_with_bad_to_dict_is_left_out pins this as intended
findings.description: Any runtime error in a feature's to_dict (home, furniture, wardrobe, loot, dungeon, social) produces a save that validates but no longer contains that section. The save is reported as successful, and the next load resets the section to a new-game state. Silently writing a partial save trades a loud failure for permanent data loss.
findings.player_impact: A bug in one feature's save code could wipe all friendships, the home tier or the furniture of a run, with no warning and, after two more saves, no backup.
findings.recommendation: For a registered or core section whose to_dict fails, abort save_game: return false, set last_error code 'gather', leave the old file and .bak untouched, and show NOTIF_SAVE_FAILED for manual saves. Alternatively, write the previous on-disk copy of that section (from the current file) instead of omitting it. Update the pinned test to expect the refusal.
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: confirmed: gather_payload (save_manager.gd:584-591) push_errors and skips a section whose to_dict returns a non-Dictionary, then writes and reports success. A GDScript runtime error inside to_dict returns null, so this path is reachable. Registered sections and husbandry/shops are optional (the required check happens only in the elif at validate_payload, line 697). Missing sections call reset() in _apply_payload (915-917). _roll_backup rotates the file only when validate_payload says it is ok, and a file missing an optional section passes. So the second manual save after the fault replaces the last good .bak. tests/sections/save.gd:792 pins section_with_bad_to_dict_is_left_out as intended behaviour. Extra detail: if a REQUIRED core section's to_dict fails, the written file fails validation on load, so the slot becomes 'corrupt'. For the auto slot that means no save at all, which is worse than the finding describes.

findings.title: Loot orbs on the ground are not saved, but their source is marked used when it drops them, so a save, quit or load loses them
evidence: scripts/world2d/enemy_2d.gd:369-370 - drops are spawned as LootDrop2D orbs and the enemy cell is immediately LootMarkers.mark_done
scripts/world2d/resource_node_2d.gd:143-161 - dungeon nodes get ctx.deliver='orbs' and mark_done; overworld nodes set the resource_day flag (158) before spawning orbs
scripts/loot/loot_service.gd:206-211 - creature kills default to DELIVER_ORBS
scripts/world2d/loot_drop_2d.gd:2 ('Delivery is retriable. A full pack never destroys a drop') and 103-111 - orbs wait on the ground while the backpack is full
scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd:861-876 - world to_dict has no entry for ground drops; scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:110-120 - quitting autosaves and then leaves
findings.description: The promise that a drop is never destroyed holds only within a session. The kill or harvest is committed to the save (done cell or day flag), but the orbs it spawned are scene nodes and are not in world.to_dict. This matters most with a full backpack, when orbs stay on the ground by design.
findings.player_impact: With a full bag in Mørkeskoven, quitting through the pause menu (or loading) loses every uncollected drop, including rare materials and gems, and the enemies and nodes do not come back that day.
findings.recommendation: Save live orbs per area in WorldRoot2D.to_dict as 'drops': [{area, pos, item, amount}] (including PendingDrops rows) and respawn them in _apply_saved. Alternatively, on save or area exit, deliver orbs through LootService.deliver and route any overflow to the home chest (HomeManager.chest).
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: confirmed: enemy_2d.gd:369-370 spawns LootDrop2D orbs and then calls LootMarkers.mark_done. resource_node_2d.gd:143-161: dungeon nodes call mark_done (151), and overworld nodes call set_flag(_day_key) (158) before the spawn (161). loot_service.gd:206-209 defaults to DELIVER_ORBS. loot_drop_2d.gd:3 promises retriable delivery, and collect() (95-111) leaves the orb on the ground when deliver fails (full pack). PendingDrops rows are also only in memory. world_2d.to_dict (859-874) has no drops entry, and nothing in scripts references LootDrop2D for save or restore. Mitigation: orbs magnet to the player within 183 px after 0.5 s (_process), so with free bag space the loss window is short. The full-backpack case is the real exposure. P3 is right.

findings.title: Some small daily rewards use unsaved RNG, so reloading re-rolls them
evidence: scripts/traetoppen/life/crown_cache_2d.gd:40 and :51 - items.pick_random() and randi_range(gold_min, gold_max) use the global, unsaved RNG
scripts/traetoppen/life/seed_basket_2d.gd:23 - randi_range(1, sum) picks the seed (moonflower vs glow_berry)
scripts/economy/crafting_system.gd:24, 138 - a static RandomNumberGenerator, never saved, rolls the bake bonus
scripts/world2d/farm_grid.gd:45, 242 - rng.randomize() on _ready and the harvest_bonus_chance roll (yield_amount is only cached once a harvest is attempted)
scripts/social/social_rng.gd:4 - the project's own rule: 'NOT randf() (a reload would re-roll)'
findings.description: These outcomes break the project's 'no re-roll on reload' rule, which shops, dungeon loot, resource nodes and the social layer all follow. Saving manually right before the interaction lets a player reload until they get the best result.
findings.player_impact: A player can farm max gold from the crown cache, the rarer seed from Hoppe's basket, and bonus bakes and harvests by saving and reloading. This is minor but contradicts the deterministic design elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Use SocialRng.roll(SocialManager.world_seed, ["crown_cache", total_day, slot]) or DungeonRng.hash_key(...) keyed on total_day and the object id for the crown cache, seed basket, bake bonus (recipe, day, craft count) and harvest bonus (cell, planted_day).
findings.dim: Save/load completeness and integrity across every subsystem
findings.verification: confirmed: crown_cache_2d.gd:40 (items.pick_random()) and :51 (randi_range for gold) use the global RNG, and cache_day is set inside the same callback. seed_basket_2d.gd:23 randi_range picks the seed. crafting_system.gd:24 has a static RandomNumberGenerator, and seed_rng (28) is only called by tests (no game caller found). The roll at :138 matters for the hobbit (race_perks.lua:80 bake_bonus = 0.25). farm_grid.gd:45 calls rng.randomize() and :242 rolls harvest_bonus_chance (race_perks.lua:28 = 0.2 for one race). yield_amount is cached only once a harvest is attempted. social_rng.gd:4 states the 'NOT randf() (a reload would re-roll)' rule for the social layer. Calling it the project's rule stretches it a little, but the pattern (DungeonRng.hash_key in resource_node_2d.gd:154, saved loot rng) is consistent elsewhere. Accurate, and low stakes.

findings.title: Blund's lines contradict what he is doing (says 'you found me' when not hiding)
evidence: lua/dialogue/ghostfam_blund.lua:195-204 - the default non-ghost line is DLG_GHOSTFAM_BLUND_GREET_1 = 'Du fandt mig! Jeg har et nyt sted hver aften, og du er den første, der ser det.' (localization/ghostfamily.csv:23)
localization/ghostfamily.csv:94 SOC_GHOSTFAM_BLUND_GREET_H0_1 'Jeg gemmer mig! Kig ikke. ...' is prepended by DialogueBridge.decorate (dialogue_bridge.gd:20-23)
lua/routines/ghostfam/ghostfam_blund.lua:14,17,72-77 - Blund is plainly visible walking 17:05-18:00, on f_bench 23:30-24:00 and on f_porch all day on festival days
lua/dialogue/ghostfam_blund.lua:46-80 - every gift branch opens with SEEK_GHOSTFAM_FOUND_1 'Åh nej, du fandt mig! Hvordan vidste du det?'
scripts/ghostfam/seek/hide_seek.gd:108-110 - a deferred gift is also paid on an ordinary non-find talk (before_talk else branch) and reaches those same branches
findings.description: When Blund is not hiding, a non-ghost player talking to him sees 'Jeg gemmer mig! Kig ikke' followed by 'Du fandt mig!', while he stands openly on the bench or the porch, including all day on festival days when Silke says he is at the party. When a gift was deferred because storage was full and is then paid at the bench, Blund also says 'Åh nej, du fandt mig! Hvordan vidste du det?'. The FOUND_2 and FOUND_3 variants are also skipped whenever a gift is paid.
findings.player_impact: Small but repeated incoherence in the child character, and it muddles whether the player actually found him.
findings.recommendation: In ghostfam_blund.lua add a non-hiding greeting (e.g. 'Hej! Jeg gemmer mig først, når mørket kommer. Find mig i aften!') and keep GREET_1 for found contexts. Make gift branches use the found line only when found_now > 0 and otherwise a 'Her, jeg har gemt den til dig' line. Add a SOC_GHOSTFAM_BLUND_GREET_H0_DAG/MORGEN variant so the prepended greeting does not claim he is hiding.
findings.dim: Ghost family arc and Blund hide-and-seek against GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM
findings.verification: confirmed: Paths checked. With found_now=0, gift_now=0, hour<24, daypart not morgen, not Wednesday ≥17 and a non-ghost player, ghostfam_blund.lua:195-204 returns DLG_GHOSTFAM_BLUND_GREET_1 'Du fandt mig! ...'. This is reached when Blund is not hiding: walking before 18:00 and between slots, on f_bench from 23:30 to 01:00 (routine :17), and on f_porch 09:00-23:30 on all nine festival days (:76). DialogueBridge prepends GREET_H0 'Jeg gemmer mig! Kig ikke' for hearts<2 (social_talk.gd:76-77). On festival days the FEST family is tried first, so the H0 line is less likely there. A deferred gift is paid in before_talk's else branch (hide_seek.gd:108-110). That sets gift_now, and every gift branch (:46-80) opens with SEEK_GHOSTFAM_FOUND_1 'Åh nej, du fandt mig!', so FOUND_2 and FOUND_3 are skipped whenever a gift is paid. All accurate.

findings.title: Family members talk about themselves in the third person in the mother and garden topics
evidence: scripts/world2d/story/mother_story.gd:118-120 - for npc ghostfam_dyne/ghostfam_silke the page is {speaker: npc, lines: [FM_FAMILY_KIN|FM_FAMILY_FRIEND]}

findings.description: Silke's 'Runden' requires talking to her in Hyggebyen during 20:06-20:39 exactly, and nothing tells the player when. Gnist's 'Sidste kunde' requires talking to him in the last half hour before closing. findings.recommendation: Widen Silke h4 to her whole Hyggebyen round (hour:20.05-22) and move the camera mark to her live position, or use mark:round_s only for staging. Widen Gnist h8 to hour:23.5-25. The heart bubble (Npc2D._update_bubble) already signposts the scene once its condition is true.

findings.verification: partly: The window numbers are correct. Silke h4 runs hour:20.1-20.65 (natlys.lua:405), which is 33 game minutes = 16.5 s at 2 game min/s (game_balance.lua:84). She has round_s 20.0833-20.6667, round_e until 21.25, then round_n until she leaves for traetoppen.t_lamp from 22.9167 (ghostfam_silke.lua:20-23). The h4 window exactly equals her round_s stay, so it is deliberate staging around mark:round_s, though still narrow. (2) The 'clash with Blund's slot-B search' claim is wrong. Silke's 20:06-20:39 window overlaps the end of slot A (18:00-20:30) and Blund's walk. Gnist's 00:30-01:00 window overlaps no seek slot (slot B ends 23:30). Mitigations: both events are retryable daily (cooldown_days 1, once only on success), and the ♥ bubble refreshes on the clock (npc_2d.gd:146-149 _clock → _update_bubble → events_ready).

findings.title: Silke's light walks the whole scene tree 10 times a second
evidence: scripts/ghostfam/glow/npc_glow.gd:52-56 - _refresh every 0.1 s
scripts/ghostfam/glow/npc_glow.gd:65-67,71-75 - _enabled_lights(world) recursively visits every node under world_2d to count visible PointLight2Ds
findings.description: To respect the city's light cap of 15, Silke's NpcGlow counts every visible PointLight2D by recursively walking the entire world subtree every 100 ms. The city builder creates many nodes (platforms, props, foliage, lanterns), and Silke is outdoors from about 18:00 to 02:00.
findings.player_impact: Avoidable CPU cost every frame-tick while Silke is in the area, adding up with the town director and other per-tick work. Low risk now, but it scales with city complexity.
findings.recommendation: Keep a light registry (lights add themselves to a group such as 'city_light', or the city builder exposes a count) and query get_nodes_in_group once per refresh, or recount only on area or light-change signals.
findings.dim: Ghost family arc and Blund hide-and-seek against GHOST_FAMILY_ADDENDUM
findings.verification: confirmed: npc_glow.gd:52-56 calls _refresh every 0.1 s. :65-67 then calls _enabled_lights(world_2d), which recursively visits every descendant (:71-75). This only happens for a glow with a 'light' spec, i.e. Silke (npc_glow.lua:6). It runs whenever Silke's Npc2D is in the loaded area, regardless of night_factor (the walk happens before the visibility test), so it is not limited to 18:00-02:00. The actual frame cost is unmeasured. The tech-debt description is accurate.

findings.title: Notice board is hard to reach and shows a fixed giver-ordered list that hides most givers
evidence: data/traetoppen/traetoppen.json props 'notice_board' (level upper, at [930,520], decor:true) is painted as a plain sprite by city_builder.gd:381-404; there is no handler on the outdoor board
data/interiors/core/int_raadhuset.json:35 the only NoticeBoard2D is inside the Rådhus; lua/buildings/traetoppen.lua:58-65 Rådhuset hours 09:00-15:00, closed Sat/Sun

scripts/traetoppen/life/notice_board_2d.gd:10 offers().slice(0, 5); life_flow.gd:28-29 + quest_manager.gd:384-390 keep the fixed giver order mayor_lyra, baker_maja, merchant_pip, farmer_rosa, fairy_lily, smith_thorin

notice_board_2d.gd:22 a row shows only QUEST_<ID>_TITLE (no giver, place or reward); localization/life.csv LIFE_BOARD_INTRO 'Her er dagens opslag.' although the list never changes by day
findings.description: The board on the Rådhus terrace looks interactive but is decoration. The real board is indoors and reachable only 6 h on 5 days a week, the same window in which the mayor sits at her desk. Its content is the head of a static list: the mayor's three repeatable or long quests and Maja's two fill the 5 slots, so four of the six configured givers are hidden for most of the early game. Rows carry no giver or location, so after accepting the player does not know where to turn in. (The offers do respect is_offerable / requires_zone, and accepting goes through QuestManager.accept_quest correctly, apart from the dialogue_started leak reported separately.)
findings.player_impact: Players who reach town after 15:00 or at weekends never see the board. Those who do see the same five notices day after day and cannot discover Pip's, Rosa's, Lily's or Thorin's errands there.
findings.recommendation: Make the outdoor 'notice_board' prop on 'upper' the interactive NoticeBoard2D: add a 'board' marker to traetoppen.json markers so it is open all day. Keep the indoor one as flavour. Rotate the offers: take at most one quest per giver, then fill to traetoppen.board.max, seeded by total_day the way post_box_2d.gd:43 does. Show 'Fra: <giver> · <location>' under each title, using TTQuestText.from_line.
findings.dim: Treetop city traversal, fast travel, notice board and wayfinding across areas
findings.verification: partly: Accurate: the outdoor 'notice_board' prop (traetoppen.json, decor:true) is painted only by _paint_props (city_builder.gd:381-404), and there is no 'board' marker in the city JSON. The only NoticeBoard2D comes from int_raadhuset.json:35. Rådhuset is open 9-15 and closed on weekdays 5,6 (Sat/Sun). rows() takes slice(0,5) of offerable_for in fixed giver order. On day 1 that is fix_roof, enchanted_garden, fairy_friendship (mayor) and cookie_delivery, birthday_cake (Maja), so math_bakery_counts and the Pip/Rosa/Lily/Thorin quests are cut. Rows show only QUEST_<ID>_TITLE. Corrections: (1) The Rådhus is open Mon-Fri, but the mayor's desk shift is Tue-Thu 9:30-15, so it is not 'the same window'. (2) The other givers are hidden only from the board. The farm mailbox rotates through the full six-giver offer list by total_day (post_box_2d.gd:37-43), and each giver shows a '!' bubble while they have offerable quests (npc_2d.gd:386), so these quests are reachable early. findings.title: Atomic-save fix is likely not atomic on Windows, and startup deletes the only surviving .tmp
evidence: scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:1005-1007 _replace_file = DirAccess.rename_absolute(source, destination)
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:940-944 _remove_stale_temp_files deletes every *.tmp ('it is garbage, the real file is intact')
scripts/autoload/save_manager.gd:6 'the auto slot has no backup'
Release targets: macOS and Windows
findings.description: The Codex fix stopped GDScript from unlinking the target. But _replace_file relies on DirAccess.rename_absolute replacing the target atomically. On Windows, Godot's DirAccessWindows::rename removes an existing destination first and then moves the file (MoveFileW). It is not an atomic replace (I could not check the engine source here; verdict plausible). A crash or power loss between those two steps leaves only save_auto.json.tmp. On the next start, _remove_stale_temp_files deletes that .tmp as 'garbage', so the auto save is gone. The auto slot has no .bak to fall back on. Manual slots have a .bak, so they are safer. Lowered to P3 on re-verification: the loss window is microseconds between two syscalls during an autosave, on Windows only, and the GDScript part of the Codex risk was already repaired in 7f3ccd39.
findings.player_impact: On Windows, a crash at the wrong moment of an autosave can lose the Continue save completely.
findings.recommendation: On startup, if <file>.tmp exists and <file> is missing, validate the .tmp and promote it instead of deleting it. Alternatively, on Windows write via a second file and swap with a journal. Add a fault-injection case to codex_review.gd: target removed, then crash before the move.
findings.verification: partly: The GDScript evidence is accurate. save_manager.gd:1005-1007 has _replace_file = DirAccess.rename_absolute. :940-944 deletes every *.tmp at startup (called from :150), with a comment calling it garbage. Header :6 says the auto slot has no backup. tests/sections/save.gd:1189-1195 even asserts that the stale .tmp is swept. The prior codex-review.txt:164-171 risk (GDScript remove-then-retry) was repaired in 7f3ccd39, so what remains depends on the engine. From memory of Godot 4.x, DirAccessWindows::rename does `if file_exists(new) remove(new); MoveFileW(...)`, which is not an atomic replace. I could not check this against 4.7 source here, so it stays plausible, not proven. The startup sweep has no 'promote the .tmp if the target is missing' path, and that part is confirmed. I lowered severity to P3 because the loss window is microseconds between two syscalls during an autosave, and only on Windows. The .tmp was already read back and verified at that point, so promoting it is a cheap and safe fix. macOS rename(2) is atomic. Merged into CORE-12 in the report. (Re-verified separately after the first verifier crashed.)

findings.title: Hygge decor per gold still drops as rarity rises (furniture capacity limits the cheap spam)

findings.description: E5 is still open only as a minor note. Among buyable furniture rows, decor per gold falls with rarity: median about 0.020 for normal (bed_birch 2/105), 0.017 for uncommon, 0.0074 for rare (the earlier 0.013 used the rarity.lua base price). Unique and legendary furniture has buy_price 0 and sell_ratio 0 (loot only). Because furniture capacity binds (furniture_manager.gd:154-159 sums decor per placed piece), decor per slot is what matters, and it rises steeply with rarity (2-3, 4-8, 9-16, 19-36, 34-63); even 74 normal pieces at tier 10 reach only 222 of 240.

findings.verification: confirmed: home_progression.gd:11-12 and content_features.gd:521-524 both call Grant.requirements(tier) for tiers 2-10. docs/qa/journey/README.md:45-46 shows the fresh animal and ghost journeys ending at day 20 with a tier-2 house. The README Scope line (:67) says it 'does not replace … all ten house tiers earned in one save'. No runtime test earns tiers 3-10. Nuance: tools/features/sim/balance_sim.py (plus tools/dungeon_loot pacing.inject) is an offline expected-value model of gold and days per home tier. Gold-curve pacing is therefore modelled analytically, but not as a runtime or CI gate: no workflow invokes run_balance.sh. origin/main's merged release PR changes none of this. Reported as a standalone finding in the report. (Re-verified separately after the first verifier crashed.)

findings.title: Codex architecture and CI advice is mostly not done at the reviewed commit: WorldRoot2D has grown and the city has no texture-cold budget
evidence: scripts/world2d/world_2d.gd is 949 lines (Codex review: 852); still owns travel, sleep, faint and pass-out queues (:53 _pass_out_pending, :759 _on_player_defeated)
tests/sections/city_map.gd:710 city gate still checks the BEST warm rebuild only; town_budgets.gd:103 gates cold entry for the interior but not for traetoppen (:118 warm only)
scripts/world2d/area_art_prefetch.gd exists (partial: art prefetch done)
.github/workflows/playtest.yml: no tools/art/.venv setup, ubuntu-latest only
findings.description: These are partly addressed: art prefetch now exists, and the interior has a cold-entry budget. Still not done: the transition-coordinator split, a first-visit budget for the city, a pinned Python validation job (art skips still pass under --strict), and any CI runner on a release OS. Re-verification: origin/main fc901cf0 adds a pinned Python setup to playtest.yml and Windows/macOS export plus packaged smoke in build.yml, so those parts are open only at f80e7aed and local main. Still open everywhere: no expected-skip policy (--strict passes with skips) and a Linux-only playtest. The city does have a cold-citizen travel bound (town_budgets.gd:429-447), but it runs after art prefetch.
findings.player_impact: Indirect. City first-visit hitches can come back unnoticed, and CI never runs on macOS or Windows.
findings.recommendation: Add a city cold_entry_ms check in town_budgets.gd. Add a CI job that sets up tools/art/.venv and fails on unexpected skips. Pull the travel/sleep/faint state machine out of world_2d.gd into a TransitionCoordinator.
findings.prior_ref: docs/reviews/codex-review.txt#Architecture assessment / Performance / Validation and delivery coverage
findings.verification: partly: At the reviewed snapshot (HEAD f80e7aed; local main 61cd5183 adds only a design doc) the evidence is accurate. world_2d.gd is 949 lines, with _pass_out_pending at :53 and _on_player_defeated at :759. The codex review (:253) said 852. city_map.gd:710 gates only the BEST warm rebuild, town_budgets.gd:103 has interior_cold_build while :123 has only city_warm_build, and playtest.yml is ubuntu-latest with no venv. Corrections: (1) The Python-stage and release-OS parts are no longer open upstream. origin/main fc901cf0 (Merge PR #1 codex/release-pipeline, 2026-10-18 06:40) adds `tools/art/setup_env.sh` with pinned setup-python to playtest.yml. It also adds build.yml with windows-latest/macos-latest export plus packaged smoke (release.py --smoke), and export_presets.cfg. These, and PRIOR-03, remain open only on the reviewed snapshot and local main, not on origin/main. Still open even on origin/main: no explicit expected-skip policy (--strict still does not fail on skips), and playtest itself runs only on Linux. (2) The city is not entirely without a cold bound. town_budgets.gd:429-447 city_travel_twelve_cold_citizens limits a whole travel into traetoppen to <=800 ms with 12 cold citizens. That check runs after the art prefetch loop, though, so it is not a texture-cold first-visit budget. (3) The codex review asked for a pinned Python job, packaged smoke and windowed perf; it did not ask for a macOS/Windows playtest runner. The transition-coordinator split is not done. Severity P3 is fine. Reported as a standalone finding in the report. (Re-verified separately after the first verifier crashed.)
